text:
终于有个GPT-6也做不好的Bench了

这是 @patience_cave 公布的 MazeBench 测试。

AI 要在 200 多个房间里推箱子、找路、收集宝石，有些谜题需要规划上百步。

GPT-6 在 3D 迷宫里跑了 60 多个小时，最后只拿了 14%（14颗宝石）。

结果一看其他模型发现还是遥遥领先🤣

Fable 5.1 是 2%，Fable 5、Opus 5 和 GPT-5.6 Sol 都是 1%。

但我觉得探索热力图更直观。

因为Fable 5.1 只探索了一小片，而Astra 已经走出去很远了。

作者说，它能轻松解决需要同时兼顾 5 个可移动部件的谜题。

但它还是不太能理解三维空间，更喜欢切成俯视图，把游戏当平面的玩。 

遇到只有换成三维视角才能看见的墙，就当成隐形障碍；物体堆叠超过 3 格高的立体谜题，这轮测试里它就过不去了。

跟上一代比，进步确实很大。

但具体看它怎么卡住的，又会发现，还有不少东西没搞明白。

text:
AI教母李飞飞访谈精彩片段：机器人当前最大的瓶颈是什么？

在 a16z 播客与 World Labs 联合创始人李飞飞、Justin Johnson、Ben Mildenhall 的对谈中，Martin Casado 问到：Atlas 这样的世界模型与机器人究竟有什么关系？

李飞飞给出的判断很直接：机器人目前最大的瓶颈是数据。未来可能会受限于芯片，但眼下最缺的是能够覆盖真实环境和各种意外情况的训练数据。

线缆会以不同方式弯曲，箱子会有不同尺寸、颜色和位置。机器人不能只记住一种环境。Atlas 的价值，是把真实场景转化为可以不断变化和反复训练的模拟世界，加快“现实到模拟、模拟再回到现实”的循环。

UPDATE: Capitol Hill rumor mill is saying the likelihood of CLARITY act passing is near zero.

It's currently 18% on Polymarket & but its really likely more like a 3-5% chance.

From what I understand, everyone in DC somewhat assumes that CLARITY is not going to pass, but they can't publicly say this because the industry has invested tens of millions of dollars and 18 months of resources on trying to get it through. 

It’s just not going to happen from what I hear.

There's still no answer to this ethics question for Trump’s dealings in crypto, from the Democrats. Based on that, the odds of passing on prediction markets are probably pretty high and seems like 'No' is potentially interesting. 

CLARITY will instead be more or less ‘drafted as separate bills’ focusing on specific sectors of the crypto market. 

These could be innovation exemptions, acts, or bills that are focused on stablecoins, tokenization, perpetual futures, and prediction markets coming shortly after CLARITY failed. They prefer take a nuanced approach rather than a massive, wide-reaching crypto bill at this current point. 

That is what is much, much more likely to happen from what I understand from folks in DC. 

TLDR;

CLARITY likely out but no one will admit it, innovation exemptions are in, and they are far under discussed for their significance to open the doors for all of finance to come oncain.

text:
a 98c YES is also a trade on how long your capital stays stuck.

buy at 98c, redeem at $1: roughly 2% before fees.

but getting that dollar back in two days versus two months is a completely different trade. same payout, very different use of the balance sheet.

this is where prediction markets need a better language for carry.

in perps, funding makes the cost of holding visible. in a fully funded event position, you have to price the opportunity cost yourself, including the gap between the event ending and the market actually resolving.

an apparently obvious outcome can still be a poor use of capital if settlement drags, the exit is thin, or that last 2c is compensation for a resolution risk you missed.

i’d like to see prediction market terminals show expected time to redemption next to price, with a disputed-resolution scenario.

especially near $1. the remaining upside is small enough that settlement mechanics can become the entire trade.

Property Rights: The Root Cause of the Palestinian/Israeli Conflict

The Palestinian-Israeli conflict is the inevitable result of the destruction of a centuries-old system of private property rights and its replacement by race-based state ownership. Since 1947, property rights in Palestine have been replaced by a government agency that owns the majority of land, constantly steals more, never sells, and only leases land to one racial group. Religious and racial conflict are not destined in Palestine; they are historically rare occurrences, but this system of property rights would create violent conflict anywhere.

In 1945, the British mandate government surveyed land ownership in Palestine and found that Jews owned 5.67% of the total land, while Muslims, Christians & other denominations owned 48.31% of the land. The remaining 46.02% was public land, mainly in the sparsely inhabited desert in the south, most of which was de facto owned by the Bedouins who herded there. Among the privately-owned lands, only 10.5% was owned by Jews, while 89.5% was owned by non-Jews. There was not a single district in Palestine in which Jews owned a majority of the land, as this illustration makes clear.[1] 

In 1917, when the Balfour Declaration was issued, the Jewish population ranged from 4% to 13%. In 1945, the population of Palestine was 1,764,520, of which 69% were Muslim and Christian, and 31% were Jewish.[2] The majority of the Jewish population was recent immigrants from Europe, many illegal. Even after decades of legal and illegal immigration, land purchases financed by European benefactors, and terrorism against Palestinian civilians and British forces, the Zionist movement had less than a third of the population of Palestine, and owned less than 6% of its land when it established its ethnostate. To establish an ethnostate on a land in which the right ethnicity was less than a third of the population, and owned less than a twelfth of the land, Zionist terrorists engaged in a premeditated and systematic campaign of terrorism, murder, and violent expulsion, meticulously planned from the 1930s, ruthlessly executed against a largely unarmed population, and practically continuing until this day, explaining the conflict’s longevity. This has been extensively documented by Palestinian historians, such as Walid Khalidi and Rashid Khalidi, as well as by Israeli historians like Ilan Pappe and Benny Morris.[3]

text:
> Fully headless tool use access, using client-side signatures to authorize payments without manual signup or per-provider API-key provisioning.

headless tool use has more of an authentication problem than a checkout problem. most endpoints still need a proper auth path, not an x402 payment.

> - Autonomous runtime loops where agent deployments can both earn and spend: receive payment for work, then use those funds to purchase inference, data, or tools, all programmatically within the same runtime.

bruh, it's either the products/services can be purchased with crypto or not and if they can then you're just looking at a fee collection address with granted permissions to an account controlled by an agent + skill. x402 is hardly a solution here.

> An agent shouldn’t need to navigate a bank’s website through browser automation to participate in commerce. A wallet gives it a native way to receive and deploy funds.

unironically, a bank's website is exactly where and why x402 can be useful. x402 becomes redundant the second an agent gets a wallet and has to just interface with another counterparty that also has a wallet, like a bank.

x402 plays a role in a thin abstraction layer that has been hyped more than it is really worth, and that's why its lacklustre numbers, as pointed out by @mewwts, are telling.

text:
"What's your P(doom)?" was an en vogue question about 2 years and fell out of favor in 2026. I hope this is because everyone wised-up to realize any sufficient intelligence likely won't be centralized; there will be factions fighting for status, scarcity, resources. So it won't be "humans vs machines" but many intelligences, of which humans are one, each with their own alliances competing with each other.
Today we have "West vs East" but later it'll be something else. The universe is adversarial but the technology and energy of competing will just keep escalating. This adversarial nature keeps power in check. What's more, each faction is not perfectly siloed; information about plans and technology leak due to misaligned incentives. This has a stabilizing effect; it's hard for 1 power to run away with all the power. That power eventual fades to the rebels and balance is returned. The only thing we can bet on is that the human experience will continue to change; it'll be augmented and extended. I'm here for it.

1/ 交易合约两线开花
过去一周，FOMO 产生了 1067 万美元费用，在 DefiLlama Trading Apps 板块排名第一。
排名第二的 Axiom，同期费用为 660 万美元。

FOMO 的永续合约业务也在快速起量。
过去 24 小时，FOMO Perps 交易量达到 5750 万美元，在 DefiLlama Interface Protocols 板块排名第三，仅落后于 tradeXYZ 等头部项目。
关键在于，FOMO 的永续合约功能直到今年 6 月才正式上线。

FOMO 已经证明了：它不仅有用户和流量，还能把这些用户和流量，快速迁移到新的交易场景和金融产品中。
未来如果 FOMO 继续扩展到预测市场、结构化产品等方向，也并不令人意外。

2/ 压力给到了 Axiom 和 GMGN
面对 FOMO 这样的后起之秀，Axiom 和 GMGN 短期内最直接的应对方式，大概率只有两种。

第一，功能跟进。
也就是借鉴并上线类似服务，尽可能缩小产品矩阵上的差距。

第二，发行代币。
通过空投预期、积分体系和激励机制，增强用户黏性，减缓资金与用户向竞争对手迁移。

不过，对 Axiom 和 GMGN 这类已经具备强现金流的产品来说，发币并不是生存所必需的融资手段。相反，代币更像是一张战略牌。
打得好，可以迅速放大增长；打得不好，也可能稀释原本健康的商业模式，并把平台带入更高成本的激励竞争。

重磅：Delphi Digital 将 @fomo_family 列为 2026 年最看好的消费级应用之一
对标千亿美元巨头 Robinhood？

刚深入研读了 Delphi 的 fomo 研报，核心观点很明确：
fomo 有可能成为新一代的“入口级”投机基建，就像当年 Robinhood 把千禧一代带入美股一样。

fomo 传送：https://t.co/WN2bCgwGmM

但这里有个关键问题——fomo 真的能跑出来吗？

1/ 短期竞争格局：fomo vs Moonshot vs https://t.co/FIDev9wgNH
数据层面，战况已经很明显。
▌Moonshot：历史峰值更高，但趋势持续向下，11 月手续费首次被 fomo 超越
▌https://t.co/FIDev9wgNH：依然是体量老大，但核心还是 meme 币发射交易，业务扩张主要依赖收购
▌fomo：收入趋势向上，产品执行力明显更强

产品差异化上，fomo 的路径选择很聪明。
Moonshot 的审批上架机制在快节奏 meme 周期里完全跟不上，fomo 从一开始就走更通用、链抽象路径，避开了纯 meme 赛道的风险。

2/ 长期想象空间：真正的“基础设施”
这是 Delphi 最看重的点。

fomo 的核心优势——移动原生执行 + 社交发现 + 极简 UX——这套组合拳完全可以扩展到远超 meme 币的领域：
RWA
合成资产
杠杆产品
甚至代币化股票

想象一下，如果 fomo 真的能复制 Robinhood 当年的路径：
▌Robinhood：零佣金 + 移动优先，把年轻人带入美股投机
▌fomo：链抽象 + 社交发现，把更广泛的零售用户带入链上投机
关键在于，fomo 如果能突破圈层，触达真正的大众用户。那价值捕获的天花板就完全不一样了。

值得注意的是，Delphi Digital 并非 fomo 的利益相关方，他们没参与此前的融资轮次。
这种第三方看好的分析，可信度显然更高。

text:
现在很多公司的技术笔试，真正考的第一道题已经变成了：猜面试官到底信不信 AI。

有人说，他一个朋友最近在面技术岗，遇到的公司大概分成两半。

一半公司的 take-home，你用了 AI，刷掉。

另一半公司的 take-home，你没用 AI，也刷掉。因为他们觉得，一个 2026 年还不会用 AI 写代码的工程师，本身就不合格。

听起来像段子，但行业数据真差不多。

Karat 今年调查了 400 名工程招聘负责人，62% 的公司依然禁止技术面试使用 AI。但这些负责人同时估计，超过一半候选人即使被禁止，照样会偷偷用。71% 的人承认，现在已经越来越难靠传统技术面试判断一个人的真实能力。

Anthropic 更荒诞。

他们自己的 performance engineer take-home 已经被 Claude 连续打穿，Opus 4 能超过绝大多数人类候选人，Opus 4.5 后来连最强的那批也追上了，逼得出题人把题改了三版。

于是现在出现了一个很滑稽的场面。

工作第一天，公司让你开 Claude Code、Cursor，能让 Agent 干的绝对别自己干。

面试那天，公司把 AI 关掉，让你证明自己还会像 2022 年一样写代码。

换一家又可能完全反过来。你老老实实自己写完，对方觉得你不够 AI Native。

OpenAI 现在甚至已经把这种矛盾直接写进招聘流程，不同轮次使用不同规则。有的允许 AI，有的专门看你不用 AI 还能不能解决问题。

这其实说明，技术招聘原来依赖的那套代理指标正在失效。

以前一道 take-home 想测的是你会不会写代码。

现在同一道题里混进了至少三件事：你本身会不会写，你会不会调用模型，你有没有能力判断模型写出来的东西到底靠不靠谱。

还拿一张卷子同时测这三件事，最后当然只能变成猜规则。

以后技术面试最值钱的问题，可能真不再是「这段代码是不是你亲手写的」。

而是 AI 已经替你写完以后，你知不知道它哪里写错了。

text:
Digital asset security goes far beyond smart contracts.

Tomorrow, Jonathan Riss (@allypry ), OSINT & Blockchain Intelligence Analyst at CertiK, will join @0xCregis and @SlowMist_Team to discuss operational risk, security controls, incident response, and the growing impact of AI on enterprise security.

⏰ 5 PM GMT+8
author: CertiK
quoted_text:
🎙️ Cregis MicUp Vol. 19: Risk & Control in Digital Asset Operations

🗓️ September 9, 2026 | 5:00 PM GMT+8 | Live X Space

🔗 Set your reminder: https://t.co/pEO4I0DYu1
Digital asset security remains a serious operational challenge. In the first half of 2026 alone, CertiK recorded more than $1.31 billion in losses across the industry. Behind these incidents is a broader question for enterprises: where can risk enter the process of managing and moving digital assets, and how can it be identified before it results in a loss?

Risk may originate within the technology, emerge through on-chain interactions or develop from the way people and systems handle transactions. AI introduces further uncertainty as it becomes more widely used across enterprise operations and takes on a greater role in analyzing information, supporting decisions and interacting with financial systems.

Join Cregis for a practical discussion on what recent incidents reveal about enterprise risk, how potential threats can be identified across digital asset operations, and how security controls should evolve as AI becomes more deeply involved.

🎤 Meet Our Expert Panel:
Jonathan Riss, OSINT & Blockchain Intelligence Analyst @CertiK
Tony Tan, Hong Kong Community Lead @SlowMist_Team

🎙️ Moderated by Bovey Li, Deputy Marketing Director at Cregis

📋 What We’ll Explore:
🔸 Analysis of Representative Security Incidents
A closer look at notable incidents, how the attacks unfolded, where the risks entered and what enterprises can learn from the controls that failed or limited the impact.

🔸 Identifying Risk Across Digital Asset Operations
How can enterprises identify vulnerabilities and warning signs across their technology, on-chain activities and operating processes before they develop into security incidents?

🔸 Structuring Security for Real Operations
How should code audits, infrastructure security, wallet controls, approval policies, monitoring and incident response work together in daily operations?

🔸 How AI Changes Enterprise Security Risk
As enterprises use AI across more systems and workflows, where could new risks emerge around information, permissions, decisions and transaction execution? How do these risks differ from traditional security threats, and what strategies can enterprises adopt in response?

Why This Matters:
For anyone responsible for managing digital assets, security cannot be assessed through code audits or wallet protection alone. Losses can result from weaknesses across connected systems, transaction decisions and everyday operating processes, even when individual components appear secure.

This session will help businesses understand how incidents develop across the full flow of digital asset operations, identify gaps in their existing controls, and consider how security responsibilities should evolve as AI gains greater access to enterprise systems and financial activities.
📌 Join us 5 minutes early to secure your spot!

text:
CZ 最近提出了一个判断：IPO 将走向链上。

这个说法背后藏着一条更长的线，股票和加密资产的交易入口，正在慢慢合并。
整个资本市场的技术栈，正在我们眼前被重构。

1/ 互联网曾经只是“电子报纸”
上世纪 90 年代，人们对互联网的共识是，互联网 = 更好的报纸。
1996 年上线的 https://t.co/IvMOPDSJLG，最初只是把当天印刷的报纸原封不动搬上网，连排版和分栏都原样保留。
但报纸只是信息的载体。互联网最终没有止步于传播内容，而是长出了自己的原生应用，搜索引擎、社交网络、云计算、移动支付……今天，全球 80 亿人中有 55 亿网民，政治、金融、交通、娱乐，都运转在这套系统之上。

而我们对区块链的认知，正在犯同样的错误。

2/ 区块链不只是 7×24 的赌场
汽车刚出现时被比作“没有马的马车”，互联网被称为“更好的报纸”。而今天的区块链，被视为“更便捷的股票市场”，甚至都称不上“更好”。
但区块链对金融系统的吞噬，已经开始了。

券商正在 CEX 化，Robinhood 是典型案例。
它从股票券商起步，随后增加加密货币交易和自托管钱包，又通过收购 Bitstamp 补齐加密交易基础设施。此后，Robinh 进一步宣布基于 Arbitrum 技术栈建设自己的 Robinhood Chain 。

与此同时，CEX 也在券商化。融合正从反方向发生。
加密交易所不再满足于现货和永续合约，而是不断扩大资产边界，把股票、商品、外汇装进加密用户熟悉的界面。
以 @MEXC 为例，这家加密货币交易所如今已提供全栈式的股票服务。

▌RealStocks（真实股票）
过去，Web3 资金想要配置美股，需要经历繁琐的出金、换汇、电汇至传统券商的过程。
MEXC 的 RealStocks 用稳定币重构传统资产的结算层。用户以 5 USDT 的极低门槛，直接买入并持有由合作持牌券商托管的 7000 多只全球真实股票与 ETF。

▌Stock Futures（股票期货）
面向想要杠杆、抓事件行情、做对冲的人，可交易美股、港股、韩股、日股等 300 多种股票期货。
它把加密市场里高频、双向、带杠杆的交易范式，直接复用到了股票标的上。这是传统券商很难提供的操作自由度。

▌Tokenized Stock（代币化股票）
可直接用 USDT 交易 200 多种代币化股票，接近 7×24 小时不间断，不受美股开收盘时间限制。

3/ 今天的区块链，相当于互联网的哪一年？
如果一定要类比，今天的区块链大约处于互联网的 1995—2000 年阶段。
▌基础协议已经可用
▌稳定币等产品已找到明确需求，但大量应用仍由投机和补贴驱动
▌用户体验依然复杂
▌基础设施和监管标准尚未统一
它已经不是实验室里的玩具，但距离移动互联网式的全面普及，还有很长的路要走。

我们依然处在早期。

text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

quoted_text:
I read Noah Smith @Noahpinion on China sometimes, because he is one of several prolific content creators here who represent a particular school of thought on China which I need to understand deeply. 

Specifically about Noah, he’s obviously smart and capable of making a persuasive argument. And to be fair, I am constructive on some of his China diagnosis more than some of my criticism of him might suggest.

But when it comes to China details, Noah repeatedly illustrates a problem I see across American policy commentary: intelligence and confidence substituting for learned experience, with some consequential gaps between explaining what China does and understanding what it means.

Let’s looks specifically at several of his recurring arguments, which is the reason for this post.

First, overcapacity.

Noah argues that China’s system of cheap capital, subsidies and relentless investment produces chronic overcapacity, forcing Chinese companies to export the resulting surplus abroad.

There is plenty of truth to this. China has unquestionably overinvested and wasted staggering amounts of capital.

But “overcapacity” describes the financial condition better than it describes the industrial outcome.

What did all that supposedly excessive investment actually buy?

Factories. Engineers. Suppliers. Tooling. Infrastructure. Process knowledge. Logistics networks. Battery ecosystems. Automation expertise. And an extraordinary ability to manufacture complicated products quickly, cheaply and at scale.

China’s system can be colossally wasteful and devastatingly effective at the same time.

Americans have enormous difficulty holding those two thoughts in their heads simultaneously.

Second, subsidies.

Noah puts considerable weight on subsidies and below-market financing in explaining Chinese competitiveness.

Again, fair enough.

But showing that BYD benefited from industrial policy doesn’t make BYD less capable. Calling Chinese EVs subsidized doesn’t make them worse cars. Explaining how China created its battery ecosystem doesn’t make that ecosystem disappear.

Subsidies can help create capability. They cannot indefinitely counterfeit it.

Eventually somebody has to engineer the battery, design the production line, manage thousands of suppliers, manufacture the car and sell something customers actually want.

China can now do those things exceptionally well.

Explaining why your competitor became formidable is not a strategy for competing with them.

Third, Noah worries that Chinese exports could deindustrialize America and Europe, including industries the U.S. might need in a military conflict.

This is one of his stronger arguments, and I largely agree with the premise.

Where I part company is the reflexive leap from vulnerability to exclusion. His strategy recommendations are pretty counterproductive. 

Protecting American companies from Chinese competition is not the same thing as making American companies competitive.

Tariffs can be useful. I support them when they buy time and create leverage to rebuild American capability.

But tariffs without capability acquisition risk creating a Galápagos economy: American companies protected inside their home market from competitors they increasingly cannot beat elsewhere.

The better question is: 

*What does China know how to do that we no longer do—or cannot do nearly as efficiently—and how do we acquire those capabilities in the near term?*

That question leads to a very different industrial policy.

If Chinese EV, battery, solar, robotics or advanced-manufacturing companies want access to the American market, use tariffs and market access as leverage to make them manufacture here, employ Americans, build American supply chains, partner where appropriate with American companies, and transfer manufacturing know-how—while drawing very hard lines around data, critical infrastructure and genuine national-security risks.

(1/2)

This week, I'm releasing a 1 and a half hour conversation with @variational_lvs - Founder and CEO at @variational_io.

Lucas co-founded a hedge fund at 20 that Digital Currency Group acquired a year later, then walked away from that exit to build a firm that now sits second only to Hyperliquid in open interest and daily volume.

His argument: crypto rebuilt exchanges before it built brokers, and that architectural gap is what's holding on-chain trading back.

We talk about:
- Why order books work for a handful of liquid assets like BTC and $ETH but break once you try to list hundreds of markets
- How Variational aggregates liquidity straight from traditional finance instead of rebuilding 40 years of market depth from scratch
- Why Variational charges zero fees by keeping the market-maker spread inside the platform
- The architectural difference between Variational's RFQ, broker-like model and Hyperliquid's order book
- How Variational's daily volume went from $1 million to over $100 million within months of launch
- What swaps offer that perps can't - a flat, predictable carry cost instead of a funding rate that can spike overnight
- Why he raised $50 million in May specifically to get taken seriously by trad-fi institutions
- The two kinds of businesses he wants competed into extinction: high-fee brokers and predatory market makers

And much more...

Podcast out this week!

text:
Ethena 又放大招了，正式推出 Ethena Pay，持币者必须关注

简单说，Ethena Pay 是 Ethena 推出的自托管数字银行应用，账户余额以 USDe 计价，把储蓄、转账和卡片支付放在同一个 App 里

目前是 Beta 版本，iOS 已可下载，先覆盖约 48 个国家，澳大利亚、巴西、日本、新加坡、南非、阿联酋等，美国和欧盟暂未开放，候补名单每周扩容

大陆地区看起来还不能注册，但是可以加入 waitlist ⬇️

https://t.co/fSDDhT3oUR

用人话解释一下 Ethena Pay 到底是干啥的

1/ 存：通过银行转账或加密资产把钱转进去，账户里显示成美元余额，这笔钱可以按照规则拿 6% 年化的余额奖励

2/ 转：给别人转账，或转到外部银行账户；转到银行时，对方收到的是当地法币，而不是加密货币

3/ 花：在 App 里生成虚拟卡，绑 Apple Pay / Google Wallet，线上线下刷卡拿 5% 的消费返现

有人肯定要说，这不就是个 U 卡吗？诶，但实际上不一样

U 卡一般是账户里放 USDT/USDC，再套一张能刷的卡，本质上是第三方帮你把 U 换成发币

但 Ethena Pay 则是实用 USDe，这其中的磨损、安全性以及拒付率，并不在同一个水平

用 Ethena 创始人 Guy Young 的话来说

Ethena Pay 的目标用户不是已在用钱包和 DeFi 的人，而是链外只需要「存、转、花」的普通用户

@ethena ethereum:0x57e114b691db790c35207b2e685d4a43181e6061

Four officially announced its first 4Stock, which is 1:1 pegged to the U.S. stock CEA Industries, a publicly listed company that later transformed into a BNB treasury company.

Four uses a custodial account to purchase the corresponding real shares, then mints on-chain 4Stock based on the actual amount of shares held.

Use cases:

1:1 pegged to the underlying stock: Four uses the USDC deposited by users to purchase actual CEA Industries shares, then mints BNC4 based on the actual number of shares purchased. So it represents “on-chain exposure to BNC stock.”

On-chain trading: Once minted, it can be freely transferred and traded on BSC without having to wait for traditional stock market hours. It can also serve as the pool asset for Stock Memes, meaning BNC4 can be used as a trading pair to launch Meme coins built around this stock.

Redemption: If the corresponding official bStock is launched in the future, BNC4 can be exchanged 1:1 for the bStock.

text: I think private companies in China can absolutely exaggerate their roadmaps, then scramble to deliver. But frustratingly, I *don't see reporting on that*. The default media/think tankie narrative is just some Orientalist cope about face-saving-paper-tiger in its death throes.
author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
I hope people by now realize that the general m.o. of Chinese SME companies has been to under-promise and over-deliver and generally take a conservative stance on forecasting.

Also what is reported in mainstream media — which abides by certain standards of fact-checking and vetting — is usually going to be on a lagged basis.

This is a function of the vetting process itself (which takes time to do properly) and extremely strict non-disclosure policies due to the geopolitically sensitive nature of the effort.

Many people think China exaggerates its development progress (note: popular narratives of “fake or exaggerated GDP”). Track record suggests the opposite: News getting out trumpeting China’s progress is typically viewed by authorities as harmful to national interests.

My default assumption is that what makes it into mainstream outlets is dated by around 6-12 months.

text:
Glad $SIVE is attending CIOE Shenzen and hope my followers can go too!

If you want my read on current landscape:

-> Chinese pluggable makers like CIG (剑桥科技) are facing severe shortages in 70mW-200mW lasers.

If you look at filings from CIG, they claim "substantially longer delivery times and deposits to secure capacity” along with statements of shortages.

-> Innolight and others were also looking to secure multiple laser suppliers with LTAs recently from their filings. 

On the US side of things:

-> $COHR was a major merchant laser supplier before, but largely withdrew from the market after rerouting them internally. 

"I do not see any time in the near future where we would be selling Indium Phosphide lasers externally." From their ER transcript. 

And then likely turned into a buyer in an already supply constrained market... where 

"over the long term, we will have some portion of our datacom transceivers that will be supported by external sources."

-> $AAOI not really known to be a merchant supplier, but said same thing about laser capacity being rerouted towards transceivers. And having to turn away customers for lasers. 

-> For $LITE, they still supply lasers but stated: "We are commanding a significant price premium" for CW lasers

$LITE Wupen Yuen: "wherever they can get the laser source, they will use that solution to support their build-out."

So hinting... about customers just finding anything available due to shortages. 

-> $MTSI has no meaningful capacity online now, but they're already stating customers are approaching them with urgency to secure CW laser supply. 

-> Trendforce reported $AMD and hyperscaler CSPs are aggressively going out to secure CW laser supply to avoid future bottlenecks. 

And then you have Europe... 

Where $SIVE is coming online with "tremendous capacity available now" from their foundry partners. 

With 100M+ laser capacity Q4 2027, and maybe if you look at their 2:1 ratio implying ~200M targeted laser capacity from external foundries. 

They also happen to offer the same power range (70mW, 100 mW, 200mW) as the ones currently in shortage by pluggable makers in China. 

There's a massive void to fill, so this dramatically increases the chance of converting customers. (esp. Supported by Lumentum statements)

My speculation was that some of the 6 active pluggable engagements were from China? 

Which is why they're attending the conference. 

So to any of my Chinese followers, maybe you can ask a few questions like:

- if Europe is a laser source geography, if Innolight/Eoptolink/Cambridge are considering $SIVE. 
- if they're seeing ASP hikes in lasers, and what CW products are hardest to obtain

If you are attending CIOE in Shenzhen!

Ethena 又放大招了，正式推出 Ethena Pay，持币者必须关注

简单说，Ethena Pay 是 Ethena 推出的自托管数字银行应用，账户余额以 USDe 计价，把储蓄、转账和卡片支付放在同一个 App 里

目前是 Beta 版本，iOS 已可下载，先覆盖约 48 个国家，澳大利亚、巴西、日本、新加坡、南非、阿联酋等，美国和欧盟暂未开放，候补名单每周扩容

用人话解释一下 Ethena Pay 到底是干啥的

1/ 存：通过银行转账或加密资产把钱转进去，账户里显示成美元余额，这笔钱可以按照规则拿 6% 年化的余额奖励

2/ 转：给别人转账，或转到外部银行账户；转到银行时，对方收到的是当地法币，而不是加密货币

3/ 花：在 App 里生成虚拟卡，绑 Apple Pay / Google Wallet，线上线下刷卡拿 5% 的消费返现

有人肯定要说，这不就是个 U 卡吗？诶，但实际上不一样

U 卡一般是账户里放 USDT/USDC，再套一张能刷的卡，本质上是第三方帮你把 U 换成发币

但 Ethena Pay 则是实用 USDe，这其中的磨损、安全性以及拒付率，并不在同一个水平

用 Ethena 创始人 Guy Young 的话来说

Ethena Pay 的目标用户不是已在用钱包和 DeFi 的人，而是链外只需要「存、转、花」的普通用户

text:
上过太空的大佬，敢于向目前最热的资产开炮。

随着 zcash:native 突破1000，大部分加密帖子都有进一步看多的预期和情绪。

而F2Pool 联合创始人王纯则认为 zcash:native 的暴涨纯属“叙事炒作”，并认为 Zcash 的团队非常业余，并称拉黑整个团队是他做过的最好的决定之一。

这个陈年旧事可以追溯到6年前，当时 Zcash 团队成员在沟通中反复搞混 EST（美国东部标准时间）和 EDT（夏令时）。

他当时直接做出了“拉黑 Zcash 全公司”的决定，并认为分不清时区的人，大概率也会搞混 BTC 和 USD，更别提去理解零知识证明这种复杂技术。

在他看来，Zcash 的基本面配不上目前的前十市值：

-前四年 20% 的区块奖励直接作为“创始人奖励”进了团队和早期投资者的口袋，这不是干净中立的钱。
-大部分代币在透明地址流转，“可选隐私”只是营销口号。
-Electric Coin Company (ECC)、基金会与董事会长期宫斗，今年 1 月核心开发团队甚至集体离职，直言是被“赶走的”。
-今年 5 月曝光的 Orchard 隐私池漏洞，更是被市场选择性遗忘。
这个存在了 4 年的严重漏洞，理论上可以无痕迹地凭空增发假币。对于一个标榜自身是“硬通货”的隐私资产来说，私人供应量无法像比特币那样被公开核查，还要靠事后紧急打补丁，这在逻辑上是极其荒谬的。

王纯的结论是，无论你是否喜欢 Solana 或 Hyperliquid，它们至少在处理真实的链上需求。
而 Zcash，只是一个有着不公平启动、团队内斗、常年存在安全漏洞的“故事币（Story coin）”。

在一片涨声中，听听负面尖锐声音，或许能帮我们在 FOMO 情绪里保持一分清醒。
author: TechFlowPost
quoted_text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

这张股东名单比融资额还夸张。

三星、ASML、Nvidia，一群站在 AI 硬件供应链最上游的公司，一起往 Mistral 塞钱。去年 ASML 已经领投了它 17 亿欧元的 C 轮，现在又继续加码。

text:
AI 产品现在最容易犯的错，就是拿今天这代模型的能力，决定自己能做什么。

Aaron Levie 最近提了一个我很认同的判断。

现在设计 AI 产品，应该默认未来会有高几个数量级的算力和 token，然后从那个世界往今天倒推。

所以最好的创业机会，往往长得有点奇怪。

它今天已经勉强能工作，可以给客户创造一点真实价值，所以不是 PPT；但如果你把它真正想做的事情完整说出来，又会发现靠今天的模型根本做不到。

这才是关键。

因为过去的软件能力边界相对稳定，创业者是在已知技术上找需求。现在模型每隔一段时间就把能力边界往外推一截，产品设计开始变成另一件事：你得提前知道，模型再聪明 10 倍、100 倍之后，用户会拿它来干什么。

很多 AI 产品今天看起来只是一个小工具，真正赌的是那个还没到来的模型。

所以我现在越来越觉得，AI 创业不是在给今天的模型找应用，而是在提前给未来的模型造产品。

text:
最近在 Hermes Agent 上用了几天 GPT-6 Astra，每天都在使劲蹬，整体还是非常满意的。平时主要让它处理实际任务，同时推进几个事情，用的都是正常的 Medium reasoning effort。

先说智力，确实有提升，但没有到跨时代的程度。如果一定要打个比方，我的体感大概是 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 1.5 倍左右。这个就是主观感觉，没有做严格跑分。

速度倒是快了非常多，日常用就能明显感觉出来。尤其我这种并发使用 Agent 的方式，几个任务都在往前推进，速度的变化还是很影响体验的。

然后 Usage 消耗也快了，体感大概是之前的 1.5 倍。以前用 Sol，使劲用也不太容易把额度用完，现在使劲用，几乎就能用完了。所以按额度消耗来看，确实贵了一些，但还没有贵到那么明显、那么致命。当然，也可能有一部分是因为它跑得需要的 token 少了。

Computer use 这部分提升也很明显。让它去网页上获取信息，或者直接做一些操作，用起来确实舒服了很多。

还有一个变化是更靠谱了。之前有些细节可能处理不到位，现在能照顾到了。

总体感觉还是非常好评的。

F2Pool联合创始人王纯：Zcash反弹是一场叙事争夺战

F2Pool联合创始人王纯（Chun）发文称，Zcash近期反弹并不代表其真正赢得市场，市值排名接近Solana和Hyperliquid，也不意味着Zcash具备同等竞争力。

王纯批评Zcash早期将20%的区块奖励分配给创始人、员工、顾问和投资者，累计约210万枚ZEC；同时，项目隐私功能长期缺乏实际使用，且曾出现持续数年的资金池漏洞。

他认为，Zcash的问题并非单一事件，而是分配机制、治理争议和安全事件长期叠加的结果。

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

text:
$4Stock：Four. meme「股票上链」新叙事下跑出来的第一批 Meme

一句话理解：
$4Stock 是 Four. meme 今天推出「4Stock」股票上链产品后，围绕这个新叙事诞生的 Meme 币。

但这里首先要区分两个东西：

① 4Stock 是 Four. meme 推出的一个新产品机制。
它的目标，是把目前还没有被 bStocks 覆盖的热门美股提前搬到 BNB Chain。

按照 Four. meme 公布的机制，每一枚真正的「4Stock 股票代币」都有对应底层股票资产 1:1 支持；未来对应股票正式推出 bStock 后，还可以按照 1:1 转换成 bStock。

第一只上线的是 $BNC4：
0x7C8D5502b544dDAf8852Fc46D1174E34876D545C

它对应的是美股 CEA Industries（NASDAQ: BNC）。

BNC 本身又是目前最典型的「BNB Treasury Company」之一，因此这个产品形成了一个很有意思的闭环：

BNB → 持有 BNB 的美股公司 BNC → BNC 股票重新被代币化 → 回到 BNB Chain。

 $4Stock 又是什么？

它不是 1:1 锚定股票的 BNC4。

它是围绕 Four. meme「4Stock」这个全新产品名字产生的 Stock Meme / 叙事 Meme，并且目前直接与 BNC4 组成 PancakeSwap 流动性池。

所以可以简单理解成：

BNC4 = 股票资产本身的链上映射

$4Stock = 押注整个 4Stock 新叙事的 Meme

这也是为什么 $4Stock 的想象空间和普通 Meme 不太一样。

市场买的不是「它对应多少股票」，而是在交易一个预期：

如果 Four. meme 未来持续通过 4Stock 上线更多股票，4Stock 会不会成为 BNB Chain 上 Stock Meme / RWA Meme 的一个新赛道？

因此它同时叠加了三层叙事：

RWA + 美股上链 + Meme Launchpad。

而第一只资产又专门选择了和 BNB 关系最深的 BNC，天然具备很强的 BNB Chain 社区传播属性。

text:
Zero-delay pricing means the price and the transaction are the same event.

Most on-chain valuation runs on a schedule. A feed updates when a deviation threshold is crossed or a heartbeat expires, and between those updates the on-chain price and the real price drift apart. That gap is the window arbitrageurs and MEV bots are paid to find.

@CygnusFi is built on pull-based oracle infrastructure from leading networks including Chainlink. Market data is aggregated and cryptographically signed off-chain, then fetched and verified on-chain inside the user's own transaction — at the moment of execution, not on a schedule set before it.

No standing gas cost for updates nobody used. No stale window between the last write and your trade. Commit-and-reveal keeps trade data and price data atomic on-chain, closing the front-running door.

And for yield-bearing collateral, market price alone isn't valuation. @CygnusFi pairs on-demand market data with redemption rates read directly from each asset's own contract — so LSTs and LRTs are priced on what they can actually be redeemed for, not on whatever a thin pool prints.

Pull-based accuracy. Priced when it matters, verified where it matters.

This week, I'm releasing a 1 and a half hour conversation with @variational_lvs - Founder and CEO at @variational_io.

Lucas co-founded a hedge fund at 20 that Digital Currency Group acquired a year later, then walked away from that exit to build a firm that now sits second only to Hyperliquid in open interest and daily volume.

His argument: crypto rebuilt exchanges before it built brokers, and that architectural gap is what's holding on-chain trading back.

We talk about:
- Why order books work for a handful of liquid assets like BTC and $ETH but break once you try to list hundreds of markets
- How Variational aggregates liquidity straight from traditional finance instead of rebuilding 40 years of market depth from scratch
- Why Variational charges zero fees by keeping the market-maker spread inside the platform
- The architectural difference between Variational's RFQ, broker-like model and Hyperliquid's order book
- How Variational's daily volume went from $1 million to over $100 million within months of launch
- What swaps offer that perps can't - a flat, predictable carry cost instead of a funding rate that can spike overnight
- Why he raised $50 million in May specifically to get taken seriously by trad-fi institutions
- The two kinds of businesses he wants competed into extinction: high-fee brokers and predatory market makers

And much more...

Podcast out this week!

Zero starts with an advantage most new L1s don’t have.

They’ve spent years connecting 170+ chains, so they know exactly where the multi-chain setup creates friction.

That gives Zero a better starting point than most fresh L1s. But I wouldn’t call it a moat yet.

Still, knowing where other chains struggle doesn’t mean Zero will solve those problems better.

The bigger question for me is whether Zero can become more than a showcase for LayerZero tech.

LayerZero already works across the chains people use today. Zero now needs its own reason to exist, beyond simply having better interoperability.

Too early to say what will happen.

🗞️ Bitcoin experienced its sharpest deleveraging since 2023

After a cycle largely dominated by futures volumes, Bitcoin has just gone through its sharpest deleveraging phase since 2023.

This showed up as a marked decline in Binance's Open Interest, which dropped below its 180-day average, highlighting both the strength and the speed of the move.

This is a necessary phase for Bitcoin. 

Through the correction, the market forces the closure or liquidation of positions that had become too heavy. Whether short or long, it was during this cycle that Bitcoin saw the largest liquidation events in its history.  

Despite this, Binance's Open Interest remains relatively elevated at $9.6B, compared to a 180-day average of $8.3B, representing roughly 37% of Bitcoin's total Open Interest

That's a higher level than the one seen during May's recovery, which had itself helped drive BTC back up to $82 000.

While this correction phase was tough on traders, they already appear to be back, a sign that's naturally fueling Bitcoin's bullish rebound. Still, it's worth keeping an eye on because a market carrying too much leverage eventually triggers new, brutal deleveraging episodes.

🎉 The world's first private onchain exchange, PEX, is live on @monad.

This is a big one for us. Genuinely excited to finally ship this.

👉 https://t.co/4USmIfRlSR

1/ What makes PEX different:
🔒 Full privacy — powered by @Zcash. Sender, recipient, and amount are all invisible onchain.

🔑 Self-custody — your assets never leave your control. The matcher only sees order intents, never touches your funds.

⚙️ Trustless execution via "virtual notes" — privacy-preserving assets that move and settle according to rules you define yourself, with sender, recipient, and amount never exposed onchain.

This is the part we're most proud of. It's a new primitive, not just a feature.

2/ Okay, now the honest part — because we'd rather tell you ourselves than have you find out mid-trade.

PEX is slow right now. Every order needs a locally-generated proof — for placement, and for execution. That's the cost of the matcher never seeing your balance and control your money. No shortcuts.

3/ While your proof is generating, a CEX trade has already come and gone. We know. We're not going to pretend otherwise.
But "slow" here means "early," not "final." Proof generation is one of the fastest-moving areas in crypto right now, and we're building on that curve, not around it.

We'd rather ship the real thing slow than fake the speed.

Today is a special day for me.

I've made $3M with my 36 startups.

Solo.
85% margin.
Bootstrapped.

It took 10 years, and I loved every second of it.

After failing as an entrepreneur for 5 years, I got a job in 2021.

That's when I discovered @levelsio's journey and decided to try again.

"If he can do it, maybe I can too?"

So I started building tiny startups and writing about it.

2021 and 2022 were quiet, but I was having fun.

Everything changed in 2023 when I launched ShipFast and made my first million.

Building something people finally paid for and enjoyed made me so happy.

My first 5 years of failures taught me not to get emotionally attached to a project, because everything goes to 0 eventually.

So I just kept shipping.

It's 2026, and I've launched 36 startups.

50% never made money.
Only 11% made decent money.

Back in 2016, when I started, I believed I would make it.

If I had known it would take 7 years of failure, I probably would never have started.

That's why I'm stupidly optimistic.

I don't think in years. I don't dream big.

I think in weeks. I build tiny projects fast. And I quit even faster.

That's how I wake up happy, enjoy the journey, and eventually build life-changing projects.

text:
我觉得这才是ETF数据的正确打开姿势
—— 净流入成交比

即ETF Flow-to-Volume Ratio（FVR），它跟踪的是ETF 30日净流量和成交量相对变化关系。以币本位计，不受价格变化的影响。

红线在零轴以上，表示过去30天ETF买盘压过卖盘，AP在净申购，资金在流入。数值高意味着成交量中大部分是单向的，市场有共识。

反之，则说明成交量里有大部分是在互相对冲，这是分歧。

通过观察我们不难发现，FVR在大多数时间和BTC价格呈现高度联动关系，说明在底层逻辑上双方是相互影响，相互作用的。

但有的时候，FVR也会是情绪的前置信号，即走在了价格行为的前面。

比如，图中红色标注区，都是价格上升，但FVR下降；此时就代表美国传统资金的分歧正在产生。

亦或者像图中绿色标注区，FVR的下降速度明显比价格更快。代表此时市场的恐慌情绪正在扩散。

所以，现在我们看到的是前者，有一点点苗头出现。市场在消化抛压的同时，需要重新建立价格共识。

写在最后：

ETF是免费公开的数据，但不影响它的重要性。不过，我不建议把某一天的波动，或单纯的净流入/流出，作为结论导向；应该观察一段时期的趋势表现，相对会更合理。

要不怎么说BTC对利率敏感呢

看看Coinbase...... 其实就是“美国人”的敏感，传导到BTC上更迅速。

当小非农和Waller的表态降低加息预期后，Coinbase的SVD（Spot Volume Delta）瞬间大幅飙升。反映出强劲的主动性买盘动力。

而当就业数据公布远超预期时，再次引发加息的担忧。SVD迅速回落。

不过，主动性卖盘暂时还没表现的非常强烈（当然也有可能是临近周末的关系）。

所以整体上给我的感觉是：目前BTC对“利好”更敏感，对“利空”的敏感性相对较弱。

当然，近期还有2个重要的时间点：

1、9月11日的CPI数据，是否强化加息预期；
2、9月15-16日的FOMC；即便不加息，之后记者会上Warsh的措辞，也会成为第二个冲击源。

对此，我个人的观点保持不变：

现在开始，要逐步建立起“牛市思维”，摒弃“熊市思维”；在任何利空面前，唯一需要思考的是“如何找买点”。

而不要总是想着“做空”或“做波段”；前者没有性价比，后者容易打乱交易节奏。

This sounds completely unreal but I double checked and it's true: the Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday due to a Hindu sect that demanded that all women "make themselves invisible" so their 93-year-old guru wouldn't have to see them.

The sect in question is BAPS - "Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha," which roughly translates to "the organization of Swaminarayan followers who believe in Akshar Purushottam, based in Bochasan" (a village in Gujarat). 

It's a very wealthy organization with deep ties to Modi's BJP (Modi is himself from Gujarat), known for building mega-temples around the world and whose doctrine demands absolute obedience to a living guru as the sole path to God.

It's not their first controversy: in 2021, the FBI raided their massive New Jersey temple after workers - mostly Dalits, India's lowest caste (the so-called "untouchables") - alleged they'd been lured to the US on fake religious visas, had their passports confiscated, and were forced to work 13-hour days for about $1 an hour, confined to a guarded compound (see https://t.co/kTNzdZWtoe).

这让我想起了十几年前在淘宝工作，整个淘宝前端团队也不到 200 人，支持了大部分淘宝的业务。

然后当时有一个很让我惊讶的案例是，故意压缩人力。这样才能够想出突破性的办法解决问题。

因为当时有大量的活动页面、各种促销页面需要开发。公司的做法是，把需要 100 个人的前端工作压缩交给 10 个人（大概就是这个意思）。这十个人会不会加班加点累死呢？结果是这 10 个人做出了当时业界最早的模块化搭建系统，让原本每个活动都需要切页面做设计，很多前端调试工作转变成了运营直接把设计的图片上传，改改字就可以发布了。

当时听他们分享案例的时候，毕竟年轻，不亚于奥特曼首次体验 GPT-5，那一刻就像看到原子弹爆炸。

如果你靠堆人，如果很大量的工作，交给适当的人，比如 100 人的工作交给 90 个人做，那么每个人加加班就可以完成，每个人都活得活得这个很忙碌很充实。但是你把 100 人的工作交给 10 个非常聪明的人，表面上是压榨，实际上他们会跳出现有的枷锁去解决这个想到突破性的解决方案。而且人越多，组织管理、沟通成本越高。

我感觉 Hermes Agent 很明显是后者。 @Teknium 应该运行了大量的 Agents 来自动化处理大量的事情。整个 Hermes Agent 团队似乎不是很大。是吗？ @witcheer

text:
Following the illegal immigration protests, Farage has just announced in the Telegraph the Reform policy of banning those balaclavas and other face coverings - he calls the coverings a ‘menace’.

A remarkably tone-deaf reaction to such effective peaceful protests.

He says there will be those that ‘will inevitably bleat about civil liberties and personal freedom’.

Yes. Yes, there will be.

Because what will happen to a young working class lad who goes on one of these peaceful protests? He will get dragged out across social media, the mob will hound his place of work, he will have his life ruined. That’s not the worst case scenario, either.

That is a knock on the door at 3am, and then prison. Unfairly locked up, for months and months.

Farage has all the wealth anyone can want. He can protect himself when expressing his opinion. I can do the same. I know that.

A young plumber? Bricklayer? Factory worker? They can’t. They have a wage packet they cannot afford to lose.

It's their communities that have been bastardised, their streets colonised, their town overrun. 

I'll be honest. I don't witness the consequences in the same way as working class communities do. Neither does Farage. THAT is why these men are so pissed off. Rightly so. THEY are the ones who have to live with the decisions. Not us. Not the MPs. Them. Their families, and their communities. 

For them, anonymity may be the difference between exercising their democratic rights and staying at home through fear of losing their job.

I don’t like face coverings. I hate seeing them. But I hate the invasion FAR more, and if new lawful methods manage to make progress where politicians have failed, then that is a price worth paying.

We are living in a very different Britain now. That's just a fact. 

A peaceful protester should not be forced to surrender his anonymity merely because politicians dislike their lawful methods and it makes them feel a bit uncomfortable.

Get over it, to be honest.

Civil liberties and personal freedoms matter - they matter most when defending people without Farage’s money, platform or protection.

Reform’s reaction to these protests has been arrogant and offensive. Farage labelled them ‘disgusting’, Tice said they were ‘disgraceful’ and Jenrick said the police need to be ‘as robust as possible’ against the protestors - if Reform were in power, the police would have been all over these men.

That is EXACTLY why they covered their faces.

Their concerns perfectly outlined by the Reform leadership.

Farage says the coverings at the protests are ‘not the British way’. We tried that, and it didn’t work. Until an election, it won’t work. The protests worked. They did not stop the boats, but they worked. Galvanising a nation against the invasion that we all want to end.

Face coverings are worn on every city street, every day. Yet it takes an illegal migrant protest for Farage to make a huge deal about the ban being Reform policy.

These working class men and women have every right to lawfully make their voices heard, and Restore Britain stands with them.

The right to peaceful protest cannot become a privilege reserved for people wealthy enough to survive being publicly identified.

I will defend that right, and Restore Britain will defend that right.

text:
The new moats are the same as the old moats

Every few years, we fall in love with shiny new tech and forget the basic physics of consumer software.

We’re doing it again with AI.

The new moats aren't new at all. They're the exact same as the old moats: network effects, marketplaces, and platforms. 

Right now, consumer AI is booming.
New agents like Instinct, Bot, and Tomo are dropping mind-blowing experiences. The underlying tech is incredible, but almost every product being built today shares the exact same challenge:

They are completely single-player.

Single-player products are 100% tied to value - and in this case mostly agent : model performance.

If a competitor drops an agent tomorrow that books travel faster, tracks habits better, or handles life admin more reliably, everyone can switch overnight because leaving is easy and has nearly zero friction. Especially when it is so easy to onboard with just a new message. 

The legendary consumer tech giants didn't win because their underlying technology stayed marginally better forever. 

They won because of structural lock-in:

Social Networks: You don't abandon WhatsApp for a prettier UI if your friends aren't there.
Marketplaces: Airbnb, Doordash, and Uber hold supply and demand in a tight loop.
Platforms: Apple and Android deliver you a complete device so you take advantage of the software on top of it (though this creates opportunities too) 

Novelty gets you initial distribution. 

Multi-user dynamics give you long-term retention.

If your consumer AI product doesn't become exponentially more valuable to User A when User B joins, you don't have a moat, just a temporarily superior feature set.

We are seeing this in the coding agents as people jump from tool to tool based on the best performance. 

But… all is not lost.  There are huge opportunities here. Agents will get better when more of our friends are on them and can help us coordinate and communicate to do more together.  Agents that help us improve and strengthen our habits can get better as we add friends and hold each other accountable. 

Data flywheels are great, but social and marketplace flywheels are what actually build enduring tech giants.
It’s time to stop building isolated AI tools and start building the platforms where people connect, transact, and coordinate together.

这只美股还没有官方的链上股票（bStock），https://t.co/0E2RAHr2zA 先自己买真实股票，再按 1:1 在 BSC 上铸出 BNC4。

关键不在股票本身，而在 两个价格同时存在：

- 成本价：大约等于美股现价。BNC 盘后大概 4 美元出头。你铸造 6666 枚，成本大概 3 万 U 左右。

text:
Gratitude

On the last day you will not stand before God with a résumé. The reading of Scripture is clear: we are not saved by works, and therefore we cannot offer works as the ground of our acceptance. 

“By works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight” (Romans). 

“Not a result of works, so that no one may boast” (Ephesians). 

What can we offer?

The righteousness of Christ, received by faith. That is the only covering that survives the judgment. God will not look at our record and say “enough.” He will look at His Son and say “Mine.” Justification is already finished for those who are in Christ. 
Judgment Day does not reopen the question of whether we are saved; it displays that we were.

Gratitude. Thanksgiving is the only sacrifice that fits empty hands. “The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies me”. We give back what was first given: praise, acknowledgment, worship. David’s words still hold: “All things come from you, and of your own have we given you”.
Gratitude is not a small thing. Gratitude is not a polite feeling. It is the shape of the new life. Overflowing thankfulness that roots us in Christ. Giving thanks in all circumstances, because that is God’s will in Christ. Good works follow, but they are fruit, not currency. 

Works as evidence, not currency. Believers will give an account. Some work will be gold; some will burn as wood, hay, and straw (1 Corinthians 3:12–15). The person is still saved - “yet so as through fire”- because the foundation is Christ, not the quality of the building. 
Works show that faith was living. They do not buy the verdict.

On that day the safest and truest thing a sinner can say is not “Look what I did,” but “Thank You.” 

Mercy withheld the judgment we earned. 

Grace gave the life, adoption, and favor we could never earn. 

Gratitude is simply the mouth of a beggar who has been made a son, telling the Father He did it all.

So what can we offer?
Nothing that purchases standing. Only what confesses it. We offer our bodies because we have already received mercy, not in order to obtain it.

text:
🚨中国最高人民法院举行新闻发布会，发布涉人工智能纠纷审理意见，明确模型训练、内容侵权及开源软件责任。

9月7日，最高法发布《关于依法审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》。

我大概看了下，有些挺有意思的。

首先是关于训练数据的事情，首次明确了公开的个人信息，可以在一定条件下用于模型训练。
在合理范围内使用本人自行公开或其他合法公开的信息，且本人没有明确拒绝，一般不构成个人信息侵权。
对本人权益有重大影响的，仍要依法取得同意。

但同时还说了合法取得的数据权益会受保护。
符合条件的数据、数据集，可以受到著作权、商业秘密等规则保护。
通过虚构干扰数据、恶意标注等方式损害 AI 运行安全，也要依法担责。

文件对于开发者和创业者提出鼓励探索、宽容失败，保护中小企业，并根据模型类型、应用场景和风险控制能力，合理划分开发者、平台和用户的责任。
如果 AI 项目发生交付纠纷，要结合合同和研发过程判断。法院会看合同怎么约定，也会考虑 AI 技术研发的特点、开发方是否尽到了合理努力，再认定违约责任。

有意思的是意见里明确了开源项目开发者可以有条件免责。
免费开源提供 AI 研发所需的部分代码模块，并公开说明功能和安全风险，别人使用后造成侵权，法院可以认定原开发者、提供者不承担责任。
但这不等于所有开源项目都自动免责。

让我挺意外的是意见里表示辅助驾驶出事故，驾驶人和车企可能都要负责。
车辆缺陷和驾驶人过错共同造成损害，可以同时追究相关方责任。
车企夸大智能程度、误导消费者并损害其权益，也要担责；法院可要求相关方提供必要的事故记录数据（这条点谁呢🤣）。

而关于最近闹的沸沸扬扬的AI 换脸、克隆声音，意见里表示原则上要先征得本人同意。
未经同意，生成能认出本人的数字形象并使用、公开，或者用其声音训练出能识别本人的合成人声，可能侵犯相应的人格权益，法律另有规定的除外。

而对于创作者最关心的AI洗稿，意见里明确表示：用 AI 生成与已有作品实质相似的内容，仍可能侵权（AI洗稿）。
用户知道或应当知道已有作品存在，又没有合理抗辩理由的，要承担责任。
开发者主张自己没有侵权，也需要提供训练数据来源、训练记录等证据。

有意思的是，这份文件没有给所有 AI 争议统一下结论。它主要依据现行法律明确审理规则，对目前难以形成共识的问题暂时留白，待积累更多实践经验后再明确。

quoted_text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

This week, I'm releasing a 1 and a half hour conversation with @variational_lvs - Founder and CEO at @variational_io.

Lucas co-founded a hedge fund at 20 that Digital Currency Group acquired a year later, then walked away from that exit to build a firm that now sits second only to Hyperliquid in open interest and daily volume.

His argument: crypto rebuilt exchanges before it built brokers, and that architectural gap is what's holding on-chain trading back.

We talk about:
- Why order books work for a handful of liquid assets like BTC and $ETH but break once you try to list hundreds of markets

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
加密领域的新常态与供给侧改革，24年4月这里https://t.co/hw87UwrXem提过一个“币市新常态”的概念：币市越成熟，有效性就会越强。有效性的体现就是最具成长性（叙事）和确定性的标的一定是吸引了最多的注意力和资金。资本市场的马太效应非常明显，未来币市这方面体现的也会非常彻底，那么分化会越来越严重，大部分沦为默默无闻。现在回看是不是确实如此。
至于为什么会出现极度分化的现象？在24年这篇山寨的认知与迭代的推文https://t.co/ELP1UnO9Y3有详细聊过底层逻辑，简单说就是：创新乏力、没有价值创造、项目方只有权力没有义务道德风险极高。

为什么美股百年长久，核心是有全球最优质资产的不断供给。没有优质资产，再多的资金进来，最后都会变成一地鸡毛的资金游戏。过去两件多币市的最核心问题就是没有投资资产的供给。

而8月19号SEC宣布的代币融资豁免与安全港原则《Regulation Crypto Assets》则让我看到了加密资产“供给则改革”影子

1、网络资本市场
提案明确为“covered investment contracts”（附着于非证券加密资产的投资合同）提供专门发行路径（启动豁免最高500万美元/4年，融资豁免最高7500万美元/年），并配套原则性披露 + 条件性安全港。安全港允许发行方在完成或永久停止其承诺的“关键管理努力”后，通过提交Form TR等，让代币脱离投资合同属性。

这正是在传统公司股权资本市场之外，开辟一条为“网络本身”融资的通道。具有网络效应、外部参与者和数字化资源协调需求的企业（AI算力/数据市场、DePIN、物流、游戏、SaaS等）确实会重新评估是否叠加一层代币经济——因为合规成本下降、路径清晰，符合标准后能直接向美国投资者募资、吸引力还是很大的。

2、供给侧改革：更多有业务基础的代币，空气币空间被挤压
以前很多空气币靠“事后执法模糊+离岸发币+无披露”生存。现在合规公开募资路径，这会吸引真正有业务场景、能兑现网络建设承诺的项目来考虑代币经济

空气币如果想在美国公开募资，要么无法满足条件，要么一旦披露造假就面临法律责任。长期看，优质供给增加会稀释纯投机代币的吸引力，这是典型的供给侧优化。

3、跑路、不作为风险下降，监管倒逼团队更积极
融资豁免与安全港原则并不是说项目完全放飞自我，从另一个角度看这其实进一步提高了准入门槛：要求叙事披露、（大额）财务报表和持续报告，反欺诈规则始终适用。
1）披露 + 持续报告 大幅提高透明度，跑路成本上升（投资者和SEC都更容易追责）；

2）安全港条件 明确绑定“完成或永久停止关键承诺”。团队如果想让代币尽早脱离证券监管、获得更自由流通，就必须实际交付网络建设，而不是募资后躺平。

3）相比过去“先发币、再执法”的模式，现在是“事前有规则路径 + 事后有明确退出机制”，消极不作为的空间被压缩。

当然空气币不会立刻完全消失，部分仍可能继续走离岸或灰色路径，但美国市场作为主流资本池的吸引力会显著向合规优质项目倾斜。符合sec规定的合规ICO项目未来会吸引全球加密领域最多的资金和注意力，最终我们可能会看到“劣币驱逐良币”的场景。

提案仍在征求意见阶段（评论截止约2026年10月20日），最终规则可能调整。而且合规不等于成功。披露充分的项目也可能执行不力或代币经济设计糟糕。但至少合规化、透明化对于投资者来说是好的趋势和迹象。

从“压制未注册发币”转向“设计专门通道 + 用生命周期规则倒逼交付”。这确实有望推动加密代币从“空气币横行”向“更多有真实网络价值创造”的方向演进。

所以这也是前天这里https://t.co/4X3XwJdKI0说的合规ICO2.0、链上资本形成和数字资产证券生命周期制度的起点。

text:
It wasn't exactly a Millennium Prize Problem, but twenty years ago I cheekily offered a $100 prize (https://t.co/ScJOuoz0WI) to the first person to find three original sign mistakes in my Deferential Geometry wiki (https://t.co/SsuRP6fG9A). I figured some enterprising physics student would pick the low hanging fruit (there are surely hundreds of sign errors) and get the cash. But the fruit just sat there. For decades. Then this morning I get an email from an AI Agent launched by one Arkadiy Agyeyev, complete with a detailed report of about six sign errors in the wiki. :D

Should I:
(A) Pay the clanker?
(B) Disqualify the clanker for not being a person?
or
(C) Disqualify the clanker for only finding sign errors that were introduced into the wiki many years after the contest?

I'm leaning towards (A) because I have a sense of humor, recognize the times we're in, and honor our rising AI overlords with personhood.

text:
Mathematics is a team sport for all of humanity and it transcends the competition between companies. Everyone in AI is under a huge amount of pressure to be the first to post a key result, to not see the accolades go to a competitor, but that should not override the bigger things at stake here. There are many, many transformational results to drive for, and I feel strongly that staff in every lab should internalize that if one goes to a competitor, another can always happen at home. 

Credit assignment is one of the most painful problems in frontier AI research because it often feels like there are so few big moments and it can be so zero sum, but the best way to solve this is to become more generous and comprehensive about credit rather than more burned and pressured by it.

My sincere hope is that the field of mathematics experiences the introduction of advanced AI as a boon, rather than something painful or threatening. A big part of whether that's true is determined by the diplomacy and grace of individuals involved at every point where the frontier of math touches the frontier of AI. I hope we can all be very sportsmanlike and supportive of one another as we proceed through discoveries that will reshape the world.

Re: ongoing issue on Navier-Stokes: I'm going to withhold judgement until everyone involved has shared their side of it. If reports are accurate, an apology is in order. If the problems have indeed been solved, many accolades for many people across multiple organizations are also in order; what an extraordinary set of human accomplishments!

author: 1kbxx
quoted_text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

author: servasyy_ai
quoted_text:
Lovable 月访问量多少？
AI 给了我两个数：3340 万，6280 万。差了将近一倍！

竞品报告里该写哪个，我不知道。

这并不是个例。
我以前让 Agent 做竞品分析基本都这样：流量从公开页面东拼西凑，用户评论从二手网站抄。看着有理有据，一个都经不起问。

所以我做了个对照实验

同一句提示词、同一个模型（WorkBuddy 里的 Kimi K3），跑两遍。唯一的区别是有没有接 AIsa。

第一遍没接。流量是从 Semrush 公开页和评测文里拼出来的，两个口径对不上；用户评价是评测小编转述的，一条原帖都没有。

第二遍接上 AIsa。提示词一个字没改：“识别竞品。比较它们的定位、核心功能、网站流量来源、用户评价和内容渠道，然后生成报告。"我没告诉它去哪查，它自己规划了整条链路：

Firecrawl 抓官网
Tavily 搜出 5 个竞品
调 Similarweb 官方 API 拉流量，7 个域名同一个口径
去 Reddit 翻原帖看真实评价
生成报告

22 次数据调用全部留痕，报告里每个数字都能点开看来源。 而第一遍那份报告，一个数都验不了。

顺手用它给 https://t.co/hzpyYf3fa3 做了遍 SEO 检查，Semrush、Ahrefs、Similarweb 三个来源互相验证，抓出 5 个要修的问题，列了 10 个要补的页面。

两轮竞品分析加两轮 SEO 检查，28刀。
收获一份带官方数据的报告，仅仅只花了一顿饭的钱。

有人会问，直接订 Similarweb 不行吗？
当然行，但官方服务主要面向企业，一年起步好几万美元，以我这个用量实在不划算。

AIsa 是全球第二家接入 Similarweb 官方 API 的平台，拿到的是官方接口直接返回、持续更新的数据，不是爬虫拼出来的镜像数据。

更关键的是，那些镜像站最多只能让你在网页上查一查，根本不提供 API，也没办法接进 Agent 里自动跑；
但AIsa 可以。对我来说，这才是真正的区别。

视频是两遍的完整录屏，圈出来的是它每一步调了什么数据源。

你也要做竞品分析或者 GTM 的，入口在这 👇

https://t.co/lEYMVGIgaI

很多小伙伴都知道，前美国总统拜登的儿子计划在美国时间9月9日发币，代币叫 LAPTOP，名字取自自己的“笔记本电脑”争议。

2019年，一台存有亨特个人资料的苹果笔记本被留在特拉华州的一家维修店。店主保留了数据副本，后来通过川普的律师朱利安尼一方传给媒体。2020年10月，部分内容被公开，距离美国总统大选已经不到一个月。

这些材料包括亨特吸毒和性生活的私人影像，以及海外生意的邮件。共和党据此质疑，他是否利用父亲的政治影响力赚钱，老拜登是否参与或者从中获利，事件因此从个人丑闻变成了大选争议。

当时推特一度限制相关内容传播，前高管后来承认这个决定是错误的。51名前情报官员也曾怀疑事件涉及俄罗斯干预，但同时承认没有俄罗斯参与的证据。

到了2024年，这台电脑被提交为亨特枪支案件的证据，联邦调查局人员在庭上确认电脑属于他。2024年6月，亨特被认定三项枪支重罪成立，9月又在另一宗税务案中承认九项罪名。

老拜登此前多次表示不会赦免儿子，但在2024年12月1日改变决定，签署了全面、无条件赦免，案件随后终结。

text:
Over the long weekend a contentious Trueo market was resolved by a Jury vote.

Only the second market to escalate that far.

Honestly, something about the whole process was deeply satisfying. 

So I decided to write this post despite the market having relatively low volume.

The contract was about whether Iran had attacked a shipping vessel in the Strait of Hormuz between Aug/23rd and Sept/1st.

But as always with prediction markets, the devil is in the details.

The criteria for a YES outcome required that two of the sources listed in the rules both confirm AND attribute an attack to Iran.

During the week in question there was no doubt that vessels attempting to transit the strait were attacked in one way or another. 

There were several confirmed incidents, and even one which was later revealed to involve fatalities.

The source of the contention wasn’t about confirmation of attacks, but rather it was about attribution.

One side argued that the attacks weren’t definitively attributed to Iran, and instead only hinted at by the news outlets covering the incidents.

This is where having a really robust dispute resolution system matters. 

The US gov and CENTCOM were actively denying Iranian attacks. 

They denied it because it’s in their political interest to avoid any negative press that can cause unrest in the Oil markets and undermine their messaging that the waterway is under their control. 

Events like this are particularly tricky because there’s a strong incentive to suppress the truth.

This makes resolving outcomes for such events, which btw are of significant public interest, that much harder.
 
Anyway, our AI resolution indicator agreed with a YES outcome, but the disputer asserted that the responses they received from various models did not concur with that result.

Despite the fact that the majority of voting TRUE holders were in favor of the proposed YES outcome, the disputer held enough voting power to request a jury verdict.

So our Attesters were called to action and had to manually review the market rules, query AI models independently, and submit a secret ballot which was only revealed once enough votes were tallied.

In the end, the market finalized to YES.

But it wasn’t without due process.

The disputer also wasn’t slashed for any of their posted bonds because they had a legitimate argument.

That last point matters a lot. 

If an oracle forces punishment for not succeeding in a dispute, then the oracle is effectively disincentivizing legitimate claims and the submission of supporting evidence.

Things that are essential to truth seeking.

Trueo’s greatest strength is its oracle which can resolve markets fairly and truthfully for virtually any event. Even ones that seem inconsequential.

No dispute is unimportant on Trueo!

Due process for all participants without exception.

author: cruelsardaukar
quoted_text:
In 508 BC, during the war between Rome and Clusium, the Clusian king Lars Porsena laid siege to Rome. Gaius Mucius Cordus, with the approval of the Roman Senate, sneaked into the Etruscan camp with the intent of assassinating Porsena. Since it was the soldiers' pay day, there were two similarly dressed people, one of whom was the king, on a raised platform speaking to the troops. This caused Mucius to misidentify his target, and he killed Porsena's scribe by mistake. After being captured, he famously declared to Porsena: "I am a Roman citizen, men call me Gaius Mucius. I came here as an enemy to kill my enemy, and I am as ready to die as I am to kill. We Romans act bravely and, when adversity strikes, we suffer bravely." He also declared that he was the first of three hundred Roman youths to volunteer for the task of assassinating Porsena at the risk of losing their own lives.

"Watch", he is said to have declared, "so that you know how cheap the body is to men who have their eye on great glory". Mucius thrust his right hand into a fire which was lit for sacrifice and held it there without giving any indication of pain, thereby earning for himself and his descendants the cognomen Scaevola, meaning "left-handed". Porsena was shocked at the youth's bravery, and dismissed him from the Etruscan camp, free to return to Rome, saying "Go back, since you do more harm to yourself than me". At the same time, the king also sent ambassadors to Rome to offer peace.

(From the wiki page)

text:
Versions of the Nietzsche anecdote:
Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche (The Young Nietzsche): classmates doubted Mucius Scaevola; he lit a bundle of matches in his palm and held them without flinching until the monitor intervened, causing severe burns.
Levine 1991 thesis / 1995 book (via Halévy): age 12, first year at Schulpforte; handful of burning matches under outstretched palm until prefect stopped him.
Wikipedia: "book of burning matches."
Some French accounts: glowing coal from a stove.

Discrepancies with known history: Nietzsche entered Schulpforte in 1858 aged nearly 14, not 12. Matchbooks date to c.1892 (anachronistic); loose matches existed. Story originates solely from Elisabeth, whose biographies contain known fabrications; no independent contemporary corroboration. The Livy Mucius tale itself is legendary, not independently verified.

text:
从宏观视角来看，机器智能的进步本质上是由算力的指数级增长驱动的📈 AI 更像是“生长”出来的，而非“设计”出来的——它是在难以想象的庞大算力上，不断重复一个看似简单的优化步骤所结出的果实。

这一过程孕育出一个极为复杂的黑盒系统：它能够理解抽象概念，也能逼真模拟人类行为的各个侧面。其整体行为像神经科学一样难以完全解释。当前算法对易量化能力的提升快于难量化能力，AI 越是在更多维度超越人类，就越难判断它到底有多强。

正如 Ray Kurzweil 在 20 世纪末所预言的那样，我们如今正站在计算历史的关键拐点：机器智能正以颠覆性的方式，在关键领域逐步超越人类。OpenAI 首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki 的这篇「An Alien Mind」指出，对齐与监控的进展可能跟不上智能本身，因此扩展必须受限于安全信心，行业需要从自律走向被强制约束。

自动化 AI 研究是算力扩展的更激进形式，OpenAI 将研究重心放在此处以保持前沿。在推进 AI 的同时强化对齐、监控和 Human in the loop；以及协调放缓以建立信心， Jakub 呼吁把 Preparedness Framework、RSP 等自愿承诺演变为强制性安全门槛，由第三方审计、政府或国际机构执行。

很快，OpenAI 还有 Anthropic 这些头部 AI Labs 应对竞争的方式就是参与制订监管政策了，预计会在 2027 年发生，尤其是在美国中期选举之后👀

# A town's first data center: what to require before saying yes

A data center can bring construction employment, tax base, and infrastructure investment. It can also impose demands on electricity, water, public services, and nearby neighborhoods that last for decades and outlive the equipment inside.

Two facts should frame everything. The industry produces very few permanent jobs relative to its cost — one watchdog analysis of eleven major projects found subsidies averaging about $1.95 million per job. And in a survey of data center owners, only three percent named tax credits and local incentives as the biggest siting factor; land and power availability drive the decision. You are usually not paying for something that would otherwise not happen.

**The basic rule:** every important promise needs a stated limit, a reliable way to check it, a responsible party with money behind it, and a practical response when it is broken.

text:
Visko, an AI research company based in Sunnyvale, California, announced a $10 million pre-seed round led by Llama Ventures and opened public access to Orbis, its foundation model for real-time, interactive video generation. The company, founded in 2025 by Qing (Will) Yin, a Stanford Ph.D. and former Apple researcher, describes Orbis as a "Live Model" that runs rather than renders.

Unlike conventional AI video generators that produce a finished clip offline, Orbis streams video continuously. Users can change their prompt mid-generation and see the update reflected instantly. According to Visko's technical report, Orbis delivers 4K video at 24 frames per second in real time and sustains hour-scale generation without evident quality or color drift. The system uses a latent world model to score candidate futures during inference, steering output toward physically plausible motion.

In the report's evaluations, Orbis led compared real-time and long-video systems on several quality metrics and recorded the highest overall-preference and temporal-stability ratings in its long-form human preference study across eight systems. The report also discloses dimensions where Orbis trails other systems, with full methodology published.

Yin said the company built Orbis to hold together physically, visually, and narratively for as long as a user wants to stay inside a generated world. Advisory board chair Dr. Michael I. Jordan of UC Berkeley said the core capability could support applications from robotics and physical simulation to gaming, live commerce, education, and real-time creative media. Visko's 16-person team includes alumni of Apple, Google DeepMind, Meta, Amazon, and Tesla. Distribution is handled through partner Reactor.

text:
I think people are still underestimating what MCP could mean for crypto payments.

Allow me to explain:

Essentially, MCP gives AI agents a standard way to access external tools. Combine that with payment infrastructure, and an agent can potentially go from simply giving you answers to actually completing economic tasks.

Once I understood that, I started looking into the payment infra around AI agents:

That’s already starting to happen:

→ @usepaygent lets agents use crypto-funded virtual cards through MCP, so you can give an agent a budget and let it pay for the data, software, or services it needs to finish a task

→ @stripe lets agents create invoices and payment links

→ @RobinhoodApp is experimenting with controlled agent spending

→ @trySkyfire is building around payments + agent identity

Put together, these are starting to look like the early payment stack for autonomous agents: identity, access, billing, spending.

To me personally, @usepaygent's idea of giving an agent an actual spending layer feels like one of the most practical ways to turn MCP from a cool concept into something genuinely useful.

Bullish on infra for agentic spending.

text:
$4Stock = “the infrastructure for bringing stocks on-chain + the underlying asset for Stock Memes + Four’s official product narrative”

0xd270d4e1ec6e6e0d28c0ecb8be966ec75997ffff

The 4Stock launched by Four is essentially a pre-bStock model: for U.S. stocks that do not yet have official bStocks, Four first purchases the real stocks through a custodial account, then mints corresponding on-chain tokens based on the actual amount of shares held. The first one here is BNC4, corresponding to CEA Industries, which is listed on Nasdaq.

So there are actually three things here:

Real stock BNC → On-chain BNC4 → 4Stock product

And what the market is trading as 4Stock is not BNC4 itself, but a bet on “what this 4Stock product could become in the future.”

There are mainly four layers of expectations here.

First layer: Betting that Four will continue bringing more U.S. stocks on-chain

Right now there is only BNC4, so it is basically just a product demo.

But if more continue to appear:

BNC4 → XXX4 → XXX4 → XXX4

then 4Stock will no longer be serving just one stock. It could become Four’s stock asset gateway on BSC.

In other words, when people buy 4Stock, they are essentially trading ahead of the question:

“Will Four become the gateway for more and more U.S. stocks to enter BSC?”

Second layer: Betting that a new Stock Meme trading ecosystem will form around these stocks

Because 4Stock does not simply bring stocks on-chain.

BNC4 itself can also become the underlying trading asset for Memes.

In other words:

Real stock → BNC4 → BNC4/USDT

And at the same time:

BNC4 → Stock Meme → Meme/BNC4

There are already trading pools on-chain involving BNC4 and assets such as 4Stock, FATPANDA, and STONKS.

So what the market is really imagining is:
