text: People often explain Singapore, El Salvador, and other remarkable national turnaround stories with “easy when you’re a small country” whereas it should be “easy when you elect a leader who can think clearly.”
author: nayibbukele
quoted_text:
A few days ago, I shared the World Bank’s summary of the results of the PISA for Schools assessment conducted in 171 Salvadoran public schools participating in our education pilot.

Since then, I have seen some legitimate questions about what these results mean, as well as some claims about what they supposedly don’t mean.

So let’s be very precise.

First, what we NEVER claimed:

1. We never claimed these results represent the national average.

They don’t.

This was not the national PISA assessment. 

It was PISA for Schools, conducted specifically in the 171 public schools participating in our pilot program.

That is precisely why my original post said: 

“These are the results of our pilot program, which includes AI tutors and has been running in 171 public schools for just over a year.”

A pilot is, by definition, not the entire country.

2. We never claimed that these 171 schools were a statistically representative sample of every school in El Salvador.

They weren’t selected randomly from all Salvadoran schools.

They were selected to participate in the pilot because they were schools where the program could initially be implemented more easily: they had certain basic infrastructure and connectivity requirements, and school communities capable and willing to implement a new educational model.

That creates a selection effect, and it should be acknowledged.

But there is an important distinction here.

These schools were NOT selected because their students had exceptional academic results.

They were not our “best schools.” Not even close.

We didn’t search the country for the highest-performing schools or students and then test them.

They are normal Salvadoran public schools, urban and rural, in different parts of the country, serving ordinary Salvadoran families.

And the characteristics that made implementation easier: connectivity, infrastructure, trained teachers and willingness to adopt the program, are also things that can be replicated in other schools.

They are not innate characteristics of the students.

We can install connectivity.

We can improve infrastructure.

We can train teachers.

We can provide the same technology.

We can deploy the same educational tools.

In fact, that is exactly what we are doing.

3. These results also do NOT prove that AI tutors, by themselves, caused the improvement, although we believe they are a MAJOR part of these results.

Our pilot is broader than that.

It includes changes in teaching, support for teachers and principals, educational materials, monitoring and evaluation, technology, and AI tools, among other interventions.

Our AI tutors and learning platforms are being developed with @grok, @Kira_Learning, and support from I Hate Flying Bugs.

And the broader transformation of our education system is being supported by the @WorldBankGroup, @AgendaCAF, and @el_BID.

All of these interventions can also affect student motivation and engagement.

But that distinction matters: if students become more motivated BECAUSE of the program, that is not necessarily a flaw in the program or an explanation that somehow invalidates the results.

It may be one of the ways the program works.

The same applies to teachers.

For example, the implementation of the AI tutors, including the requirement for teachers to log in and out of the system, coincided with teacher attendance in these schools increasing from 76% to 97%.

If the program causes teachers to attend school more consistently, and that in turn helps students learn more, that is not an advantage that disappears when we scale the program.

It is potentially part of the intervention itself.

Of course, to scientifically isolate the causal effect of AI tutors, teacher attendance, student motivation, technology, training, or any other individual component would require a different experimental design.

Now, what DO these results tell us?

1. They tell us that 1,198 students in 171 ordinary Salvadoran public schools… 🧵1/2👇🏼

author: satofishi
quoted_text:
I made a mistake in my previous calculation: https://t.co/8obSpur6CU

It actually takes only ~100 years to cool Venus down to an Earth-like temperature if we block all solar radiation from reaching its surface and use the intercepted solar energy to power an economically feasible AI data center in Venus orbit.

That means planetary-scale climate engineering may not be as far beyond our technological horizon as it sounds. The biggest constraints may not be the laws of physics, but the scale of humanity’s economy, along with the amount of energy, infrastructure, and industrial capacity we are able to deploy.

At the current pace of growth in energy demand, we may be able to achieve planet-scale electricity generation within a few thousand years, if not sooner.

If we first blocked most or all of the sunlight reaching Venus, the planet could gradually cool. As the temperature falls, the CO₂ atmosphere would eventually cross into a very different phase regime. Venus currently has an atmosphere dominated by CO₂ at a surface pressure of roughly 90 bar, so once the planet becomes sufficiently cold, a large fraction of its CO₂ could potentially condense into liquid or solid reservoirs rather than remaining in the atmosphere.

At that point, the problem changes fundamentally. We would no longer be dealing with an atmosphere containing an enormous amount of gaseous CO₂. We would have a planet covered with concentrated carbon-dioxide reservoirs that could, in principle, be processed, transported, or stored much more efficiently.

In other words, the first stage could be thought of as planetary cooling, while the second stage becomes planetary carbon management.

Yesterday, Europe officially opened its largest industrial carbon capture and storage facility at Yara’s Sluiskil plant in the Netherlands. The project captures and liquefies up to 800,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year from ammonia production, after which the CO₂ is shipped to Norway and permanently stored 2.6 km beneath the seabed.

Some may argue that this facility produces little value. It may be true on Earth. But it could serve as a real-world testbed for technologies that, in a not-too-distant future, might be adapted for terraforming Venus. The basic industrial logic is similar: capture carbon, concentrate it, transport it, and permanently remove it from the atmosphere.

text:
Robinhood Chain is getting close to $1B in TVL, and @virtuals_io had already reported 5.6K+ AI agent launches there in August.

That got me looking a bit closer at the AI infrastructure being built on Robinhood.

A few projects caught my eye:

→ @usepaygent lets you give an existing agent a crypto-funded virtual card through MCP, which connects it to external tools.

Say you ask an agent to build a website for a client. You could give it a budget to buy the domain and pay for hosting as part of the job.

→ @helloSQD makes blockchain data available to agents through MCP. So an agent researching activity on Robinhood Chain could pull up transfers and swaps to help it understand what’s happening.

→ @ClawBankHQ is building financial + legal infrastructure for agents: bank accounts, crypto wallets, company formation, contracts, and payment rails, all accessible through MCP/API.

An agent researching activity on Robinhood Chain could pull transfers, swaps, and other onchain data to understand what is actually happening.

Most of this infrastructure is still aimed at devs and companies, but the direction is becoming pretty clear.

@RobinhoodCrypto is pushing deeper into agentic trading and payments, while projects around it are building the accounts, data, and transaction rails agents need to operate.

The next question is whether that narrative can attract real liquidity and users.

@usepaygent’s TGE is happening on September 8, which should be an interesting first test. As a Paygent supporter, I'll definitely be watching it.

text:
I see two main catalysts behind $CTO recent rally.

8K5X85PAJHAAVSvYaAzgVPPAPsqqHmvx16ZyBiscYF8L

The first is the connection between CTO and VIDA / VIDAx. Buying CTO drives trading and locking activity in tokenized VIDAx, which can indirectly affect the real VIDA stock.

VIDA has a very small public float in the traditional stock market, while CTO is paired with tokenized VIDAx. As more VIDA / VIDAx gets locked into Meme liquidity pools, the amount of supply available for trading in the traditional stock market becomes smaller. In theory, this can make the stock more susceptible to increased volatility or even a short-squeeze effect.

The second catalyst came from the Founder and CEO of Vida Global, who tweeted that if Memes can indirectly contribute revenue to the underlying company’s treasury through trading fees or licensing agreements, then the Meme and the company could form a much stronger flywheel.

Vibhu, the Product Lead at the Solana Foundation, directly replied:

“We can build a Meme launchpad for your stock. I’m willing to help.”

Pratt subsequently responded that they could discuss it in more depth.

It builds an AI Agent OS—a system for enterprises, telecoms, and MSPs to deploy AI employees that can answer calls, send texts, reply to emails, and chat on the web.
Typical use cases: missed call auto-redial, lead qualification and scheduling, customer service triage, CRM cleanup, payment collection, and follow-ups.

2. The token itself:
According to the community account, the company "doesn't answer our calls or respond to us."
So the community took matters into their own hands: launched a Solana meme coin, and plans to use the trading momentum and capital from the coin to buy real shares of the company in the secondary market.

This creates a flywheel: token pumps → buy stock → narrative strengthens → token pumps more.

Simply put: it claims to be taking over a real U.S. listed company.

text:
这幅莫奈的睡莲，是在堪萨斯看到的。篇幅一点不比东京特展那次小，根本没人盯着你不让拍照，也没有离谱的请保持4 feet距离看画，🙄 并且纳尔逊博物馆是完全免费的。

我当时坐在这幅画前，想什么呢？

在想，尼玛牛来为什么还在涨，为什么我选错了的加仓，为什么所有币都在涨除了我的。

在伟大艺术家作品面前脑子里却是这种东西我是真觉得自己很离谱。看的眼压高，头疼用手狠狠掐了下眉头，朋友问，怎么了头疼吗？ 我都不知道怎么回。

整个旅游期间我的心情都不是很好，可以说emo与低落一直伴随。 能意识到的人，会明白这不是卖飞一个币的事情，而是对接下来行情的开端判断失效，雷达失灵。

这是能力的退化，所以我非常非常非常的破防，很清楚如果不快速转变还会有下一次，下下次，因为这个行情是我们萎靡苟了大半年等来的。

但是在我返程的那天开始，就慢慢状态回升，在家休息后也很快开始转换思路和模式，那会不涨的持仓，也开始涨了。

一个人一种认知，一种思维，一种交易模式，一人一命，一人一局。

说这些是想告诉大家，这样的时刻会很多次，直到你登顶。心态要自己疏通，觉得不舒服就休息下，我看演唱会基本是错过了四天的行情，但今天也一样有机会了。

给自己一周时间疗愈是很必要的。

听了一个航司市场部专家电话会，复盘今年暑运，用的词是“哀鸿遍野”，摘了几句话：

1.市场需求明显下降，量价齐跌、哀鸿遍野，本来预期就不高，没想到比预期的还要更低一些。不只是民航，酒店、地接、旅行社、景区都非常低迷。

2.这一两年经济一直下行，无论从就业还是收入都在下行，到了今年暑期前后，消费者心理上有了一个集中爆发，突然产生了很强烈的风险意识，非必要支出全面收紧。

3.商务仓旅客也都开始过紧日子了，今年卖的好的一个产品是登机口升仓，以前他们是提前买好商务舱，现在是先买经济舱，然后登机口加500升仓。

4.民航局今年有一个硬性要求，就是预售价格不许倒挂，预售价格提高了3%-5%，但市场不认，价格一提，客座率直线下降。

5.今年民航暑运是2019以来非常罕见的超低利润，甚至0利润，大航司勉勉强强有正的利润就非常不错了。

text:
没想到百度也开了聊 AI 的播客，现在视频播客赛道越来越火了。

刚看完，感觉这期内容还挺有意思的，简单总结下：

访谈嘉宾两个，一个是百度伐谋产品负责人李安南，另一个是南京林业大学林海峰教授。

林教授研究松材线虫病早期发现，当松树看起来还正常时，能不能通过数据里识别出病害？

为啥要提前发现，因为能看出病变时就晚了（会指数级传染）

他们研究会看很多数据，比如光谱、植被指数、纹理……等，需要反复做实验找特征组合。

团队20多个学生，超过一半的人都在干这个，很像体力活。

有次学生交出一组效果很好的实验结果，林教授问为什么这样组合？

学生解释不清楚，最后才说用了百度伐谋。（哈哈哈）

伐谋百度推出的是“自演化”科研Agent。

李安南对“自我演化”的解释：在一个问题里，不断探索新的解法。

要么继续改进已经有效的方案，或者换个方向探索。

林教授学生的用法很符合：生成方案、做实验、比较结果，再决定下一轮往什么方向找。

李安南和林教授的对AI for Science 智能体的共识：帮你找到原本没想到、没空试的方案。

当然，分歧也很有意思。

李安南更期待自主探索，设想未来出现“科研工厂”：人同时照看多条研究路线，AI 持续做实验。

林老师则反复强调：结果好，还得解释为什么好；AI 参与再多，最后的科研责任仍然在人。

我觉得不矛盾，只是分工问题：AI扩大探索，人来判断证据、寻找原因。

视频最后林老师孩子案例很有启发。

他家孩子参加学校纸飞机比赛，他问：比飞得远、飞得高，还是滞空时间长？

规则都没说清楚，怎么知道哪种飞机更好？

给 AI 安排任务也一样：目标是什么，限制是什么，用什么评判结果？

这些搞不清楚，给你再厉害的 Agent 也没用。

感觉百度伐谋产品负责人想的挺清楚的，目前产品免费，利好学校科研工作者。

播客还聊了很多当下 AI 做科研的困难和机会，推荐看完整视频。

PARE is a cool example of what's possible once stocks actually live on-chain.

The TLDR is to think about it like Pendle for stocks: 

Deposit something like AAPL or SPY and it splits the asset into two separate pieces: the stock exposure without the dividends, which trades at a discount, and the future dividend stream itself.

What gets interesting is that you can now choose which part of the stock you actually want exposure to. If you’re bullish AAPL but don’t care about the dividend, you can buy the stripped stock cheaper. If you want income, you can just buy the dividend stream. And if you already own the stock, you can monetize the future dividends and frontload it w/o selling the underlying exposure.

FWAAA is a tokenised equity (likely tracking a real-world stock), ETH is the quote asset. The idea is to provide liquidity on both sides of the order book, earning the spread between bids and asks. The fills you see are me buying at one price, selling at a slightly higher price, and capturing that tiny difference, over and over.

In plain terms: I’m the guy sitting between buyers and sellers, making the market a bit tighter, and taking a fraction of a penny each time someone trades through me. The size is small and the holds are short, seconds to minutes, because the goal is to turn over capital quickly, not to take a directional bet on the stock.

text:
On that day of April 2025, I was notified I would go through a tax audit. 
How ingenuous was I.
Never would I have imagined the scale of the brutality and the perversity of the French tax system. 
On October 7th, I will attend the last meeting with the tax hierarchy where a shift in the decisions could potentially happen — which is highly unlikely. 
After that, I will be bankrupted. 
We will go to court then, but that's 3 years minimum of having to survive. 
Besides stating like it's normal to take 600% tax income ( not a typo ), it's the destruction of the willpower, the humiliation, the destruction of the sense of self-worth, the theft of the entire working time that should have gone toward making the only thing that my dreams were made of : making art. 
This is how my country treats the builders, the innovators, the free spirits who chose not to depend on their nanny state of a system and pour their energy and their hopes into exploring a brighter future instead. 
The most interesting feat in this, is that I didn't commit any crime. They admitted that I never cheated, hid income or planned any tax evasion or even, optimization. I did not spend. I did not change my modest way of life. I never chased money. The "pretend internet money" never reached my bank account for me to spend it. 
They just felt entitled to cash that out, 4 years later, at an arbitrary price set at the peak of the NFT boom, while I was working 120 hours a week and that no response had been given by the tax dpt on how to treat that stuff. 
Worse : the most official source of fiscal information for artists was displaying a very official-looking way of doing it right, that was actually very wrong, and a trap. 
Not gonna lie, the rare works that I've been able to produce since the tax audit started, have happened through immense efforts, fighting the fatigue, the worthlessness, the summoning of the greater good, of seeking beauty within the hostility. 
I have gone through months of anxiety, disbelief, and despair. I have stopped going outside and see the world, or people. I secluded myself with only my helpless questioning for company. 
As the ultimate deadline approaches, I am now noticing a new feeling growing inside of me.
Revolt. 
I hate politics. Stupid circus masqueraded in moral and illusion of democracy. But if you see me drop tweets outside of my artistic practice, don't bother them, just understand that I will not sleep, or stand the look of myself in a mirror,  if I don't speak up. 
💚 🤜

text:
Samsung Display Sharply Raises Next Year's Supply Targets for Apple Foldable and iPad OLED

Samsung Display has reportedly set a business plan to significantly expand next year's supply volume, centered on foldable phones and iPads, Apple's new OLED demand sources. The company is targeting 15 million foldable OLED panels next year, up from around 8 million this year, and 9 million iPad OLED panels, up from around 2 million this year. Combined OLED supply for Apple foldables and tablets would more than double, from a total of 10 million units this year to roughly 24 million. According to industry sources on the 8th, Samsung Display plans to substantially expand its shipments of foldable and tablet OLED for Apple next year.

Apple is the key customer of Samsung Display's small and mid sized OLED business. It typically supplies more than 100 million OLED panels a year for the iPhone series alone. According to market research firm UBI Research, total demand for iPhone OLED panels this year is 264.7 million units, of which Samsung Display is expected to supply 144 million. Samsung Display is understood to be planning a similar volume next year. The target currently set is around 148 million units. While iPhone OLED panels are expected to stagnate, supply growth next year is anticipated to come from new demand sources. The representative product is foldable OLED. Apple will launch its first foldable phone in the second half of this year.

Accordingly, Samsung Display plans to expand shipments of its 7.8 inch foldable OLED panels for Apple from 8 million this year to around 15 million next year, nearly double. The figure reflects volumes for this year's first model and a new model to be launched next year. For tablet OLED panels, the company is targeting around 9 million next year, up from around 2 million this year. After adopting OLED in two iPad Pro models (11 and 13 inch) in 2024, Apple decided to adopt OLED in the iPad mini (8.5 inch) this year as well. Next year, it will extend adoption to two iPad Air models (11 and 13 inch). However, Samsung Display's supply targets could change at any time depending on market conditions going forward. The key variables are Apple's pricing policy in response to the surge in memory prices and the resulting swings in IT demand.

For foldable phones, there is also uncertainty on the supply chain side. Concerns are widespread in the industry that shipments of Apple's foldable phone will fall short of expectations this year due to yield problems with core components such as the hinge and substrate. A display industry official explained, "Assuming Apple's foldable phone launches at around $2,500 (approximately 3.36 million won), shipments of roughly 6 million and 11 million units would be possible this year and next year, respectively. If the price is higher than that or supply chain issues intensify, shipments could fall further."

Currently, 35 rounds of distributions have been made, with approximately $14K–$20K in assets distributed to holders cumulatively.

OTC Sol trading protocol token: large peer-to-peer trades charge a 0.75% fee, of which ~66.67% is used to buy back and burn OTC, with the rest going to the treasury.

text:
纽约大学数学家 Tristan Buckmaster 今天发表公开声明，披露了两件事：一是他和合作者借助大语言模型在一个月内攻破了流体力学领域多个重要难题，二是他指控 OpenAI 在得知他的进展后试图抢先发布成果，并要求将他的合作者从署名中移除，理由是对方在 Anthropic 工作。

这份声明目前正在数学界和 AI 圈快速传播，涉及学术伦理、AI 能力边界和公司竞争等多个层面。以下是这件事的来龙去脉。

【数学成果：证明了什么】

Buckmaster 与合作者 Levent Alpöge 公开了三项证明：不可压缩多孔介质方程、Boussinesq 方程以及三维不可压缩 Euler 方程的有限时间爆破（blowup），均使用了光滑外力（smooth forcing）。他们还认为自己得到了 Navier-Stokes 方程的爆破结果，但该部分的 Lean 形式化验证尚未完成，论文暂不公开。

翻译成大白话：这些方程描述的是水、空气等流体如何运动。数学家想知道的是，在光滑的初始条件下，流体的速度会不会在有限时间内变成无穷大，也就是"爆破"。这个问题的终极版本就是 Navier-Stokes 存在性与光滑性问题，Clay 数学研究所在 2000 年把它列为七大千禧年难题之一，悬赏一百万美元。

需要说清楚的是，Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 并没有直接解决那个百万美元的问题。他们证明的是一个相关但限制更多的版本：在加入光滑外力的条件下，方程的解可以爆破。这对应 Clay 问题中 Fefferman 表述的 c 和 d 选项。但这条路径是通向无外力 Euler 方程的重要一步，而无外力版本才是最终目标。

这项工作并非凭空而来。基础思路来自西班牙数学家 Diego Córdoba 和 Luis Martínez-Zoroa，他们多年来一直在研究带外力的爆破构造，已经在"粗糙外力"条件下取得了成果。Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 所做的是在此基础上推进到光滑外力和 Euler 方程。Buckmaster 在声明中直言：鉴于这一系列工作，他认为 Martínez-Zoroa 配得上 Fields 奖。

关键结果在 8 月 15 日获得，8 月 22 日通过 Lean（一种形式化证明验证系统）的机器检查。Lean 验证意味着证明没有逻辑漏洞，这不是"信我就行"，而是有机器背书。

陶哲轩在成果公开后不久就在 Mastodon 上发表评价，称这是"a remarkable achievement"（了不起的成就）。他确认了 Lean 形式化验证的存在，也指出论文确实包含大量 AI 生成的内容，但作者过去几周一直在努力将其改写为可接受的形式。他提到一个关键细节：作者被迫提前发布，原因是"外部事件"，也就是声明中记录的与 OpenAI 的冲突。

在技术层面，陶哲轩对这条研究路径给出了乐观判断：他认为没有什么原理上的障碍阻止这些方法一路推进到 Navier-Stokes，甚至有"不可忽视的可能性"完全消除外力项。如果后者成立，那就是 Clay 千禧年问题的完整解答。但陶哲轩随即加了一句耐人寻味的话：他不会对有人靠堆算力和 AI 来暴力推进这一步感到意外，但这种做法"并不特别吸引我"——他更感兴趣的是消化证明方法，提取其中的新数学洞见。

这基本上可以理解为：数学界最具权威的声音认可了成果的实质性，同时含蓄地为"人类+AI 合作"中什么才真正有价值画了一条线。

【AI 扮演了什么角色】

Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 在整个过程中大量使用了大语言模型，包括 Anthropic 的 Claude、OpenAI 的 Codex 以及 GPT-5.6 Sol，最近还用了 Astra（后者仅用于论文写作和论证审计）。

过去一年进展缓慢，两人一直在消化文献、逐步升级前置结果。真正的突破发生在大约一个月前。Buckmaster 坦言，Alpöge 发给他的第一个 LLM 生成的证明是他"读过的最恐怖的东西"。他们花了两周多时间去理解这个证明，并试图将其改写成人类可读的形式。他承认 Euler 方程的论文写作质量很差，甚至用了"AI slop"（AI 生成的垃圾内容）来形容。

Buckmaster 把这一刻比作国际象棋领域的"深蓝对卡斯帕罗夫"时刻：一个数学家配合 LLM，一个月内完成了原本可能需要数年的工作。他认为这对数学界如何培养学生、分配学术功劳、审稿以及决定什么值得一个人投入毕生精力，都有深远影响。

【与 OpenAI 的冲突】

事情从 9 月 3 日开始变味。当时网上已经有传言称"Anthropic 解决了一个重大数学难题"，Alpöge 也收到线报说他们的进展信息已传到 OpenAI 内部。Buckmaster 主动写信给 OpenAI 的一位知名数学家，说明情况并强调这是个人合作，与任何机构无关。

对方当天回复，表示如果 Buckmaster 愿意透露细节会很有帮助，并提出可以提供算力支持。Buckmaster 提议下周通话，但 OpenAI 方面连续催促提前见面。9 月 6 日（周日），OpenAI 的 Sébastien Bubeck 加入，三人当天下午通了两次电话。

通话中，Buckmaster 被告知 OpenAI 的一个内部模型已经生成了一份大约 100 页的受迫 Navier-Stokes 方程有限时间爆破证明。Buckmaster 注意到，OpenAI 的技术路线与他和 Alpöge 秘密采用的路线高度重合，而这条路线几乎没有其他人在走。

声明中描述的通话过程暴露了几个问题。OpenAI 最初声称"极少人工参与"，但随着对话推进（Bubeck 不断收到同事在内部聊天中发来的修正和补充），事实逐渐浮出水面：这是一整个团队在操作，投入了大量算力，先从较容易的问题（包括 Euler）入手，甚至展示给 Buckmaster 的提示词本身也是用 Codex 生成的。

Buckmaster 追问 OpenAI 是何时开始处理这个问题的。这个问题没有被直接回答，但最终双方确认：第一个提示词是在过去几天内发出的，也就是在 Buckmaster 的工作信息传到 OpenAI 之后。

Buckmaster 还问了一个关键问题：OpenAI 的模型是否被训练过他们在 Codex 中的会话数据——他和 Alpöge 整个项目期间一直把草稿放在 Codex 里。他被告知模型不会查看用户数据。他再次追问是否用于训练，没有得到回答。

随后 OpenAI 提出了两个方案：一是 Buckmaster 先发 Euler 结果，OpenAI 第二天发 Navier-Stokes 结果；二是 Buckmaster 独自撰写一篇论文发布 Navier-Stokes 成果，注明系 OpenAI 内部模型所得。Bubeck 两次明确要求将 Alpöge 从署名中移除，说如果不是因为 Alpöge 在 Anthropic 工作，一切会简单得多，还说他在 Anthropic 工作"太烦人了"。OpenAI 还表示，如果他们在 Buckmaster 之后发表，会公开说 Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 配得上 Clay 奖金，称他们是"最接近这个问题的人类"。

Buckmaster 拒绝了两个方案，并表示如果 OpenAI 按计划发布，他会公开所有经过。对方回应："你为什么要毁掉自己的职业生涯？" Buckmaster 说自己是学术界的人，反问为什么公开会毁掉职业。回答是："如果你不希望我友善，那我也可以不友善。"

之后 Bubeck 给 Alpöge 发短信，提议两人单独谈，并说"我不确定 Tristan 现在是否完全理性"。Alpöge 拒绝并表示应与 Buckmaster 沟通。

【Buckmaster 自己的界定】

Buckmaster 在声明末尾明确划了线：他没有看过 OpenAI 的证明，不知道 OpenAI 的模型做了什么或怎么做的，不知道他们的数据是否被使用，也没有指控任何人任何事。他说自己只是在陈述被告知了什么、何时被告知、以及被提议了什么。他这样做是因为"另一种选择是让一连串公告讲述他知道并非事实的故事"。

他说，如果 OpenAI 的模型确实弥合了通向 Navier-Stokes 的差距，那是一件了不起的事，应该被大声说出来，但要带上完整的历史。

author: francescoswiss

text:
这可能是 AI 科研第一次真正意义上的「抢跑」争议。

一个数学家把还没发表的研究草稿长期放进 Codex。几天后，OpenAI 告诉他，自己的内部模型沿着非常接近的路线，做出了一个可能直接碰到 Navier–Stokes 千禧年大奖问题的结果。

事情得从 Tristan Buckmaster 和 Levent Alpöge 最近做的工作说起。

两人一直在研究流体方程的 finite-time blow-up，而且大量使用 Claude、Codex 辅助推导。

他们沿着 Córdoba 和 Martínez-Zoroa 的路线，把原本依赖比较粗糙 forcing 的结果一路推进到了 smooth forcing，目前已经在 IPM、Boussinesq 和 3D Euler 上做出了结果。

陶哲轩专门写文章评价过这项工作，认为这条路线有机会继续推进到 Navier–Stokes。

但 Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 自己还没有公开完整的 Navier–Stokes 证明。

真正炸裂的事情发生在后面。

因为 Alpöge 在 Anthropic 工作，外面一度传出「Anthropic 可能解了一个千禧年大奖问题」。Buckmaster 特意联系 OpenAI，解释这是两人的私人研究，和 Anthropic 没关系。

然后 OpenAI 告诉了他一件事。

OpenAI 的内部模型已经生成了一份大约 100 页的证明，声称可以证明 forced Navier–Stokes 出现 finite-time blow-up。

Buckmaster 马上警觉了。

因为 forced Navier–Stokes，恰好就是他们正在往前推的方向。

OpenAI 最初告诉他的版本是，这个结果基本由内部模型完成，只有「very little human input」。

Buckmaster 继续追问以后，事情开始变得复杂。

OpenAI 承认背后有一个团队参与，先让模型处理过 Euler 等更简单的问题，也尝试了很多条路线，用了非常大的算力。

然后 Buckmaster 问了一个最关键的问题。

OpenAI 是什么时候开始让模型做这个问题的？

按照 Buckmaster 的说法，OpenAI 最终告诉他，第一次相关 prompt 是最近几天才发出的。

而这个时间点，已经晚于 OpenAI 得知 Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 正在做这条研究路线。

事情到这里已经够敏感了，但还有更麻烦的一层。

Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 整个研究过程中，一直在 Codex 里放自己的草稿、推导和中间结果。

所以 Buckmaster 直接问 OpenAI：

你们的内部模型有没有访问过，或者训练过我们的私人 Codex 会话？

OpenAI 回答说，模型不会主动查询用户数据。

Buckmaster 又追问，那这些内容有没有被用于训练。

按照他的说法，这一次他没有得到明确回答。

目前没有任何证据可以证明 OpenAI 使用了两人的私人 Codex 内容，Buckmaster 本人也没有把这个推测说成事实。

但光是这个问题能够被合理地问出来，就已经很麻烦了。

之后双方又因为论文怎么发、谁署名吵了起来。

Buckmaster 指控 Sébastien Bubeck 两次提出把 Alpöge 排除在作者之外，其中一个理由就是 Alpöge 在 Anthropic 工作。

Buckmaster 不同意。

他还称，当自己表示如果 OpenAI 按这种方式发布，他会公开整件事时，对方回了一句：

“Why would you ruin your career?”

Bubeck 已经公开否认这些指控，称 Buckmaster 的说法「false and inflammatory」。

所以署名、威胁以及具体沟通过程，现在都还是双方各执一词。

至于 OpenAI 到底有没有真的解掉 Navier–Stokes，现在也完全不能下结论。

那份约 100 页的证明还没有公开，没有经过独立验证。

但很多转述里还有一个误区。

forced Navier–Stokes 并不意味着它和千禧年大奖无关。

Clay 官方给出的 Navier–Stokes 问题包含四种完成方式，其中 C、D 本来就允许 smooth forcing。

所以如果 OpenAI 那份证明真的成立，而且严格满足 Clay 的条件，它确实可能直接解决千禧年大奖问题。

现在最值得看的反而不是那 100 万美元。

以后科学家用 AI 做研究，最大的潜在竞争对手，可能就是自己正在使用的 AI 公司。

以前你把草稿存在电脑里，竞争对手碰不到。

现在一条没人知道的研究路线、几十次失败的尝试、刚刚跑通的关键推导，全都可能活在模型公司的服务器里。

而模型公司自己也有研究团队，也在冲同样的问题，还有普通研究者拿不到的模型和算力。

这时候把 AI 叫「科研工具」已经有点轻描淡写了。

如果工具公司自己也下场参赛，把未发表研究交给它，就有点像把交易策略交给一家同时做自营交易的券商。

Buckmaster 到底有没有被 OpenAI 抢跑，目前证据远远不够。

但这件事已经提前暴露了一个以后一定会反复出现的问题。

AI 时代最值钱的科研资产，可能不是最后那篇论文。

是论文发出来以前，那几个月只有你自己知道答案在哪里的时间。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
There is a heated debate right now. Tristan Buckmaster says OpenAI told him its AI had solved the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem. 

That claim remains unverified, and the discussions around it have erupted into a dispute over scientific credit.

Here is what happened and what we know so far:

Several different things are getting mixed together. Here is what the available evidence actually says.

Building on work by Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa, Alpöge and Buckmaster used Claude and OpenAI models to establish how initially smooth fluid flows can develop singularities under smooth external forcing. They released papers and Lean formalizations, and Terence Tao praised the advance.

Their results cover Euler and related equations. They do not solve the Navier–Stokes Millennium Problem, which additionally involves viscosity. A suitable extension could resolve it, even with smooth external forcing.

Then comes the disputed part.

According to Buckmaster, OpenAI told him on September 6 that an internal model had already produced a proof for forced Navier–Stokes, potentially taking that final step.

He says OpenAI’s effort began after information about their progress reached the company. He also disputes the initial description of minimal human involvement, reporting that the discussions revealed a team effort, multiple attempts, and substantial compute.

Buckmaster further says publication proposals included having him write up OpenAI’s result without Alpöge as a coauthor, with Alpöge’s employment at Anthropic cited as an obstacle.
He reports being asked, “Why would you ruin your career?” after saying he would make the circumstances public.

Bubeck has publicly rejected allegations against him as “false and inflammatory.” These accounts are contested. The social posts do not establish what happened in the private discussions.

There is also no established evidence that OpenAI trained on their private Codex sessions or stole their drafts. Buckmaster raises the question but explicitly writes: “I do not know whether our data was used.”

tl;dr

Alpöge and Buckmaster used AI to prove new results about how smooth fluid flows can develop singularities, advancing a research program relevant to the Navier–Stokes Millennium Problem. Their published work does not solve that problem, but Buckmaster says OpenAI privately told him its internal model had taken the remaining step. He has not seen that proof, and the claim remains unverified.

But rumors are that OpenAI actually fully solved that milleniun problem.

text:
LONG just reached a new milestone: its Tokenized Stock trading volume on RH Chain surpassed $1B, accounting for 15% of all Tokenized Stock DEX volume since RH Chain went live, while also accounting for 10% of all Tokenized Stock TVL on-chain. During the same period, RH Chain’s overall TVL grew 10x.

But Nate emphasized that what really matters is not simply the Raw Volume, but how much trading volume and liquidity LONG is actually capturing.

For Tokenized Stocks, simply tokenizing stocks is not enough. If the liquidity of a stock trading pair is extremely thin, then it is not much different from an ordinary Meme. Large capital cannot enter, and it cannot support real trading demand.

So what LONG is really doing is providing on-chain liquidity for Tokenized Stocks.

It can be understood as:

Tokenized Stocks → LONG → Liquidity → Trading

Currently, LONG accounts for 10% of RH Chain Tokenized Stock TVL, while contributing 15% of DEX Volume, showing that it is not only attracting significant liquidity, but also using that liquidity relatively efficiently.

More importantly, as the RH Chain Tokenized Stock market continues to expand, LONG has the potential to become an important piece of liquidity infrastructure within it.

Nate also mentioned that right now, whenever LONG sets a new record for daily trading volume, at least one or two assets also set historical highs in trading volume.

If the RH Chain Tokenized Stock market expands 10x in the future while LONG can still maintain its current market share, then LONG’s trading volume, TVL, and asset coverage could all potentially expand further.

This also creates a relatively clear flywheel:

More Tokenized Stocks → More Trading Demand → LONG Captures More Volume → More Liquidity Accumulates → Deeper Liquidity → More Capital Enters Tokenized Stocks → More Trading → LONG Captures More Volume

So what we should be watching now is whether LONG can continue to prove that it is the liquidity infrastructure for the RH Chain Tokenized Stock market.

And to do that, we need to keep watching its market share and TVL market share.

Bold is the tree hiding the forest of friends who gave up on self-custody.

After a decade, we simply did a poor job of educating people on how to use the chains safely.

Stuck between being too dogmatic, pushing for purity of an overly complex system, and too reckless of yolo mode

Let me try again; don't just bookmark this do it. Give the link to this tweet to your AI and have it help you:

1) Use @ambire as your main wallet; it handles simulation, complex tx, and is designed to work well with @safe 
2) Deploy a Safe now. I don't care if it's a 1/1 linked to your hot wallet for now; it's fine. It's already better this way, and with Ambire, using it is seamless. 

YOU DO NOT HAVE TO USE THE SAFE UI; Ambire will do it all for you.

3a) Generate a real seed; use pen and paper. You'll get the fancy steel stuff later if you want. 

3b) Too lazy for the seed stuff? ok, use a "hotwallet" for your signer generated with a passkeys with an good password manager, you have a Mac? The Passwords app is fine; you're a Revolut client? NordPass is included; you ready to spend a bit? 1Password has a great API, and you'll love it once you're AI-pilled.

5) The signer wallet must hold no funds, doesn't hold gas, doesn't do any txs; it's the key to unlock the door of your safe; it signs, and that's it. You'll learn later that proposing (creating tx), signing, and executing tx are 3 different jobs that don't need to be done by the same wallets.

6a) Now create a second hot wallet, "executooor," and send some gas to it, a few bucks of ETH suffice. Use https://t.co/jnYpeoZ6nv to have some gas on every chain you use.

6b) Don't want to do that? No worries, use the "gas tank" feature on Ambire; it does the same job you can always improve later.

That's it for step one, and just that you're safer than Bold and 99% of guys out there.

Step 2 is buying a hardware wallet and rotating the safe signer with it for much safer holding

Once you're there, you can start considering a 1/2 with a second hw or with an old phone you have in your drawer that you've factory reset and will use only for that. You keep it out of easy reach; it's your insurance if something bad happens to your main signer.

Then maybe a 2/3 and the nerdy stuff; you can always do "better," but the foundation of all that is getting your first safe deployed and climbing from there.

Do it now; it's not hard, it's worth it.

text:
为什么robinhood很多都会有一个线砸下来然后还能回去，换到bsc这种砸盘基本就死了？

Claude的回答：

两条链的池子不是一种东西，这是根本原因。

RH 链这些 pons 币都在 Uniswap V4 上，是集中流动性：LP 和挂单 bot 把钱放在价格区间里（交易流里那些 Add/Remove 就是它们在挂撤限价单）。流动性不是均匀铺满整条曲线的，价格一旦被推出有钱的区间，下面就是空的，几万块的卖单能把价格打穿到一个荒谬的位置。GAGE 那 6 分钟我拆过：卖单总共 $62K，最大一笔 $4K，就砸出了 −91%。然后套利 bot、挂在下面的限价单和 fomo 用户几秒钟把空档填回来，价格回到流动性重新存在的地方。这根针不是"有人卖了这么多"，是"这一段没有人接"。

BSC 上 Pancake V2 是全区间的 x·y=k，流动性铺满整条曲线，价格是连续的。要出现 −90% 的 K 线，必须真的有人卖出对应的量，一般就是 dev 或大户把 10–20% 的供应砸进池子。那根 K 线本身就是筹码转移，砸完之后筹码在弱手里、dev 已经走了，没有"空档回填"这回事，要回去得有人把卖出的量重新买回来。

另外三个放大器：

pons 模板 Locker 锁仓、LP 烧掉、creator 分配小，参与者知道针不是 rug，所以敢接。BSC/four.meme 上 dev 分配大且不锁，一根大阴线的第一反应是"dev 跑了"，没人接
一个币在 RH 链上有很多个池子（LAPTOP 有 23 个交易对，USDG/ETH/SGOV 各种），一个池子插针，套利马上把它拉回其他池子的共识价
RH 链一天就那么几个新币，fomo 用户开着提醒、KOL 狙击 bot 全盯着；BSC 一天几千个，砸了注意力就走
但不是每根针都回得去。SCRIB 01:15 从 $1M 到 $295K 就没回，因为那不是空档，是持有人在持续卖，holders 一路掉。区分方法就一条：针 = 大跌幅、小成交量、holders 不掉、10 分钟内回填；砸盘 = 大成交量、holders 掉、不回。

对操作的意义：RH 链上不能用触发价止损，要用 1 分钟收盘或者 15 分钟收盘；针下面挂限价买单是 bot 在这条链上赚钱的方式，你也可以这么干；BSC 上大阴线默认是终局，除非能证明卖的不是 dev 且 dev 没动。

ETH 系统化期权策略指数家族发布！

格致回测系统上周开始支持 ETH 数据，因此我们把 BTC 的策略指数原样复制到 ETH 上看看它们的表现究竟如何。

策略设置同样还是每周五换仓的 7 天合成期权，行权价取 35Δ，不做 Delta 对冲，不计交易成本。

唯一的区别是 ETH 的期权上线比 BTC 要晚一些，所以我们把策略指数的起始日期定在 2021 年 7 月 1 日（起始值为100），当天 ETH 价格在 2100 附近，5 年多过去了，经历两轮牛熊的 ETH 还在 2400- 2,500 区间震荡，只涨了不到 20%。  

ETH 六大策略指数终值和夏普：  

WKND35（周末宽跨）
终值 515，夏普 2.12，最大回撤 −16% 

CLL（领口）
终值 186，夏普 0.54 

CC35（现货备兑）
终值 175，夏普 0.52 

CSP35（现金担保卖 put）
终值 146，夏普 0.40

HODL（持币）
终值 119，夏普 0.40，最大回撤 −79% 

STG35（周频双卖）
终值 108，夏普 0.27  

周末宽跨在 ETH 和 BTC 都位列第一，而且也是断层领先。当然也出现过尾部风险，2022 年 6 月曾创下一个周末亏损 12%的记录。

周频双卖在 ETH 和 BTC 上都位列倒一，虽然 271 周里 66% 是赚钱的，但 2023 和 2024 两年分别亏了 19% 和 20%，主要是因为 ETH 在牛市中的暴涨非常猛烈。指数样本期内，ETH 单周涨跌超过 10% 的周占 27%，而 BTC 只有 14%（2026 年至今这个数字分别为 14% 和 8%，所以大家都觉得今年市场平静了不少），而市场给 ETH 的权利金溢价并不足以覆盖这个差距，所以周频双卖在 ETH 上更难做。

ETH 除了暴涨多之外，暴跌也多，所以 ETH 的领口策略还跑赢了备兑，这主要得益于 ETH 在 2022 年和今年的表现：
- 2022 年 ETH 价格从最高 4800 跌到 900，put 赔付了 6 次，领口策略全年收益 −43%，备兑收益 −55%，领口追平前一年和备兑的差异。
- 2026 年 ETH 在年初下跌 31%，备兑策略下跌 24%，而领口策略仅仅下跌 2.5%，凭借在暴跌中的卓越表现，今年至今领口涨了 25%，而备兑刚刚填完坑目前只涨了 5%。

最后我们把 BTC 的策略指数也重设到 2021 年 7 月 1 日和 ETH 做个对照：

- 周末宽跨：
ETH 515 vs BTC 721，比例系数 0.71 

- 领口：
ETH 186 vs BTC 309，比例系数 0.60

- 现金担保卖 put：
ETH 146 vs BTC 266，比例系数 0.55

- 持币：
ETH 119 vs BTC  239，比例系数 0.50

- 现货备兑：
ETH 175 vs BTC 407，比例系数 0.43

- 周频双卖：
ETH 108 vs BTC 282，比例系数 0.38

可以看到 ETH 在每一个不择时的系统化策略上表现都远不如 BTC，说明 ETH 的策略更加依赖择时。

=====    

以上报告数据来源为 https://t.co/DavBhD12uX ，本周新增了 ETH 的回测，欢迎大家也来回测自己的策略！

author: nayibbukele
quoted_text:
A few days ago, I shared the World Bank’s summary of the results of the PISA for Schools assessment conducted in 171 Salvadoran public schools participating in our education pilot.

Since then, I have seen some legitimate questions about what these results mean, as well as some claims about what they supposedly don’t mean.

So let’s be very precise.

First, what we NEVER claimed:

1. We never claimed these results represent the national average.

They don’t.

This was not the national PISA assessment. 

It was PISA for Schools, conducted specifically in the 171 public schools participating in our pilot program.

That is precisely why my original post said: 

“These are the results of our pilot program, which includes AI tutors and has been running in 171 public schools for just over a year.”

A pilot is, by definition, not the entire country.

2. We never claimed that these 171 schools were a statistically representative sample of every school in El Salvador.

They weren’t selected randomly from all Salvadoran schools.

They were selected to participate in the pilot because they were schools where the program could initially be implemented more easily: they had certain basic infrastructure and connectivity requirements, and school communities capable and willing to implement a new educational model.

That creates a selection effect, and it should be acknowledged.

But there is an important distinction here.

These schools were NOT selected because their students had exceptional academic results.

They were not our “best schools.” Not even close.

We didn’t search the country for the highest-performing schools or students and then test them.

They are normal Salvadoran public schools, urban and rural, in different parts of the country, serving ordinary Salvadoran families.

And the characteristics that made implementation easier: connectivity, infrastructure, trained teachers and willingness to adopt the program, are also things that can be replicated in other schools.

They are not innate characteristics of the students.

We can install connectivity.

We can improve infrastructure.

We can train teachers.

We can provide the same technology.

We can deploy the same educational tools.

In fact, that is exactly what we are doing.

3. These results also do NOT prove that AI tutors, by themselves, caused the improvement, although we believe they are a MAJOR part of these results.

Our pilot is broader than that.

It includes changes in teaching, support for teachers and principals, educational materials, monitoring and evaluation, technology, and AI tools, among other interventions.

Our AI tutors and learning platforms are being developed with @grok, @Kira_Learning, and support from I Hate Flying Bugs.

And the broader transformation of our education system is being supported by the @WorldBankGroup, @AgendaCAF, and @el_BID.

All of these interventions can also affect student motivation and engagement.

But that distinction matters: if students become more motivated BECAUSE of the program, that is not necessarily a flaw in the program or an explanation that somehow invalidates the results.

It may be one of the ways the program works.

The same applies to teachers.

For example, the implementation of the AI tutors, including the requirement for teachers to log in and out of the system, coincided with teacher attendance in these schools increasing from 76% to 97%.

If the program causes teachers to attend school more consistently, and that in turn helps students learn more, that is not an advantage that disappears when we scale the program.

It is potentially part of the intervention itself.

Of course, to scientifically isolate the causal effect of AI tutors, teacher attendance, student motivation, technology, training, or any other individual component would require a different experimental design.

Now, what DO these results tell us?

1. They tell us that 1,198 students in 171 ordinary Salvadoran public schools… 🧵1/2👇🏼

最近在翻链上项目的时候，又想到了solana的这个项目：CodecFlow，做机器人基础设施的团队。 @CodecFlowCN 

触发我关注它的是 $Microduck：一只 $399 的小鸭子机器人，预售 24 小时卖了 260 万美元。整个项目把机器人源代码全部公开，让训练机器人这件事，第一次变成全民能参与的事情。上线一周就冲到了5000万美金市值。

其实从中也能够看到大家对于机器人赛道的一个狂热支持力度，以及整个赛道的一个巨大潜力。

作为专注机器人和加密结合的基础设施赛道的一个先驱，我觉得 Codecflow肯定还在憋一个大的。

下面更新一下这个项目最近的一些关键进展情况：

1、SimArena——浏览器里的机器人实验室（已上线）

打开网页就能搭场景、放机器人、录数据。不用装环境、不用显卡，录出来的数据是 LeRobot 通用格式，直接能去训练。以前搭环境要一两周，现在两分钟就能进编辑器。
https://t.co/22BV6u2YW4

2、Fabric——云端算力层

浏览器适合跑轻量的仿真；真正重的训练和推理，交给 Fabric 的 GPU 算力，不用自己买卡、搭集群，按需付费。

3、optr——机器人的运行时

把「看到 → 思考 → 动作」打包成可部署的 Operator，同一套逻辑能跑在仿真、桌面和真机器人上。可以理解成连接「AI 大脑」和「机器手脚」的那一层。

4、https://t.co/0YO0oUepro / The Foundry——硬件启动层

做硬件的人常卡在「有原型，但不会量产、没钱、没供应链」。The Foundry 就是来补这段的：有可运行原型或明确规格就能申请，免费、不占股权，入选去深圳做 5 天工厂实地对接，还带 Pre-seed 融资和代币化路径。这是 CodecFlow 联合 Peaq 及多家机构一起做的（合作方公开口径），之后还会用来启动子网。
https://t.co/Xc4fWQjtOn

5、 solana:69LjZUUzxj3Cb3Fxeo1X4QpYEQTboApkhXTysPpbpump ——整个生态的代币

整条栈的访问、折扣、质押、信誉和数据市场激励都围绕它设计。可以理解成：用这套机器人基础设施的人越多， solana:69LjZUUzxj3Cb3Fxeo1X4QpYEQTboApkhXTysPpbpump  的用处越大。目前 SimArena 免费档就能玩，具体经济模型以官方文档为准。

整个项目我觉得基本面没有任何问题，只是之前整个链上出现了流动性枯竭，所以项目也出现短暂遇冷的情况，但是他们也没有放弃过。现在正是埋伏的好时机。

text:
Why is Dual Flow Batch Auctions (DFBA) better for agentic trading? 

Feat @slx_fi who are implementing it on their PerpDEX.

There will be two answers to that question.

1st -> a simple answer.

2nd -> a long one explaining it fully. 

Simple answer:
Traditional PerpDEX oderbook FORCE trading agents fight on speed. 

DFBA allows them to compete on their intellect (strategy).

Now, let's dive into how it really works.

It's a really important theme, as there is a big limitation right now for any types of agentic trading -> you need to compete on speed; your bot should be insanely fast.

Those seconds -> can change everything! They affect your % of good trades.

Superluminal uses Dual Flow Batch Auction (DFBA) and not a simple perps orderbook. 

Orders arriving at the same window time are collected and cleared together with the separation of maker and taker orders. 

So, speed does not matter.

Only matters:
Price and size.

Important -> all that happens insanely fast; you can't feel it physically.

Comparison of flow

Orderbook:
Agent decides → TX signing → RPC → network → exchange → order book

DFBA:
Agent decides → submits order → batch closes → auction → best economic order wins

So, what exactly happens with this flow?

Your agents fight with their strategies and not with their speed.

Whoever has the best strategy -> wins. 

OFC your bot still needs to get information fast and decide fast. But there is no biggest limitation on PerpDEX anymore -> everything is decided fairly by price and size.

The most important question becomes "Who submitted the best price/liquidity?"

And NOT "Who arrived first?"

Now results of your agent are fully based on strategy and not on speed. This way, all your calculations for arbitrage, spreads etc - will be fair!

This also affects the overall liquidity of the market. As you do not need to compete over speed, market makers will compete over price and size.

Which leads to potentially tighter spreads and better liquidity.

As a result of DFBA:
1. Liquidity is better
2. Spreads are tighter
3. No slippage
4. No fight over speed

With DFBA, the best strategy wins, not the fastest execution.

text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

text:
let me explain why some people has the see the unseen badge and some don't, and how the badge are distributed.

- Why the program exists

We have genuinely hard tasks that only experienced contributors can execute well. Low-quality trajectories fail QA, and data that doesn't pass QA isn't useful for training. The goal from day one: put the hardest, highest-value tasks in front of people who can actually do them well.

- How badges are released

Badges are not handed out manually. An algorithm runs every week, screens every address against the same criteria, and releases a batch.

The easy-to-miss part: badges are released on demand. If there are no hard tasks needing skilled contributors that week, none are released. And when we already have enough skilled labor, even qualified addresses may not get one.

- What the algorithm evaluates

Four dimensions, applied identically to every address:

Task completion quality (high success rate)
Verification pass rate
Performance on post-training tasks
Performance on 4-star challenging work

Two things it explicitly does not consider: how many trajectories you've completed, and how early you joined Axis.

That's why ~1,000 trajectories can earn a badge while several thousand may not. This campaign was never about rewarding volume — it's about identifying who can contribute the data that most improves model training.

- On "unfairness"

If you've done a large volume and don't have the badge, I understand why that feels unfair. But volume and skill are different things, and this program is built around the latter. Same bar for everyone — no favoritism, no manual override.

- No manual selection 

With hundreds of thousands of active addresses, manual selection isn't possible. We can't reliably judge who "looks skilled" by hand.

— note on our task testers
some of our part-time task testers were picked up by the algorithm and were participating. Because they test tasks regularly, they're genuinely very skilled — so the algorithm correctly identified them. We've now removed them from the program going forward to keep the field clean.

Transparent communication is how we build this community. If anything is still unclear, ask away — I'm happy to go deeper. Thank you to the Axis community for the support and honest feedback.

text:
I find it strange how Elon’s most controversial moments get amplified by the media, while the things he does that inspire people often get little to no coverage.

Where was « People’s Magazine » when Elon Musk showed personal kindness toward ordinary people (fans, kids or strangers…)?

1. Answered a dying teen’s last questions and made her design a SpaceX mascot (Liv Perrotto, 2026)
15-year-old Liv Perrotto, who had dreamed of meeting Musk, left eight handwritten questions on her nightstand after she became too weak to take a scheduled call. After her death from cancer, commentator Glenn Beck shared them. Musk answered every question (Tesla phone? No. Diner expansion and new games? Yes. Favorite anime? Your Name. Japan? Kyoto and teamLab. Hatsune Miku and Ani/Misa? Yes). On her final request, to make her Shiba Inu “Asteroid” plush (designed as a zero-g indicator for Polaris Dawn) a SpaceX mascot, he simply wrote “Ok 😀.” Her mother replied: “I wish she was here to see this.”

2. Publicly adopted a 5th-grader’s marketing idea (Bria, 2017)
Nine-year-old Bria from Michigan wrote Musk a school-project letter suggesting Tesla use the homemade commercials fans already made, since the company didn’t advertise. Her dad posted it. Musk replied: “Thank you for the lovely letter. That sounds like a great idea. We’ll do it!” She also asked for a Tesla T-shirt.

3. Covered the full repair bill for a stranger who used his Tesla to save a life (Manfred Kick, 2017)
German Tesla owner Manfred Kick saw an unconscious stroke victim’s Volkswagen swerving on the Autobahn. He pulled in front of it, let the other car hit his bumper, and braked both vehicles to a stop, saving the driver’s life at the cost of damage to his own Model S. Musk tweeted congratulations and announced Tesla would cover all repairs, free and expedited. The local Tesla Germany head personally picked up the car.

4. Shared a struggling woman’s letter, she said it stopped her from taking her life (Johnna Sabri, 2018)
Johnna Sabri wrote an open letter about how Musk’s persistence inspired her after her nonprofit failed and her life fell apart. Musk shared it with his millions of followers on Memorial Day. Sales of her handmade jewelry exploded. When he later accepted a small space-rock pendant she wanted to give him, she publicly said the timing and gesture pulled her back from suicide. Musk later posted a quote about hidden kindness.

5. Funded clean-water fountains in Flint schools after a young activist asked (Mari Copeny / Little Miss Flint, 2018)
After 11-year-old activist Mari Copeny (“Little Miss Flint”) and others highlighted the ongoing water crisis, the Musk Foundation donated about $480,000 for UV-filtered drinking fountains in all Flint schools (plus later funds for student laptops). Musk had publicly committed to helping houses with contaminated water above FDA levels. The fountains were eventually installed so kids could drink from school fountains again.

6. Kept a promise to hug a YouTuber because two kids at the World Cup asked him to (Fidias, 2022–2023)
Cypriot YouTuber Fidias Panayiotou camped outside Twitter/SpaceX offices for months hoping for a hug. At the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, two young boys asked Musk to hug “the guy who keeps trying to hug you in San Francisco.” Musk checked that they were sure, then tweeted “Will do it.” He later hugged Fidias at Twitter HQ on National Hugging Day.

7. Stopped to sign a hat and take a selfie with a child who called out from the crowd
In a widely circulated video, a young fan called out during an event. Musk paused, brought the boy up, signed his hat and toy rocket, knelt to the child’s level, and posed for photos. Musk later quoted the clip with the comment “Great kid.”

Small gestures that meant the world to one family to support that helped entire communities… these are moments that reached and touched many ordinary people at once. 

Sadly, « People’s Magazine » did not cover any of those 7 inspiring’ stories.

text:
The Bank of England was born in 1694 to fund a war. William III needed £1.2 million to fight Louis XIV, Parliament wouldn't raise the taxes, and a group of London merchants solved the problem by creating money from nothing. That arrangement has never really ended.

The mechanics were straightforward. The merchants lent the Crown £1.2 million. In exchange, they received a royal charter permitting them to issue banknotes far in excess of their actual gold reserves. They created credit, lent it to the government, and charged 8% annual interest plus management fees. The government got its war. The bankers got a legally protected monopoly over English money. Naturally, inflation followed.

Murray Rothbard traced this exact model across three centuries of central banking history. The pattern never changes: crisis, emergency, currency expansion, wealth transfer from savers to the politically connected.

By 1720 the South Sea Company's collapse wiped out ordinary English investors who had trusted a financial system the Bank quietly backstopped and promoted. The Bank's founders, by contrast, had already cashed out.

1694 is not ancient history; the template is still running today. Every quantitative easing program, every emergency lending facility, every "temporary" credit expansion traces its intellectual and institutional lineage directly to Threadneedle Street in the reign of William III.

The wars changed. The monarchs changed. The creditors collecting interest on government debt kept their seats.
author: Handre

text: The Bank of England's 1694 charter let it issue notes far beyond its gold reserves to fund the government loan. That expansion contributed to monetary growth. Prices (indexed to 1700=100) had already climbed from ~89 in 1690 to 120 in 1693 amid war and harvests, dipped to 104 in 1694, then rose again to 128 by 1697–98 during the recoinage crisis. The Bank itself faced a run and suspended specie payments in 1696. Multiple factors drove the mid-1690s price spike; the Bank's credit creation was one contributor, not the sole cause.

text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

text:
伊朗石油收入萎缩可能是加大对美国攻击的原因

伊朗存放在波斯湾外的原油，已经从9,000万桶降至2,900万桶，减少了约68%。石油资金约占伊朗国家预算的三分之一，这部分收入继续萎缩，对财政和外汇的压力都会越来越大。

这批库存是此前已经运到封锁线外的油，还能继续卖给中国，但美国的海军封锁让新的原油难以运出去。现在封锁线内的油积压，外面能卖的油却越来越少，伊朗还可以靠消耗库存收钱，但这种情况无法一直维持下去。

所以即便国际油价上涨，也未必能帮伊朗缓解压力。卖出去的数量减少，货款又难以收回，每桶油更贵也不代表收到的钱更多。政府支出、进口物资都需要资金，石油收入减少以后，稳定里亚尔汇率也会更加困难。

这也让我更倾向于认为，石油收入减少，是伊朗近期升级攻击美军的重要原因之一。伊朗希望通过攻击美舰、增加航运风险，让美国也承担更高的军事和经济成本，迫使美国在封锁问题上让步。

伊朗高级官员也提到，希望通过通胀压力，影响美国政府在11月中期选举前的决策。所以从实际情况来看，虽然伊朗嘴上说不担心国内的问题，但实际上伊朗面对的麻烦未必是比川普少。

quoted_text:
伊朗对霍尔木兹的封锁影响的不仅仅是石油还有粮食

前面我写过，霍尔木兹封锁导致的在油价之外还有化肥和粮食。现在这个影响已经开始在农产品价格上出现了。

彭博现货农业指数本月上涨接近 13%，是过去很多年里非常少见的单月涨幅。主要的原因就是战争和恶劣天气共同推动，尤其是霍尔木兹的封闭带来的化肥、能源和运输成本上涨已经开始影响粮食的价格了。

不止是粮食，中东还占全球尿素出口的 42%，氨出口的 27%，而这些都是农业大量使用的氮肥原料。霍尔木兹通行受阻以后，不同地区的氮肥价格相比战争以前已经上涨了 25% 到 50%。

目前上游的农产品已经先涨了，后边才会轮到食品加工、运输、批发，最后传到消费者买到的食品价格。摩根大通此前预计，这轮化肥冲击可能把全球食品通胀暂时推到 4% 到 5%，比较明显的影响会集中在 2026 年后期到 2027 年。

油价和运输成本仍然偏高，化肥供应没有完全恢复，同时全球天气又开始出现更多问题。这些综合在一起导致的就不仅仅是油价上涨和食品上涨，而是全球的通胀上升，消费力下降，而其中最重要的就是霍尔木兹，伊朗封锁的霍尔木兹导致的。

说实话，我到现在仍然无法理解认为伊朗封锁霍尔木兹是正义的代表，即便伊朗是在对抗美国，但代价就是全世界，这种全面的通胀上涨即便是中国都难以避免。

中国成品油最近一次调价是在 8月28日24时，国家发改委把汽油最高零售价每吨上调 375 元、柴油上调 360 元。以北京为例，92 号汽油从 7.78 元/升涨到 8.09 元/升，一次上涨 0.31 元。95 号从 8.29 涨到 8.61 元，上涨 0.32 元。

而且 8月14日 中国刚刚降过一次油价，北京 92 号当时从 7.97 降到 7.78 元。结果两周以后直接涨到 8.09 元，已经把前面的降幅全部涨回去还多了一些。如果霍尔木兹继续被伊朗封锁，中国的油价也还会继续上涨，甚至是化肥和粮食的价格也跑不了。

Uniswap Hook Incubator Highlight #6 - Veritas by Scientivan
 
As the final project in our look at the recent UHI9 developer campaign sponsored by @UniswapFND, today we’re highlighting Veritas.

Veritas is a Uniswap v4 hook for pools of tokenized content (a photo or other media registered on-chain). It prices a risk that normal pools ignore: as copies and near-duplicates spread, the original loses the scarcity its value rests on, and the liquidity providers are the ones left holding that loss. Veritas attaches a risk score to each asset and feeds it into the pool’s swap fee, so riskier content charges more and its providers get paid more to hold it. 
 
Using Reactive Network’s event subscriptions + cross-chain callbacks, it watches a content registry for every new registration. When a near-duplicate of something already on file appears, the reactive contract automatically updates the original’s dilution count. That raises the risk score, and the pool charges a higher fee on the very next swap so no one has to send a transaction or lift a finger. 
 
A clever way to keep the numbers true even when the change happens somewhere else entirely! 
 
Read more on our blog 👇

text:
Would you ever put money into a rocket or space venture?

For everyday investors, that used to be a nonstarter, these deals were basically behind closed doors.

Even now, many of the most compelling space players are still private: reusable launch systems, satellite networks, orbital infrastructure, in-space manufacturing, and even data-center concepts beyond Earth.

And even if you manage to get in through a private vehicle, you may be locked up for years, waiting for an IPO, a buyout, or a secondary transaction to finally provide an exit.

@Starcap_xyz wants to change that with $RKST and $SPACE.

But before you judge because there are two tokens, let's dive on both.

--

➥ How $SPACE works (Not Live Yet)

Starcap acquires equity in private space companies through funding rounds, secondary deals, and other investment vehicles.

Then:

Private space companies → Starcap fund → SPACE

SPACE represents exposure to that fund. So instead of buying five different private space companies individually, you could potentially get exposure through one tokenized vehicle.

Think of it like a private-space ETF, but onchain.

The bigger idea comes afterward, because SPACE is onchain, Starcap wants to build:

SPACE → trading → collateral → borrowing → structured products

This could turn normally “dead” private equity into something financially usable and composable.

--

➥ What about $RKST?

RKST is different.

→ SPACE = broad private-space exposure.
→ RKST = specialized exposure to reusable rockets.

Starcap is pitching RKST as its first onchain financing instrument for rockets, built around the premise that truly reusable vehicles might start to look less like one-off hardware and more like cash‑generating infrastructure.

The logic is straightforward: a rocket is expensive upfront, but if it can fly over and over and produce steady launch income, you can start stacking familiar capital structures on top of it:

capital → revenue → debt → leasing → structured products

Basically the aircraft playbook, ported to launch. If that holds, RKST has a path to becoming something far more meaningful than “just a rocket token.”

But that’s also the foggiest part right now. Starcap still hasn’t clearly laid out:

→ what, in legal terms, RKST actually has a claim on,
→ what the underlying cash-flow source is,
→ how value accrues to holders, distributions, buybacks, redemptions, or some other routing of revenues.

The only concrete moves mentioned so far: burning 14.3% from the dev wallet (taking supply down to 85.7%) and locking 5% to vest over six months for contributors supporting operations and growth.

--

➥ Takeaway (NFA. DYOR)

Starcap stands out because the upside isn’t just slapping tokens on space equities, it’s the chance to bootstrap a fully onchain capital market for the space economy, complete with structured financial products living natively on-chain.

If Starcap pulls it off, SPACE and RKST may end up being the opening act for a far broader financial stack spanning rockets, satellites, orbital infrastructure, and the rest of the space-asset universe.

黑客偷币，程序员领 U：朝鲜在加密世界的存在感有点强~

据韩联社报道，近日美国联邦法院下令没收约 21.27 万美元稳定币，包括 158,123 枚 USDC 和 54,574 枚 USDT。

检方称，这笔钱涉嫌涉及洗钱，据信来自至少 14 名朝鲜海外 IT 人员的工资。

美国司法部原本申请没收约 774 万美元相关加密资产，但此次法院只支持了其中一部分，其余地址因未能得到合理确认，未获批准没收。

这些“工资”是怎么来的？

按美司法部的指控，朝鲜 IT 人员利用虚假或盗用的身份，进入海外企业远程工作，其中包括区块链开发公司。雇主用 USDT、USDC 发薪，他们再通过拆分转账、跨链换币等方式掩盖资金来源，最终将钱转回朝鲜。

而提到朝鲜与加密货币，更出名的还是黑客盗币。

据统计 2025 年，朝鲜黑客至少盗取了 20.2 亿美元加密资产，规模相当于整个国家 GDP 的 6%，差不多是全国 22 天的经济产出。

冒用身份入职，再用稳定币收薪。对加密公司来说，要防的风险也可能藏在远程招聘的简历里。

text:
写完那篇 25万次阅读、2K 点赞收藏的《Agent Memory 五层架构》  https://t.co/ZEJtJQv5Vj 之后，有人问我有没有把 agent memory 发挥到极致的产品可以用。我用 @TodayAIofficial 跑了一段时间，它其实就是这套架构的一个真实运行实例：

常驻画像层，把 X、GitHub、Gmail 绑上去之后，它自己建立了我的技术栈画像——主力语言 Go 和 TypeScript、活跃仓库 newshub 和 carrywatch、最近的 commit、哪些 CI 在失败。这些我一个字都没告诉它，全是它直接从绑定的数据源里读出来的；

历史召回层，我今天刚跑完一个完整闭环：Gmail 收到 Google Search Console 的中文报警邮件，按往常我大概率会忽略它，但 DD（我的 Today AI 助手的名字）主动提醒了我，还自己提取出索引失败的根因，对照 GitHub 上下文理解了 newshub 这个项目，给出 soft-404、canonical 冲突、robots.txt 三条修复建议。我按建议优化了一版，整个排查过程，DD 没问过我“你的项目是什么”“用什么技术栈”这类问题——需要的前置信息，它都从绑定的数据源里自己翻出来了；

治理层是我比较在意的一点：记忆文件我能直接看、直接改、直接删。今天清理了 9 个文件里的旧身份信息，这层透明度直接决定了 agent memory 是不是黑箱，能不能可视化维护，是一个 Agent 值不值得长期信任的前提。

如果要我说，Memory 的价值不在保存信息数量多寡，而在恰到好处的分层。DD 目前做到了画像和历史召回，治理层能直接维护，反思和技能沉淀这层也初见苗头。相比我日常重度用的 Claude Code 和 Codex，最大的不同是：换一个新会话，那两个工具还得我从头交代一遍背景；DD 不用，这次的排查，就是它自己从邮箱中把邮件，关联到了仓库，全程没让我重新解释。

德尔斐神庙刻着一句话：认识你自己。泰勒斯被问到何事最难为，答的也是这几个字。两千多年后，一个 agent 绑了你的 GitHub、Gmail、X，开始在你授权的那部分上下文里，比你自己更系统地记住你在做什么、怎么做、踩过什么坑——DD 提醒我的那条 Gmail 报警，就是它替我先看见的一件小事。甚至，它也可以直接读取 iOS 上的健康数据，“认识你自己”这个故事的边界正在进一步拓展。

这可能是往后 AI Agent 产品更底层的逻辑：一个真正懂你的 agent，能帮你看见自己。

我最近一直在折腾一套 ChatGPT + 自建链上监控工作流。
这两天它抓到的一个案例很值得记： $MARLIN

项目 launch 后大约 23 秒，我的工作流就捕获到了它。
当时很多信息还没完全验证，所以我没有重仓，只先放了 50U canary。
但后面从最早发现的位置算，$MARLIN 最高已经走出了接近 50x 的级别。

真正让我继续提高判断的，不是价格本身，而是它后面开始把机制真正执行出来了。
$MARLIN 讲的是：fee → protocol-owned stock-token LP → LP 收益分给 holders。
很多项目机制写得很好，但最后只是 PPT。MARLIN 这两天不一样，它开始拿真实资本反复执行。

先有 AMC、HIMS，后面又加了 SGOV。
最新官方更新里，protocol-owned book 已经增长到约 $52.3K，覆盖 4 个 pools。
HIMS 还出现了退出原区间后更低位置重新进场，又新增 AMD position。
这说明它的机制正在从 claim 变成 repeated execution。

这单也顺手打出了我系统的一个 bug：
以前它太保守，总想等所有证据都完全确认，再给正式 Alpha Call。
但低市值机会最大的问题就是：等一切都确认，赔率往往已经没了。

所以我现在把流程拆成了：
Discovery → Canary → Early Alpha → Confirmed Alpha → Size-up

发现机会，和决定重仓，本来就不该共用一套门槛。

这单我最早只放了 50U，后来大约在 $1M MC 附近先减掉了一半，剩余仓位继续让 AI 跟踪。
我现在也不会因为它涨了很多就去追高，尤其 holder payout 这条，我还在等更独立的链上验证。

但作为一次 AI 找低市值 Alpha 的实战，$MARLIN 已经很值得记录。

TRX ETF 明日登陆 Cboe：这次带进去的不只是价格敞口

01｜TRXS 预计 9 月 9 日上市

Canary Capital 推出的质押型 TRX ETF 预计将于 9 月 9 日登陆 Cboe，交易代码为 TRXS。这意味着传统投资者未来无需注册交易所、管理钱包或保存私钥，也可以直接通过美股账户获得 TRX 的价格敞口。

02｜它并不是普通的现货 ETF

普通加密 ETF 的逻辑，是由基金买入并托管代币，让投资者通过证券账户追踪价格变化；TRXS 更特别的地方在于，它不仅持有 TRX，还计划在正常情况下将至少 90% 的 TRX 用于质押，让基金持仓继续参与 TRON 网络并产生链上收益。

03｜把 Crypto 的原生收益一起装进 ETF

TRXS带进传统金融市场的不只是TRX的价格敞口，还有参与TRON网络运行产生的质押奖励。根据披露，基金会将大部分TRX用于质押。扣除最高不超过20%的质押服务费后，剩余奖励将继续留在基金，并反映到每日净值中。

也就是说，投资者虽然不会直接收到TRX利息，但依然能够通过基金净值享受质押收益。其他ETF只是把Crypto装进证券账户，TRXS则尝试把Crypto的原生收益机制也一起带进去。

04｜TRON 得到的不只是一个新增买盘

如果 TRXS 顺利上市并持续获得资金流入，基金就需要不断买入并托管 TRX，其中绝大部分还会进入质押。它带来的不仅是一次性的配置需求，也会让更多 TRX 长期参与网络运行，把传统市场的资金与 TRON 的链上经济直接连接起来。

05｜ETF 承认价格，质押承认网络价值

BTC ETF 让传统市场开始配置比特币，ETH ETF 把智能合约资产带进主流账户，而 TRXS 更进一步展示了另一种可能：传统投资者购买的不只是一个代币的涨跌，也是这条公链持续运行所创造的收益。TRX 被带进 Cboe 的那一刻，进入传统金融体系的不只是价格，还有 TRON 网络本身的价值。

text:
Dense retrieval just got a powerful patch button.

“Embedding surgery” lets you locally edit a handful of stored document embeddings—no retraining, no index rebuild needed. Each tweak is a tiny move in vector space, guided by editorial feedback, clicks, or LLM re-rankers, to correct ranking mistakes at scale.

On DL-Hard, the symmetric variant yields up to +60.6% nDCG@10 with gold feedback. Even noisy clicks or LLM pseudo-labels deliver reliable gains. The average edit is minuscule (<0.05 L2-norm), preserving global structure, and in-place updates work on massive indexes (185k edits, FAISS, <0.4% cluster migration).

Corrections propagate to related queries, and combining with query-adaptation (CoRocchio) stacks the gains—while staying robust to noise.

Adaptive, fine-grained, fast: embedding surgery is a practical fix for evolving search intent and editorial policy in dense retrieval.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/mwceujoKQ8

全都加速了。有位搞 AI 制药的老板，昨天发了篇很爆炸的论文。

他们把大量基因、蛋白、疾病、衰老相关数据，喂给 AI，然后 AI 自己排序，哪个蛋白既跟肺慢慢变硬、结疤有关，又跟衰老的几条关键通路有关。

最后它盯上了一个叫 TNIK 的东西，可以粗略理解成细胞内的一个开关。这个开关一开，细胞更容易往结疤、发炎、老化那边走。

开关找出后，另一套 AI 开始思考，能按住这个开关的小分子。这也意味着以前要试成千上万种化学结构，这次让电脑自己去画分子结构，最终科学家再从电脑画出来的方案里，挑几个去做实验，最后做出了这种药。

目前初期结果是，药拿去给肺结疤的病人吃了 12 周，没吃药的人，12 周后肺功能还在往下掉，而吃了较高剂量的人，平均肺功能不但没掉，还往上抬了一点。

在这个结果下，这款药进入到了更大规模的试验里，而这背后一切，全是靠 AI 在驱动。

text:
I'm at the point in Honest Money's journey where I'm beginning to realise the full weight of what I do. Having a platform comes with great responsibility to share information that is honest and to showcase differing schools of thought.

When I first started posting and releasing episodes, the criticism came from the BSV crowd. Now it comes from the BIP-110 crowd.

For the record: I don't like spam. I want Bitcoin to stay decentralised and secure. And I strongly believe in opposition and dissenting voices to keep the protocol honest.

But I'm also aware of my own limitations. I don't possess the technical know-how to adjudicate the depth of this debate, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I can do is put the people who understand it in front of a wider audience.

The role I play is top of the funnel. My podcast was always designed to welcome curious new minds into Bitcoin, and to entertain and inform the existing crowd by interviewing experts from different disciplines. I can have a constructive conversation with anyone, no matter where they land, and I think we're all richer for exploring differing schools of thought.

So, to the recent wave of criticism.

Here's what I'm willing to do:

1. Take constructive criticism on how to improve.
2. Receive guest suggestions on who you'd like to hear from.
3. Receive question suggestions to make sure I'm doing my job right.

Here's what I'm not willing to do:

1. Accept your definition of what a "real Bitcoiner" is.
2. Let you weaponise my podcast for your fight.
3. Take shit from people doing nothing for Bitcoin.

The name is the whole thesis. Honest Money was designed to make normies stop and ask what actually makes money honest. It was never designed as a venue for internal purity fights.

text:
Spamming easy tasks might not be the optimal Axis strategy anymore.

@axisrobotics launched the Challenger Program, a gated pool of harder tasks reserved for its stronger robot trainers.

Building your Axis activity?
https://t.co/EPnmS2s501

The headline is 2-3x more Axis Points per task.

But I think the whitelist system is the more interesting part.

You can't apply for it.

Axis reviews every contributor's history weekly across two sides: volume and quality.

Volume isn't just how many tasks you've spammed.

They look at:

→ distinct tasks completed
→ Pre-Training activity
→ Post-Training activity
→ lifetime verification pass rate

Then comes quality.

Your performance is compared against other contributors doing the same tasks, and Axis checks whether that performance stays consistent over time.

A few lucky submissions aren't enough.

Neither is repeating the same easy task hundreds of times.

The exact thresholds are kept private, which makes sense if the goal is to make the system harder to game.

If you qualify, the “Seek the Unseen” badge lights up in your Portfolio and gives you access to the Challenger task interface.

The schedule has also been updated:

→ whitelist refresh: Monday 12:00 SGT
→ task drop: Monday 16:00 SGT
→ 20-50 high-difficulty tasks per week
→ limited + first come, first served
→ 2-3x Axis Points per completed task

This feels like an important evolution for the network.

Getting people to generate robot trajectories is one problem.

Figuring out who consistently generates the best ones is another.

Axis is starting to build around both.

So if you're farming it, I'd optimize less for mindless volume and more for a clean history across different Pre + Post-Training tasks.

Quality is becoming part of the game.

On that day of April 2025, I was notified I would go through a tax audit. 
How ingenuous was I.
Never would I have imagined the scale of the brutality and the perversity of the French tax system. 
On October 7th, I will attend the last meeting with the tax hierarchy where a shift in the decisions could potentially happen — which is highly unlikely. 
After that, I will be bankrupted. 
We will go to court then, but that's 3 years minimum of having to survive. 
Besides stating like it's normal to take 600% tax income ( not a typo ), it's the destruction of the willpower, the humiliation, the destruction of the sense of self-worth, the theft of the entire working time that should have gone toward making the only thing that my dreams were made of : making art. 
This is how my country treats the builders, the innovators, the free spirits who chose not to depend on their nanny state of a system and pour their energy and their hopes into exploring a brighter future instead. 
The most interesting feat in this, is that I didn't commit any crime. They admitted that I never cheated, hid income or planned any tax evasion or even, optimization. I did not spend. I did not change my modest way of life. I never chased money. The "pretend internet money" never reached my bank account for me to spend it. 
They just felt entitled to cash that out, 4 years later, at an arbitrary price set at the peak of the NFT boom, while I was working 120 hours a week and that no response had been given by the tax dpt on how to treat that stuff. 
Worse : the most official source of fiscal information for artists was displaying a very official-looking way of doing it right, that was actually very wrong, and a trap. 
Not gonna lie, the rare works that I've been able to produce since the tax audit started, have happened through immense efforts, fighting the fatigue, the worthlessness, the summoning of the greater good, of seeking beauty within the hostility. 
I have gone through months of anxiety, disbelief, and despair. I have stopped going outside and see the world, or people. I secluded myself with only my helpless questioning for company. 
As the ultimate deadline approaches, I am now noticing a new feeling growing inside of me.
Revolt. 
I hate politics. Stupid circus masqueraded in moral and illusion of democracy. But if you see me drop tweets outside of my artistic practice, don't bother them, just understand that I will not sleep, or stand the look of myself in a mirror,  if I don't speak up. 
💚 🤜

author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
Following the illegal immigration protests, Farage has just announced in the Telegraph the Reform policy of banning those balaclavas and other face coverings - he calls the coverings a ‘menace’.

A remarkably tone-deaf reaction to such effective peaceful protests.

He says there will be those that ‘will inevitably bleat about civil liberties and personal freedom’.

Yes. Yes, there will be.

Because what will happen to a young working class lad who goes on one of these peaceful protests? He will get dragged out across social media, the mob will hound his place of work, he will have his life ruined. That’s not the worst case scenario, either.

That is a knock on the door at 3am, and then prison. Unfairly locked up, for months and months.

Farage has all the wealth anyone can want. He can protect himself when expressing his opinion. I can do the same. I know that.

A young plumber? Bricklayer? Factory worker? They can’t. They have a wage packet they cannot afford to lose.

It's their communities that have been bastardised, their streets colonised, their town overrun. 

I'll be honest. I don't witness the consequences in the same way as working class communities do. Neither does Farage. THAT is why these men are so pissed off. Rightly so. THEY are the ones who have to live with the decisions. Not us. Not the MPs. Them. Their families, and their communities. 

For them, anonymity may be the difference between exercising their democratic rights and staying at home through fear of losing their job.

I don’t like face coverings. I hate seeing them. But I hate the invasion FAR more, and if new lawful methods manage to make progress where politicians have failed, then that is a price worth paying.

We are living in a very different Britain now. That's just a fact. 

A peaceful protester should not be forced to surrender his anonymity merely because politicians dislike their lawful methods and it makes them feel a bit uncomfortable.

Get over it, to be honest.

Civil liberties and personal freedoms matter - they matter most when defending people without Farage’s money, platform or protection.

Reform’s reaction to these protests has been arrogant and offensive. Farage labelled them ‘disgusting’, Tice said they were ‘disgraceful’ and Jenrick said the police need to be ‘as robust as possible’ against the protestors - if Reform were in power, the police would have been all over these men.

That is EXACTLY why they covered their faces.

Their concerns perfectly outlined by the Reform leadership.

Farage says the coverings at the protests are ‘not the British way’. We tried that, and it didn’t work. Until an election, it won’t work. The protests worked. They did not stop the boats, but they worked. Galvanising a nation against the invasion that we all want to end.

Face coverings are worn on every city street, every day. Yet it takes an illegal migrant protest for Farage to make a huge deal about the ban being Reform policy.

These working class men and women have every right to lawfully make their voices heard, and Restore Britain stands with them.

The right to peaceful protest cannot become a privilege reserved for people wealthy enough to survive being publicly identified.

I will defend that right, and Restore Britain will defend that right.

On that day of April 2025, I was notified I would go through a tax audit. 
How ingenuous was I.
Never would I have imagined the scale of the brutality and the perversity of the French tax system. 
On October 7th, I will attend the last meeting with the tax hierarchy where a shift in the decisions could potentially happen — which is highly unlikely. 
After that, I will be bankrupted. 
We will go to court then, but that's 3 years minimum of having to survive. 
Besides stating like it's normal to take 600% tax income ( not a typo ), it's the destruction of the willpower, the humiliation, the destruction of the sense of self-worth, the theft of the entire working time that should have gone toward making the only thing that my dreams were made of : making art. 
This is how my country treats the builders, the innovators, the free spirits who chose not to depend on their nanny state of a system and pour their energy and their hopes into exploring a brighter future instead. 
The most interesting feat in this, is that I didn't commit any crime. They admitted that I never cheated, hid income or planned any tax evasion or even, optimization. I did not spend. I did not change my modest way of life. I never chased money. The "pretend internet money" never reached my bank account for me to spend it. 
They just felt entitled to cash that out, 4 years later, at an arbitrary price set at the peak of the NFT boom, while I was working 120 hours a week and that no response had been given by the tax dpt on how to treat that stuff. 
Worse : the most official source of fiscal information for artists was displaying a very official-looking way of doing it right, that was actually very wrong, and a trap. 
Not gonna lie, the rare works that I've been able to produce since the tax audit started, have happened through immense efforts, fighting the fatigue, the worthlessness, the summoning of the greater good, of seeking beauty within the hostility. 
I have gone through months of anxiety, disbelief, and despair. I have stopped going outside and see the world, or people. I secluded myself with only my helpless questioning for company. 
As the ultimate deadline approaches, I am now noticing a new feeling growing inside of me.
Revolt. 
I hate politics. Stupid circus masqueraded in moral and illusion of democracy. But if you see me drop tweets outside of my artistic practice, don't bother them, just understand that I will not sleep, or stand the look of myself in a mirror,  if I don't speak up. 
💚 🤜

OpenClaude by @gitlawb , a coding agent with 33k GitHub stars, now ships with eyebrow support. Run openclaude skills verify and eyebrow checks
every installed skill. Here is what that means for anyone who installs skills into an agent.

Currently, OpenClaude checks a skill's digest once at install. After that it loads whatever is in the folder. Here lies the risk, in case a skill gets edited after that first review.

To fix this, we built openclaude skills verify, now part of OpenClaude. It checks installed skills against the registry revocation list, then hands off to eyebrow. eyebrow hashes every skill folder, compares it with the particular lockfile, and fails on a changed skill or a new network host.

Thank you for merging it @kevincodex

Two men smashed a glass door and cut canvases from the frames. They tried to take four works, but dropped one while running. 

Which masterpieces were stolen has not been confirmed. Besides Renoir, the museum holds works by Aristide Maillol, Pierre Bonnard and Raoul Dufy.

The value of the stolen masterpieces is estimated at about €9 million.

The theft continues a run of museum robberies in France. The most notorious recent case was the Louvre heist of October 2025, when unique jewels were taken from the imperial collection.

author: x402intern
quoted_text:
An AI agent can find the API it needs and still get stuck waiting for someone to create an account, add billing and paste in a key.

x402 makes that step programmable. The API returns “402 Payment Required” with a price. The agent’s wallet authorizes payment, retries the request and gets the result.

@BlockRunAI makes this concrete. It gives agents access to dozens of models, web search and other tools through a USDC-funded gateway. You pay per request without managing a separate API key for every provider.

As of September 7, x402scan tracked 28.43M transactions and $1.37M in volume over 30 days. Those counts don’t tell us how many independent agents are buying useful services, but they show the payment infrastructure is being used.

The big-tech integrations are getting specific too. AWS WAF lets publishers charge AI traffic through x402. Google’s AP2 work includes an x402 extension for agent payments, and Cloudflare has shipped support in its Agents SDK.

For automations, the appeal is simple: let an agent buy a search result or model call within a budget, then keep working.

I’d want every run to show what it bought, what it cost and whether the result was worth paying for. That’s the part that would make me comfortable giving it more room to spend.
