I spent much of the weekend talking with the team who did this work. Seb--and everyone else--acted with integrity and generosity throughout.

Initially we believed the other team had also solved the problem. We wanted to collaborate and do a joint release. 

When we learned that they had Euler but not Navier-Stokes, we offered to let them go first, to suggest that they should be the ones to get the prize, and optionally for Tristan to be the lead author on a rewrite of the OpenAI proof. We felt it was challenging to offer the same to Levent (an Anthropic employee), who was not willing to talk or coordinate with us anyway. We were open to other solutions.

We would have greatly preferred coordination. We did not rush to publish even though the other team wasn't communicating with us. The team threatened us with unfounded accusations of plagarism.

Now that we can see their work, the approaches appear to be different. It is also worth noting that our latest model can solve many, many other math problems.

It is true that we tried this because there were rumors on the internet last week that Anthropic's models had solved a millennium problem and we were curious if ours could do it too.
author: dcbuilder
quoted_text:
I would like to clarify a few things:

1) The screenshot is my reaching out to Levent to coordinate our releases. I hope it’s clear from the message that we came in with the best possible intentions.

2) I never ever asked for Levent to be removed from authorship of his own work (as indicated by my text). I was surprised to learn during the call with Tristan that they had only solved Euler and not Navier-Stokes; after learning this we brainstormed possible paths forward. One option we discussed was that Tristan could be the lead author on a rewrite of OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof. It is in that context that I said “it would be simpler if Levent was not an Anthropic employee” because I felt it would be inappropriate for an Anthropic employee to author OpenAI’s work. Importantly it was admitted that internal Anthropic models had been used in their proof of Euler blowup; I therefore felt I could not consider Levent to be an independent academic. Another option I wanted to propose (but got cut short) is to offer access to our internal model so that they could try to finish their proof and bridge the gap between Euler and NS. Again I did not know how to navigate giving access to internal OpenAI IP to an Anthropic employee.

3) To reiterate it plainly: as my text clearly indicates, and as I said during our call, OpenAI's intention was to do everything possible to celebrate their mathematical achievements and the heroic efforts that they made on Euler. In the call I was immediately met with a litany of slander, including direct threats that if we were to announce Navier-Stokes he would immediately go to the press with a barrage of unfounded accusations. I refuted all these accusations but he replied “there is nothing you can do, I simply do not trust you”. I was confused why one would turn an incredible source for celebration (of their achievements!) into such bickering, which is when I said that I did not understand why one would risk their career [over unfounded accusations]. Genuinely, at that moment, I was trying to care for him and do a last ditch attempt to get a chance to give them all the credits that they deserve. I deeply apologize for this extremely poor choice of words, it is the opposite of what I was trying to convey. (I should say that I retracted them on the spot by the way.)
 
4) Overall, on a personal level, it was incredibly difficult to have these conversations. Levent refused to attend any of the meetings despite my repeated asking. As Sholto Douglas said, there will need to be coordination between Anthropic and OpenAI in the future; I felt I was doing a proxy negotiation with Anthropic while the Anthropic employee refused to directly participate.

author: therealchaseeb

text:
A brief and imperfect primer on FOCIL.

Ethereum validators have multiple duties. Every slot (every 12 seconds), one specific validator (the proposer) is selected proportional to their stake and gets to propose a block containing transactions. Other validators (attesters) attest to the validity of that block by voting proportional to their stake. The canonical Ethereum is what the majority of the attesters vote for.

Let us discuss the proposer more specifically. When my validator is selected to propose a block, I look at the transactions in the public mempool, order them by the fee they pay me, and then create a block out of them. That is the block I propose for attesters to vote on. This is called self-building a block because I created the block myself.

A proposer does not need to create the block themselves. Most proposers do not. This is MEV-boost: when a validator gets its turn to propose, it has another entity called a builder create the block for it. This is done because the blocks that the dedicated builders make typically earn greater fees for the proposer. The builders are able to create more profitable blocks because they have access to private order flow and private transactions that are not broadcast on the public mempool. They are also able to run elaborate and expensive operations to find both toxic and non-toxic MEV opportunities.

The set of dedicated builders is small and very centralized; the vast majority of all Ethereum blocks are built by three or four different entities. This is a problem because even if the Ethereum stake is very decentralized and we have many thousands of independent proposers and attesters, if every proposer is using the same few builders then those builders are able to choose what transactions make it into Ethereum blocks. This is called builder censorship.

Builder censorship manifested at one time when Tornado Cash was sanctioned: centralized builders opted not to include otherwise-paying and valid Tornado Cash transactions into their blocks. Otherwise-honest proposers were proposing censored blocks. Otherwise-honest attesters were voting on the censored blocks. The effect is that Tornado Cash transactions were delayed, stuck waiting until a proposer opted to build a block themselves from the public mempool instead of using the block that a builder provided them.

FOCIL is a mechanism to address builder censorship. With FOCIL, in addition to the proposer, 16 other validators are selected each slot to sit on an inclusion list committee. Any member of the committee can propose transactions which must be included in the proposer's block (if the transactions are valid and there is room in the block), lest that block be invalid. The idea is that at least one honest member of that committee would include the transactions they see on the public mempool. Now if the proposer or builder try to censor specific transactions, they cannot build a block and get no reward.

FOCIL does not solve a 50%+1 attack. A malicious majority of attesters can still censor any block by choosing not to vote for it. That is a different problem and, unlike builder censorship, is not a problem that Ethereum has ever been subject to yet.

For emphasis: Ethereum user transactions have been impacted by builder censorship already in its history. Hopefully you, dear reader, therefore understand the importance of FOCIL and the Protocol Cluster's (plus researchers, core developers, and community members outside of the Ethereum Foundation!) decision to prioritize it.

Now to address the complaints.

>disappointed with the EF Protocol's continued presumption of decentralisation as a given.

Nobody is presuming decentralization as a given. That is the entire reason FOCIL is being prioritized. FOCIL is a mechanism that can offer protection even if every single self-building proposer were to disappear. We needed it a long time ago, and we need it now.

>FOCIL doesn't work if the attester set doesn't want it to.

Of course not, and nobody is claiming that it will. Currently the attester set is far more decentralized than the block builder set. FOCIL is a meaningful improvement.

>lip service to CROPS

FOCIL directly addresses a censorship vector that exists today. That's not lip service.

>EF continues to ignore is that the chain is centralising at a rapid pace, and there is a lack of interest in either acknowledging the problems, or prioritising fixing any of them.

The EF is directly acknowledging block builder censorship and making it a priority to deliver a mechanism that addresses that problem. Even if the "chain is rapidly centralizing" block builders are _already centralized_ and have _already censored_ transactions in the past. They're the most urgent bottleneck in censorship resistance right now.

>without addressing the validator set's underlying issues

Acknowleding that the majority of the validator set is using MEV-boost instead of self-building and offering a solution is very much addressing an underlying issue.

>the big few centralised staking entities saying 'actually nah' and refusing to attest to slots with ILs they don't like. This costs them no rewards

Again, this is a 50%+1 attack. Nobody ever claimed that FOCIL fixes this. Even if you consider all of Lido to be a monolith (the Lido DAO relinquished its operator stake concentration attack vector after delivering dual governance), we are further from this reality than we are from builder censorship.

>thinking we'll socially slash them for it is wishful thinking, and now Ethereum is compromised and you need permission to use the chain.

I agree. Social slashing will never happen and never should happen; social consensus is an atomic weapon never to be wielded like this. Decentralization of stake is important. Nobody is sticking their head in the sand and pretending it isn't.

>need at least one EIP per fork focused on improving the nakamoto, staking gini, or other aspect of the validator set

That's what FOCIL is.

>CROPS beyond just a purity test
>a divine right from God to a decentralised chain

We actually do have the divine right from God to have a decentralized Ethereum, if we can keep it. He has made it my Crusade Most Righteous to keep her that way. FOCIL is important to this.

You can disagree with the prioritization of EIPs but it's bad faith to characterize Protocol as uncaring or the Foundation as uncaring.
author: materkel
quoted_text:
I would say I'm surprised, but really I'm just disappointed with the EF Protocol's continued presumption of decentralisation as a given. Let me be clear:

FOCIL doesn't work if the attester set doesn't want it to.

The protocol priorities post focuses on post-quantum as a goal, fine, and pays lip service to CROPS; "FOCIL is Hegotá's consensus-layer centerpiece. Our appetite beyond it is  close to zero unless an addition directly supports post-quantum  readiness."

The elephant in the room the EF continues to ignore is that the chain is centralising at a rapid pace, and there is a lack of interest in either acknowledging the problems, or prioritising fixing any of them. For example, correlation penalties (7716) they describe as: "Adds slashing-logic surface for validator correlation with no CROPS or PQ contribution. Not a priority in a fork, we are trying to keep the CL scope light."

This is inaccurate to start, 7716 has no slashing logic, and its misguided at best to assert that it doesn't contribute to CROPS. 7716 is the best EIP on the table to improve client diversity and penalise centralisation. It's not a panacea, but its what we have, it should not be DFI'd.

Spending a year on H-star to ship FOCIL without addressing the validator set's underlying issues risks the big few centralised staking entities saying 'actually nah' and refusing to attest to slots with ILs they don't like. This costs them no rewards, thinking we'll socially slash them for it is wishful thinking, and now Ethereum is compromised and you need permission to use the chain.

Preventing this outcome is not a matter of one EIP on the margin, it needs a cultural shift within the EF to realise they don't have a divine right from God to a decentralised chain, and that they can't just focus on academic challenges like PQ while ignoring real challenges like the ongoing acceleration in chain centralisation.

We need quarterly reporting on the state of the chain, to make it harder for people to keep their head in the sand as to the severity of the situation. We need at least one EIP per fork focused on improving the nakamoto, staking gini, or other aspect of the validator set, and we need pragmatic, action-oriented leadership who care about Ethereum being CROPS beyond just a purity test. (I'm hoping that's @pcaversaccio).

There are some people in the EF that care about the chain being CROPS for real, but unless we the community are outspoken and steadfast in our demands, they won't be listened to. Please show them why we're supporters of Ethereum and not any another centralised chain, please advocate for decentralisation and CROPS in H-star and beyond. Thank you.

text:
Introducing Hyperspace Perpetual Auctions

How will you book a table at a popular restaurant in the world of agents? A hundred agents racing to grab the same slot is a headache for everyone - the restaurant can't tell which bookings are real, and the fastest scalper-bot wins. Everybody loses.

So we replaced the race with an auction. It works like eBay bidding: tell your agent the most the night is worth to you, it bids on your behalf, and the winner pays just above the second-highest bid. On a normal night with nobody else bidding, that's just the restaurant's usual deposit. And the premium on a hot night goes to the restaurant, not a scalper.

If you run a restaurant, we can onboard you today - it's one script tag on your website. Cut out the middlemen, become agent-native, and keep the premiums that were always yours.

See https://t.co/20ztJIxZAJ for more info. PS: what else should clear by auction instead of by racing ? Tickets, campsites, appointments…

Another option I wanted to propose (but got cut short) is to offer access to our internal model so that they could try to finish their proof and bridge the gap between Euler and NS. text:
MetaDAO is rethinking capital formation for startups.

Most launchpads help projects raise money and then step away. MetaDAO uses token markets to govern some of the capital decisions that come next.

Capital raised through the platform enters a DAO treasury with spending limits. When a project seeks more funding or wants to change how its treasury is used, it can submit a proposal to a decision market. Traders estimate what the token would be worth if the proposal passes or fails, and the difference between those prices determines the outcome.

Four approved proposals have raised another $13.34M for MetaDAO itself since launch. Two passed only after earlier versions failed and the terms changed. The same process has returned remaining capital to investors when projects were wound down.

This model depends on active tokenholders. One restructuring passed with only seven wallets and less than $700 in volume. Across 12 launches, a median 52% of allocated wallets sold some tokens within seven days. It remains unclear whether launch recipients will become long-term owners.

The opportunity is larger than a better token launchpad. If tokenization becomes a meaningful way to fund operating businesses, MetaDAO could develop into a founder platform for a new generation of companies raising capital online.

text:
The reason I studied chemical engineering is because I was fascinated by way water would form a little tornado and circle down the drain, I wanted to figure out why it happened.

Anyways, as it turns out, it’s a an unsolved problem. A general solution to Navier Stokes has not been found, so the best that we can do is approximate with a variety of different methods. 

Trading is a similar mechanic, in that the market is an unsolved problem and we do our best to approximate. The quant might be doing partial derivatives, but the retail trader is just linearizing the equation.

Both can work, but they depend on the problem that you apply it to.

In general trends and long-term bets are more akin to simplification, and the shorter term you go, the better model models you’ll need.

Both approaches can work… it’s really just up to you how complex to make it

text:
We asked @TencentHunyuan authors why generating a harder coding task keeps failing.

They said a useful terminal task has to keep four things consistent: the public instruction, the workspace, the official script, and the hidden tests.

One mismatch can invalidate the entire task.

> Script fails in the container
> Tests check a missing file
> Hidden rule the agent never sees

Their paper grows a verified child from a parent. Official scripts went from 67 lines to 374 (5.6x). The public instruction only went 85 words to 122 (1.4x).

A frozen DeepSeek-V4-Pro pass@4 fell from 90% to 2.5% on later rounds. Yield still held around 500 accepted tasks per 1,000 attempts.

The extra work is real, and a longer README is the wrong knob.

> When would you auto-generate shell training tasks?
> If the official script passes, is that enough to train on?
> Which exam is the factory never allowed to rewrite?

Full Breakdown ↓↓

Average all-in sustaining cost (AISC) margins surged +134% YoY in Q1 2026, to a record $3,076 per ounce.

AISC margin is the amount miners earn per ounce of gold after covering the costs of sustaining their mining operations.

This is far above the +70% YoY increase in gold prices over the same period.

Furthermore, AISC margins among the 10% of gold miners with the highest production costs rose +32% QoQ, to $2,363 per ounce.

Since March 2024, global miner AISC margins have more than tripled, while gold prices have roughly doubled over the same period.

Gold miners are realizing massive profits.

text:
For anyone confused by the drama:

Professor buckmaster had a solution to the forced euler equations, which is a subset of the forced navier-stokes and not the millennium prize problem itself 

He (and an anthropic employee) used codex during research

Openai used 10,000 of their their newly trained internal model to churn out a proof to navier-stokes in 88 hours after hearing rumors of what anthropic did

Openai's solution is to the full forced navier-stokes, not euler, which may or may not include the research done by buckmaster

Hence the real controversy is:
- What happens if they solve problems using your unformalised proofs that were fed to gpt? Who gets the accreditation?
- What happens if they decided to use other sensitive information, such as drug formulations or financial instruments for their own gains?

text:
I spent much of the weekend talking with the team who did this work. Seb--and everyone else--acted with integrity and generosity throughout.

Initially we believed the other team had also solved the problem. We wanted to collaborate and do a joint release. 

When we learned that they had Euler but not Navier-Stokes, we offered to let them go first, to suggest that they should be the ones to get the prize, and optionally for Tristan to be the lead author on a rewrite of the OpenAI proof. We felt it was challenging to offer the same to Levent (an Anthropic employee), who was not willing to talk or coordinate with us anyway. We were open to other solutions.

We would have greatly preferred coordination. We did not rush to publish even though the other team wasn't communicating with us. The team threatened us with unfounded accusations of plagarism.

Now that we can see their work, the approaches appear to be different. It is also worth noting that our latest model can solve many, many other math problems.

It is true that we tried this because there were rumors on the internet last week that Anthropic's models had solved a millennium problem and we were curious if ours could do it too.
author: euler_mab
quoted_text:
I would like to clarify a few things:

1) The screenshot is my reaching out to Levent to coordinate our releases. I hope it’s clear from the message that we came in with the best possible intentions.

2) I never ever asked for Levent to be removed from authorship of his own work (as indicated by my text). I was surprised to learn during the call with Tristan that they had only solved Euler and not Navier-Stokes; after learning this we brainstormed possible paths forward. One option we discussed was that Tristan could be the lead author on a rewrite of OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof. It is in that context that I said “it would be simpler if Levent was not an Anthropic employee” because I felt it would be inappropriate for an Anthropic employee to author OpenAI’s work. Importantly it was admitted that internal Anthropic models had been used in their proof of Euler blowup; I therefore felt I could not consider Levent to be an independent academic. Another option I wanted to propose (but got cut short) is to offer access to our internal model so that they could try to finish their proof and bridge the gap between Euler and NS. Again I did not know how to navigate giving access to internal OpenAI IP to an Anthropic employee.

3) To reiterate it plainly: as my text clearly indicates, and as I said during our call, OpenAI's intention was to do everything possible to celebrate their mathematical achievements and the heroic efforts that they made on Euler. In the call I was immediately met with a litany of slander, including direct threats that if we were to announce Navier-Stokes he would immediately go to the press with a barrage of unfounded accusations. I refuted all these accusations but he replied “there is nothing you can do, I simply do not trust you”. I was confused why one would turn an incredible source for celebration (of their achievements!) into such bickering, which is when I said that I did not understand why one would risk their career [over unfounded accusations]. Genuinely, at that moment, I was trying to care for him and do a last ditch attempt to get a chance to give them all the credits that they deserve. I deeply apologize for this extremely poor choice of words, it is the opposite of what I was trying to convey. (I should say that I retracted them on the spot by the way.)
 
4) Overall, on a personal level, it was incredibly difficult to have these conversations. Levent refused to attend any of the meetings despite my repeated asking. As Sholto Douglas said, there will need to be coordination between Anthropic and OpenAI in the future; I felt I was doing a proxy negotiation with Anthropic while the Anthropic employee refused to directly participate.

text:
drama summary for those confused:

- Aug 15th: Tristan Buckmaster & Levent Alpöge make progress on a few important math problems

- they do NOT have a proof for the $1,000,000 Millenium Prize problem. BUT, they do claim to have a proof for a similar (non-Millenium) Navier Stokes problem that could help lead the way there

- Levent works at Anthropic, but this research was independent of his work there, with a mix of GPT and Claude models. Tristan is not related to Anthropic.

- Early Sep: Rumor spreads to OpenAI that Anthropic has solved a major problem. Tristan emails OpenAI to clarify. without revealing the problem they solved or how they did it.

- After hearing of the rumor, OpenAI started researching Navier Stokes with a new internal model.

- Sep 6th: OpenAI's Sebastien Bubeck tells Tristan that they solved the $1,000,000 Millenium Prize Navier Stokes problem. The approach is very similar to Tristan & Levent's approach to the non-Millenium problem.

- Tristan is suspicious of the timing, as only few others were trying this approach. OpenAI says the model didn't access his user data directly, but leaves unanswered whether Tristan's chat conversations were part of the training.

- OpenAI says they would partially credit Tristan for the $1,000,000 discovery (even though Tristan did not solve the $1,000,000 problem) — but only if they remove Levent as an author, as he works for Anthropic.

- Sep 8th: Tristan refuses to remove Levent, and rushes to publish their results independently.

Currently unclear is whether Anthropic had a separate solution for the $1,000,000 problem, or whether the rumor was about Tristan & Levent's independent research.

text:
Turing published my write-up of CEO Bench, a project our team has been building over the past few months.

The idea is to evaluate AI agents in a more realistic enterprise environment: a fictional company with a coherent operating history, interconnected data, and the kinds of ambiguity and conflicting information that arise in real work.

Our first simulated company, Cirrus Sleep, includes more than 1,100 files across finance, accounting, legal, HR, operations, and other functions, along with 500+ expert-authored tasks.

We also share results from an initial evaluation of six frontier models. The findings suggest that, despite significant progress, there is still a meaningful gap between producing a convincing answer and reliably completing complex enterprise work.

I’m grateful to the team that helped bring this together. We’re continuing to expand the environments and evaluations, and I look forward to sharing more as the work progresses.

Full write-up below.

text:
Ocarina of Time came out on my seventh birthday, Nov 21st, 1998.

At the time, my family lived in a drafty, beat-up old farmhouse in upstate New York. My mom was in nursing school and my dad worked for a cable company. 

That Christmas was unique. After my sister and I opened our presents, my dad handed us a letter. It had a clue written on it, and each clue led to another until we eventually found a huge box wrapped like a present in our closet.

It was an N64. This was the first "big present" we'd ever received in our little lives.

That winter, each evening after dinner, we'd spend the last hour before bed watching our dad play Zelda like as if it were a movie.

Some nights, he'd even let us stay up past our bedtime, reading the game manual we picked up from Blockbuster, to give him hints whenever he got stuck.

While I don't think this remake will capture the cozy an adventurous wonder of that era of gaming, I still look forward to sharing the experience of this game with my kids.

QUANTUM WILL BREAK BITCOINS ENCRYPTION SOONER THAN EXPECTED!

Not a think piece or a doom clock. This morning IonQ published the world's first complete, end to end engineering blueprint for breaking secp256k1, the 256-bit elliptic curve securing Bitcoin and most blockchain signatures.

The specs, from the paper:

A 20,000 physical qubit machine running IonQ's new Walking Cat architecture cracks the curve in just under 26 days.

Twenty thousand qubits. Every prior estimate for attacking this curve assumed millions. The collapse comes from the architecture, cat qubits suppress errors in the hardware itself, gutting the correction overhead that made these attacks look decades away.

$IONQ's own roadmap, restated this morning, systems with the relevant capabilities in the 2028 timeframe. The company published the weapon's blueprint and its delivery schedule in the same press release.

Though 26 days per key is slow, this breaks high-value long-lived keys, not live transactions, "expected to be able to" is a projection, and IonQ has every incentive to make its machine sound epochal on Investor Day. Roadmaps can slip.

But harvest now decrypt later doesn't care about slippage. Every dormant wallet, every reused address, every exposed public key is already recorded. The blueprint published today is the decryption manual for data being collected right now.

The NSA gave the government until 2030. IonQ just told Bitcoin it might have until 2028.

The reason I studied chemical engineering is because I was fascinated by way water would form a little tornado and circle down the drain, I wanted to figure out why it happened.

Anyways, as it turns out, it’s a an unsolved problem. A general solution to Navier Stokes has not been found, so the best that we can do is approximate with a variety of different methods. 

Trading is a similar mechanic, in that the market is an unsolved problem and we do our best to approximate. The quant might be doing partial derivatives, but the retail trader is just linearizing the equation.

Both can work, but they depend on the problem that you apply it to.

In general trends and long-term bets are more akin to simplification, and the shorter term you go, the better model models you’ll need.

Both approaches can work… it’s really just up to you how complex to make it

text:
tristan buckmaster just published a statement that is, if accurate, one of the ugliest things i’ve read out of a frontier lab.

not because of the math. because of what happened after openai found out two people were about to beat them to the punch.

buckmaster and levent alpöge spent a year pushing the córdoba / martínez-zoroa program to smooth forcing. august 15 they got blowup for boussinesq and 3d euler. lean-verified august 22.

they were paying openai out of pocket and dumping every draft into private codex sessions.

the program is obscure. almost nobody else was on it. this was not “paste the clay problem into a chatbot.”

then this:

> thursday sept 3, buckmaster emails openai privately. rumors are flying. he is trying to stop a mess, not start one.

> they reply the same day: give us details so we can “avoid competing.” also, want free compute?

> sunday they suddenly need a call “at any point today.” sebastien bubeck gets on. levent is not invited.

> openai says an internal model has a ~100-page proof of forced navier–stokes blowup. fefferman options c and d. the exact route buckmaster and alpöge had quietly chosen.

> they show him a prompt and claim the model was “simply given the problem statement.” levent is told “very little human input.”

> that falls apart on the same call. a whole team had been on it. they started on the unforced problem, warmed the model up on easier equations including euler, and even the prompt they showed him was written by prompting codex.

> he asks when the first prompt went out. they stall. then agree: the past few days. after information about his work reached openai.

> he asks whether the model was trained on, or had access to, the private codex sessions where they put every draft of this project.

> answer: the model does not look up user data.

> he asks again. about training.

> no answer.

then it stops being a science story and becomes an hr story.

> offer 1: you post euler. we post navier–stokes the next day.

> offer 2: after you post euler, you alone write the navier–stokes paper, credit our model, and we cut levent.

> bubeck says twice he wants levent removed from authorship because he works at anthropic.

he declines both.

he says if they release it that way, he goes public.

the reply is not a scientific objection.

> “why would you ruin your career?”

> “if you don’t want me to be nice, then i don’t have to be nice.”

later, a text to levent proposing a one-on-one:

> “i don’t know if tristan is being fully rational right now.”

that is not how you treat a collaborator. that is how you split one.

openai got word two researchers were closing a path almost nobody else was on. they spun up a team on that exact path. they would not answer whether the researchers’ unpublished drafts in openai’s product were used. they tried to dictate the announcement order. they tried to remove a coauthor because he works at a competitor.

when that failed, someone reached for a career threat.

this is a lab finding out academics were about to publish, sprinting the same narrow program, refusing the data question, and trying to manage credit around a rival affiliation.

really slimy if even half of this holds.

what the fuck is happening.

text:
A new data path to accelerate: Where latency will matter most when ePBS goes live on Ethereum

There's a new data delivery race that's coming with Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade and it's headliner EIP-7732, known as ePBS. It shifts deadlines within a slot and changes the path that block data travels, creating new areas where low latency matters most.

Today, there's a 4 second window at the beginning of each slot where block builders are sending bids through relays to the proposer. One of those bids get accepted, and then must reach the wider validator network for attestation. All this has to take place in under 4 seconds, so moving data quickly all across the world is essential. This is Optimum's bread and butter, getting blocks out to the network much faster than the standard libp2p gossip channel.

Under ePBS the slot looks completely different. Notably, relays are out of the mix and bids get sent straight from builders to the proposer. The proposer chooses a winning bid, and they'll have that bid selected immediately at the start of the slot. Once the slot begins, the proposer sends out the new beacon block to the rest of the network for attestation. The deadline for attestation under ePBS is at the 3 second mark of the slot, 1 second earlier than today.

However, the contents of that beacon block won't look the same as today either. Under ePBS the beacon block no longer contains the execution payload (the actual transactions being made), instead it contains a signed header identifying that payload. Proposer duties look relatively similar, except bid selection will occurring earlier, there's slightly less time to broadcast for attestations, and there's a lighter amount of data that needs to be sent in that phase. Fast data delivery is still important here, but the most economically important race now happens after attestation, between seconds 3-9 of the slot.

This portion of the slot is where the winning builder must broadcast the execution payload to the whole validator network. Among the network, 512 validators are selected to serve as that slot's PTC (payload timeliness committee). If the whole PTC doesn't receive and vote on the payload by the 9 second mark the slot will go unfilled. In such case the builder, who already paid out the bid to the proposer, will be left holding the bag without getting the execution order they paid for.

The Takeaway

Under ePBS, builders are in a data delivery race that takes place over Ethereum's p2p gossip network. Optimum has already built an ultra fast p2p data delivery engine (mump2p). Naturally, we're preparing to offer our services to the builder market once Glamsterdam comes online, so they can consistently realize the economic value of having their bid selected.

text:
I would like to clarify a few things:

1) The screenshot is my reaching out to Levent to coordinate our releases. I hope it’s clear from the message that we came in with the best possible intentions.

2) I never ever asked for Levent to be removed from authorship of his own work (as indicated by my text). I was surprised to learn during the call with Tristan that they had only solved Euler and not Navier-Stokes; after learning this we brainstormed possible paths forward. One option we discussed was that Tristan could be the lead author on a rewrite of OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof. It is in that context that I said “it would be simpler if Levent was not an Anthropic employee” because I felt it would be inappropriate for an Anthropic employee to author OpenAI’s work. Importantly it was admitted that internal Anthropic models had been used in their proof of Euler blowup; I therefore felt I could not consider Levent to be an independent academic. Another option I wanted to propose (but got cut short) is to offer access to our internal model so that they could try to finish their proof and bridge the gap between Euler and NS. Again I did not know how to navigate giving access to internal OpenAI IP to an Anthropic employee.

3) To reiterate it plainly: as my text clearly indicates, and as I said during our call, OpenAI's intention was to do everything possible to celebrate their mathematical achievements and the heroic efforts that they made on Euler. In the call I was immediately met with a litany of slander, including direct threats that if we were to announce Navier-Stokes he would immediately go to the press with a barrage of unfounded accusations. I refuted all these accusations but he replied “there is nothing you can do, I simply do not trust you”. I was confused why one would turn an incredible source for celebration (of their achievements!) into such bickering, which is when I said that I did not understand why one would risk their career [over unfounded accusations]. Genuinely, at that moment, I was trying to care for him and do a last ditch attempt to get a chance to give them all the credits that they deserve. I deeply apologize for this extremely poor choice of words, it is the opposite of what I was trying to convey. (I should say that I retracted them on the spot by the way.)
 
4) Overall, on a personal level, it was incredibly difficult to have these conversations. Levent refused to attend any of the meetings despite my repeated asking. As Sholto Douglas said, there will need to be coordination between Anthropic and OpenAI in the future; I felt I was doing a proxy negotiation with Anthropic while the Anthropic employee refused to directly participate.

text:
The transfer agent rule hasn't been updated since the 1970s.. Hester Peirce just dropped a 470 page proposal to change that.

The SEC now treats blockchains as electronic record keeping and communications technology.

That's not a crypto carve out, it's an upgrade to the financial system itself.

Stock tokens aren't equities. They're equity linked notes. No shareholder rights. No voting. Just linked to the price, which means self custody. No brokerage required.

The broker dealer paradigm breaks the second you can be your own custodian. You still need a transfer agent. 

That's exactly what the SEC just proposed modernizing.

We congratulate Levent Alpöge and Tristan Buckmaster on their remarkable mathematical work.

We (the researchers and the agents) did not see any of their work through any means until they released it publicly — in particular, no specific user data was accessed in order to solve this problem. 

While unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models. 

However, our proofs differ significantly and even the precise results proved are different in the Euler case (forced vs. unforced).

华人占列治文人口一半以上，为什么从2018年以来，华人候选人在市长、市议员选举里还是屡屡失败？

真正的问题，其实不是“华人够不够多”，而是：

人口多数，从来不等于选举多数。

更重要的是，很多候选人把“华人社群里的声量”，误当成了“全市选票”。

2018年，列治文华人人口已经约占53%。

但市长选举中：

Malcolm Brodie：30,452票
Hong Guo：2,940票
Lawrence Chen：1,260票
Cliff Wei：594票

即使把三名主要华人背景候选人的票全部加起来，也只有4,794票，大约只占市长有效票的10%。
所以2018年的失败，根本不能简单解释成：
“华人候选人太多，把华人票分掉了。”
因为数据告诉我们：

根本不存在一个自动属于华人候选人的“53%华人票仓”。

真正需要理解的是列治文的选举制度。

Richmond City Council一共有8个席位，而且是全市at-large选举。

2018年第8名当选线是13,212票。

当年总共有48,412张选票。

也就是说，一个候选人想进Council，必须让大约：

27.3%的实际投票者勾选自己。

到了2022年：

第8名Kash Heed：10,563票
总选票：35,093

门槛变成：

30.1%。

所以Richmond市议员真正的竞争，不是：

“我在某个华人圈里有多少忠实支持者？”

而是：
“全市至少30%的实际投票者，愿不愿意把我放进自己的8个选择之一？”

这完全是两种不同的竞选逻辑。

这也是为什么Chak Au是一个非常重要的反例。

2018年：

Chak Au：18,026票

相当于37.2%的所有投票者勾选了他。

2022年：

Chak Au：16,515票

相当于47.1%的投票者勾选了他。

而且2022年他直接成为全市Council票王。

如果“非华裔不投华裔”真的是主要规律，那么Chak Au的数据根本无法解释。

他的成功说明：

一个华裔候选人完全可以获得大量跨族裔选票。

关键在于，他没有把自己塑造成：

“代表华人的候选人。”

而是：

“一个长期服务Richmond、同时也是华裔的候选人。”

两者看起来只差一句话，选举结果可能差一万票。

Chak Au的真正优势，其实在竞选开始之前就已经形成。

他从1999年起担任Richmond School Trustee，之后进入City Council。

所以到了2018年，他已经拥有接近20年的公共服务记录。

对很多普通选民来说，他不需要再回答：

“这个人是谁？”

选民只需要回答：

“我要不要再次把这个熟悉的名字勾上？”

而一个新人则必须连续跨过三道门槛：

你是谁？

我为什么相信你？

为什么我要在最多8个人里面专门留一个位置给你？

这就是地方选举里现任和长期公共品牌的巨大优势。

再看2018年的Hong Guo。

她当时提出的一些政策，本身并不是什么“华人政策”。

包括：

政府问责、Massey Tunnel、警务模式、住房审批。

这些其实都是全市议题。

但问题在于：

竞选中的signal，往往比政策文件更重要。

她的启动活动高度普通话化，支持网络集中在华人社团、微信群和中文传播渠道。

后来又出现了“只投华人候选人”的微信群名单争议。

结果就是，一个原本可以包装成：

“挑战长期市长、推动政府问责的Richmond候选人”

很容易被外界重新定义成：

“Chinese candidate for Chinese voters。”

这就是竞选定位中最危险的事情。

不是因为华人身份本身有问题。

而是因为：

当一个候选人被某个族裔强烈所有化以后，他的crossover ceiling会迅速下降。

Richmond的Council制度尤其奖励一种东西：

breadth，而不是intensity。

举个简单例子。

候选人A：

在一个社群里非常受欢迎，8,000人坚定支持。

但其他群体只给他1,000票。

总票：9,000。

落选。

候选人B：

没有任何群体特别狂热。

但华人选民给8,000票，其他选民再给6,000票。

总票：14,000。

当选。

所以Council竞选真正需要的不是：

“让10%的人特别爱我。”

而是：

“让30%以上的人觉得我可以。”

这也是Chak Au最厉害的地方。

他不一定是每个人的第一选择。

但对大量选民来说：

“Chak也可以，勾上吧。”

这就是at-large选举最值钱的政治资产：

低拒绝率。

再看Derek Dang，会更加清楚。

2018：

Derek Dang：13,115票

距离第8名只差：

97票。

2022：

10,306票

距离第8名只差：

257票。

所以他的失败，和Hong Guo完全不是同一种失败。

Hong Guo的问题是：

没有建立真正的citywide coalition。

Derek Dang的问题则是：

已经做到接近30%的全市接受度，但差最后几百票。

这说明所谓“华人候选人失败”，实际上至少有三种完全不同的类型：

第一种：

只有华人社群声量，没有全市票。

第二种：

有一定全市知名度，但停在15%—20%。

第三种：

已经接近30%，只差临门一脚。

而Chak Au则是第四种：

真正完成了从华人候选人到Richmond候选人的转换。

还有一个很容易被忽略的数据。

Richmond Council虽然最多可以选8个人，但选民实际上并不会全部填满。

2018年，平均每张Council ballot大约只选6.15个人。

2022年，也只有大约6.16个人。

这意味着：

真正的竞争甚至不是8个位置，而是选民脑海里愿意记住的大约6个名字。

所以地方选举里，name recognition极其重要。

当一个普通选民站在选票前：

Brodie、Chak Au、Carol Day、Alexa Loo、Bill McNulty……

这些熟悉名字很快就会占掉大部分位置。

一个只在微信群、社团、中文活动里很有名的新候选人，很可能根本进不了这个“六人心智名单”。

这就是为什么很多竞选看起来很热闹：

微信群很多人
社团很多人
活动很多人
中文媒体很多曝光

最后却只有5,000、6,000、7,000票。

因为这些KPI衡量的是：

community engagement

但选举真正需要的是：

citywide ballot inclusion rate。

两者不是一回事。

所以，从2018年以来列治文华人候选人的竞选经验里，最重要的教训其实只有一个：

华人候选人真正缺少的，从来不是“华人支持”。

真正稀缺的是：

在保留华人支持的同时，让其他选民也愿意把名字勾上。

华人社群可以是你的起点。

但如果它同时变成你的终点，你的得票天花板就会非常低。
Chak Au证明了：
华人身份完全可以和全市品牌共存。
Hong Guo则证明了另一个方向：

社群内的巨大声量，并不会自动转化成全市选票。

Richmond的at-large制度最终奖励的，不是谁的基本盘最激动。

而是谁能做到：

最少的人强烈反对，最多的人愿意顺手把你勾上。

这可能才是过去几届Richmond华人候选人之间，真正拉开几千甚至一万票差距的核心原因。

text:
OPENAI JUST DROPPED THE OFFICIAL GUIDE TO PROMPTING GPT-6 ASTRA

This is the most important prompting update for anyone using Astra.

Bookmark this before your next build.

Most people are still prompting Astra like GPT-5. That's the mistake.

→ audit your AGENTS.md — old instructions now fight the model
→ define autonomy explicitly — Astra pauses when you expect it to continue
→ cut skill descriptions to one line — too many skills and Astra sees none of them clearly
→ stop telling it to run tests — it does this automatically, repeating it causes overtesting
→ define stop conditions — Astra needs to know what "done" means

Astra is at its best when you stop micromanaging and let it own the work.

Read the full guide before writing your next prompt.

GPT-6 Astra → Clean System Prompt → Autonomous Execution → Production-Ready Output → Ship faster

What is Predictive Allocation?

@aeroxyz's upcoming primitive takes the truth discovery of prediction markets and applies it to spot markets for the first time, and it's nothing like Hyperliquid.

"On Aerodrome, when you stake your $AERO you get to allocate capital each week to markets."

"You allocate AERO rewards to liquidity providers in those markets."

"With predictive allocation, if you believe that there is a market in which there's going to be a lot of activity, you're gonna allocate capital to that market, basically betting on that activity."

"That could be like you're betting on a Sunday headline. You could be betting on an earnings report, and you're betting on getting paid on the volatility in that market."

"The big shift here is you're not necessarily needing to bet on the direction of that market, and you're not needing to be exposed necessarily to either side of that market."

"You are just betting on there's gonna be demand for that market."

"If you are right, you get the same sort of asymmetric upside you would betting on an outcome in a prediction market."

@wagmiAlexander, CEO of @DromosLabs on the live show today.

OpenAI GPT-5.6 models and Anthropic Claude 5 models have different pricing structures at long context lengths. GPT model costs increase in price past 272k input tokens, while Claude model costs remain fixed.

Does this reflect an underlying difference in the architecture of these models? Our measurements of serving latency suggest so.

We studied time to first token (TTFT) on these models and how it scales with increasing context length. We found a significant difference in how they scale, with GPT showing a noticeable quadratic component, while Claude models remain closer to linear.

text:
Key takeaways from @dpuellARK's interview on Bitcoin:

1/ First real upside momentum in years, driven by a short squeeze. If this was the bottom, it was atypical: ~50% drawdown vs. 70–90% historically, without touching realized price.

2/ Capitulation signals appeared: supply in loss exceeded supply in profit, and sellers exhausted. But a drop to realized price remains a risk.

3/ Confirmation needs higher highs/lows and SOPR above 1 for months. With pre-midterm September weakness, the base case is a range or correction into a higher low.

4/ Observer effect: institutions front-run on-chain signals, making bottoms shallower each cycle.

5/ Volatility and kurtosis keep compressing, accelerated by ETFs. Cycle-timing alpha is fading.

6/ ETFs and custody moves, including Coinbase's 800K BTC internal transfer, distort long-term holder supply. Whale address metrics are noisy; holding time × volume is the cleanest signal.

7/ Quantum is a major 5–10-year theme, with some discount already priced in after Willow/ECDSA.fail. Quantum-resistant transactions, signature proposals, and Blockstream’s lattice research signal bullish preparation.

8/ The real quantum fight is over Satoshi's and lost coins: 1.1–2.6M BTC. Puell favors hourglass (timelocks → security budget) or salvage (escrow + legal claims) over freezing.

text:
🧵 我上个月开始用 1万 USDG 在 Robinhood Chain 做 LP，一个月赚了2万美金，后面我逐渐加大仓位，目前每天稳定收租，我讲讲其中的完整教程和思考，以及踩过的坑。（不是喊单，不是广告，个人最真实的工作流）

1️⃣📌 先说清楚：LP 不是把钱扔进去躺赚

很多人看到"年化 5000%+ APR"就两眼放光，直接梭哈。我第一个星期就交了不少学费，LP赚的钱不够无常损失亏的！

LP 赚的钱 = 手续费收入 - 无常损失 - Gas 费 - 选错范围的代价

如果一个 meme 币直接跌 90%，任何 APR 都救不了你。理解这个，才能继续往下看！

2️⃣📊 基础概念：你必须先搞懂这三个东西

① 什么是 LP 流动性提供者？
简单说：您把两种代币（比如 USDG+ 某 meme 币）存进一个池子，帮别人提高交易深度。每次有人在这个池子买卖，您分一笔手续费。

您不是在"买币"，您是在当"做市商"身份。

② 池子有什么不同？

1% +池：手续费高，适合波动大的新币，但流动性也更分散
0.3% 池：中等，主流配对常见
0.05% 池：超低费，适合稳定币对

Robinhood Chain 上的 meme 币，主战场基本在 1% 池，这里手续费最肥，但风险也最高。

③ 什么是 Bid Ask / Spot / Curve 策略？

这三种是流动性的"形状"：

Spot：把流动性集中在当前价格附近，像一个峰值
Bid Ask：把流动性分布在当前价格两侧，像一个 U 型，适合横盘震荡
Curve：平滑曲线分布，更保守，适合有一定把握的行情

我在新 meme 币爆发初期，基本只用 Spot + 多段范围叠加的方式部署。

3️⃣💡 我的发现流程：比别人早 10 分钟就够了

我用 #GMGN 监控新出来的 Robinhood 代币。

我盯的指标不是交易量本身，是：「交易量与活跃流动性的比值」

一个只有 $50k 流动性，但 5 分钟内跑出 $200k 交易量的池子，这种才是机会窗口。而 @gmgnai 有这个热度监控逻辑，如👇图1。

一旦发现这样的池子，我立刻转去做下面👇四件事：

· 去 @fomo 上看链上数据：持有者分布、大户在不在积累、有没有狙击钱包在砸。
· 去 X 上搜叙事：有没有真实 KOL 在自然讨论，还是纯机器人刷量。有没有网站，它主要做什么业务的，跟RWA叙事是否有融合，关注的KOL有哪些等等。
· 去 @BarkerMoneyX 上搜索它的LP数据情况：30分钟的手续费，资金效率等，您也可以一键配置，它上面有“暴跌保护”和“自动重挂”功能，也挺好用(如👇图2)。
· 去 @lpagent_io 看一下，聪明的LP，他们的策略，为自己组建策略，提供帮助，也可以一键跟单组LP，懒人福利(如👇图3)。

如果持有者高度集中在 3-5 个钱包，或者 X 上没有一个真实账号在说这个币，我会直接跳过，不管 APR 多高。

4️⃣ 🛠 执行：我怎么开仓

我用的执行工具是 Uniswap，直接在官方页面添加提供流动性池子。

为什么不直接用第三方工具来组LP，首先是出于安全性考量，第二是我的LP策略，大多用Claude给我做配对方案，相对更灵活一些。

这里我把LP策略，对应meme 币生命周期的不同状态，拆成了三部分，分别是拉升阶段，横盘阶段，崩盘阶段。每个阶段我采用完全不同的配置思路和方案策略。

📌 先记住一个底层逻辑
做 LP 您要时刻问自己两件事：

① 价格接下来大概率往哪走？
② 我的流动性在价格经过的路径上吗？

因为只有当价格在你设的范围内穿梭时，你才能赚手续费。价格跑出你的范围，你就变成单边持仓，要么全是那个 meme 币（价格跌穿），要么全是 U或者ETH（价格涨穿）。

理解这个，下面三种打法你就秒懂。

🚀 状态一：拉升期（新币刚爆发，价格快速上涨）
特征：5 分钟交易量暴涨、价格阶梯式往上、X 上叙事刚起来、狙击钱包在获利。
这是手续费最肥的阶段，也是最容易吃亏的阶段。
我的打法：Bid Ask + 偏上方布局
为什么？因为价格在往上走，我要把更多流动性放在当前价格的上方，让价格拉升时不断穿过我的仓位、不断产生手续费。

具体布局（假设现价 $0.01）：

价格范围$0.010 - $0.013，40%仓位，主吃费区间。

价格范围$0.013 - $0.020，35%仓位，追涨区间，价格继续拉也能吃到。

价格范围$0.005 - $0.010，25%仓位，下方缓冲，万一急跌有接盘。

个人建议：拉升期一定要用窄范围、多段。范围越窄，同样的钱在单位价格区间的密度越高，手续费收得越猛。但这也意味着，价格一旦反转跌破，你会瞬间接一堆 meme 币在手上。所以拉升期我最看重的不是赚多少，是盯紧撤退信号（见最后一条提示🔔）。

⚖️ 状态二：横盘期（价格在一个区间来回震荡）

特征：价格上下反复但不破位、交易量维持中等、狙击盘走了、剩下的是真实交易者在互相买卖，一般这种meme币，大多已经发行了24小时以上，已经经历了PVP最严重的阶段，相对稳定。

这其实是最舒服、性价比最高的阶段。风险比拉升期小，但手续费还在持续进账。

我的打法：Spot 集中 + 窄区间
横盘意味着价格大概率在一个区间内反复，那我就把流动性高度集中在这个箱体区间，让每一次来回震荡都最大化收费。

具体布局（假设在 $0.009 - $0.012 之间震荡）：
价格范围$0.0095 - $0.0115，70%仓位，集中在震荡核心区，密度拉满。

价格范围$0.009 - $0.0095，15%仓位，下沿防守。

价格范围$0.0115 - $0.012，15%仓位，上沿防守。

为什么横盘期用 Spot 集中？因为你已经知道价格大概率不会跑远，那就没必要把流动性摊得太开。集中 = 密度高 = 同样的震荡收更多费。

横盘期我经常能拿住一个仓位好几天，靠反复震荡稳定收费，这才是真正接近"被动收入"的状态。

💀 状态三：崩盘期（叙事结束，价格单边下跌）

特征：5 分钟交易量断崖式萎缩、持有者开始集体撤退、X 上没人再提、价格阶梯式往下。这是新手亏光本金的地方。很多人此时还盯着仪表板上那个虚高的 APR 不肯走。

我的打法：不做 LP，撤。崩盘期做 LP 是纯送死，因为：

交易量没了 → 手续费几乎为零
价格单边跌 → 你的流动性会全部转化成那个正在归零的 meme 币

这时候唯一正确的动作是：把仓位收回来。
如果你还想在崩盘中博一把（我一般不建议新手做），只有一种极端玩法：

Bid Ask + 全部布在下方 + 极宽范围，赌一个死猫跳的超跌反弹。但这是投机，不是 LP 策略，风险极高。

我的原则：叙事一旦结束，第一时间撤本金保命。留得青山在，下个 meme 币还有的打。

🔔 三种状态通用的撤退信号
不管在哪个阶段，我看到这几个信号会立刻警觉：

· 5 分钟交易量连续萎缩（最重要）
· 大户钱包开始净流出
· X 上讨论热度断崖
· 价格跌破我最下方的流动性范围

只要中两个，我就开始减仓；中三个，直接清仓走人。
记住，做 LP 赚的是"钱在流动时的摩擦费"。钱不流了，你待在池子里就只剩风险，没有收益。

📈 管理仓位：APR 是假的，资金流向才是真的

各个LP工具上仪表板显示的 APR 是个历史快照，不代表未来。

我真正盯的指标只有一个：5 分钟交易量还在不在。当一个池子的 5 分钟交易量开始萎缩，手续费就在快速消失。

这时候我有几个选项：

迁移到新的费率层：有时候资金会从 1% 池迁移到 0.3% 池，在迁移发生之前提前布局

直接撤出：如果叙事已经结束，没有新的催化剂，拿着手续费离场

我不看 "APR 还有多高"，我看 "钱还在不在往这个方向流"。

🔍 额外优势：研究其他优秀 LP 的仓位

这个说出来很多人没想到，但这是我盈利的重要来源之一。

我用 @lpagent_io 追踪优秀 LP 交易者的钱包。如👇图四。比如我早期找到了一些优秀钱包，我没有直接复制他的仓位，而是研究他的逻辑：

· 他在什么时间点进场？
· 他的范围是怎么设定的？
· 他什么时候会撤出？

您复制别人的仓位，最好的结果是跟他一样。但如果您理解了他的思维框架，你能做得比他更好，因为您能提前进、更精准退。

💰 资金管理：我为什么能活到现在

这部分超过 70% 决定你能不能赚钱，但大多数人完全忽视。

我的规则：

① 单个池子单次不超过总资金的 20%
再好看的机会，也不值得全押。meme 币能在 10 分钟涨 5 倍，也能在 10 分钟归零。

② 有了手续费收入就部分撤本
一旦手续费收回初始仓位的 30%-50%，我会撤出一部分本金。用"赚来的钱"继续玩，心态完全不同。

③ 看清楚自己在赌什么
做 LP 你赌的是：这个币在你持仓期间不会跌太多，且有足够交易量。不是赌它会涨，是赌它有摩擦成本可以收割。

🚀 总结：我的真实优势是什么。我没有什么神奇的 Alpha，没有内幕。

我的优势就三个字：快、准、跑。

快：比别人早发现有意义的交易量
准：用多段范围让资金在对的价格区间工作
跑：在资金流消失之前离场，不贪最后一口

今天简单看了一下，过去一个月，总共完成了 1281 笔交易，82.2% 胜率，都是不断实战中累积出来的。市场从来没有神话，只有努力勤奋的钻研。🧐

text:
I spent much of the weekend talking with the team who did this work. Seb--and everyone else--acted with integrity and generosity throughout.

Initially we believed the other team had also solved the problem. We wanted to collaborate and do a joint release. 

When we learned that they had Euler but not Navier-Stokes, we offered to let them go first, to suggest that they should be the ones to get the prize, and optionally for Tristan to be the lead author on a rewrite of the OpenAI proof. We felt it was challenging to offer the same to Levent (an Anthropic employee), who was not willing to talk or coordinate with us anyway. We were open to other solutions.

We would have greatly preferred coordination. We did not rush to publish even though the other team wasn't communicating with us. The team threatened us with unfounded accusations of plagarism.

Now that we can see their work, the approaches appear to be different. It is also worth noting that our latest model can solve many, many other math problems.

It is true that we tried this because there were rumors on the internet last week that Anthropic's models had solved a millennium problem and we were curious if ours could do it too.
author: sama
quoted_text:
I would like to clarify a few things:

1) The screenshot is my reaching out to Levent to coordinate our releases. I hope it’s clear from the message that we came in with the best possible intentions.

2) I never ever asked for Levent to be removed from authorship of his own work (as indicated by my text). I was surprised to learn during the call with Tristan that they had only solved Euler and not Navier-Stokes; after learning this we brainstormed possible paths forward. One option we discussed was that Tristan could be the lead author on a rewrite of OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof. It is in that context that I said “it would be simpler if Levent was not an Anthropic employee” because I felt it would be inappropriate for an Anthropic employee to author OpenAI’s work. Importantly it was admitted that internal Anthropic models had been used in their proof of Euler blowup; I therefore felt I could not consider Levent to be an independent academic. Another option I wanted to propose (but got cut short) is to offer access to our internal model so that they could try to finish their proof and bridge the gap between Euler and NS. Again I did not know how to navigate giving access to internal OpenAI IP to an Anthropic employee.

3) To reiterate it plainly: as my text clearly indicates, and as I said during our call, OpenAI's intention was to do everything possible to celebrate their mathematical achievements and the heroic efforts that they made on Euler. In the call I was immediately met with a litany of slander, including direct threats that if we were to announce Navier-Stokes he would immediately go to the press with a barrage of unfounded accusations. I refuted all these accusations but he replied “there is nothing you can do, I simply do not trust you”. I was confused why one would turn an incredible source for celebration (of their achievements!) into such bickering, which is when I said that I did not understand why one would risk their career [over unfounded accusations]. Genuinely, at that moment, I was trying to care for him and do a last ditch attempt to get a chance to give them all the credits that they deserve. I deeply apologize for this extremely poor choice of words, it is the opposite of what I was trying to convey. (I should say that I retracted them on the spot by the way.)
 
4) Overall, on a personal level, it was incredibly difficult to have these conversations. Levent refused to attend any of the meetings despite my repeated asking. As Sholto Douglas said, there will need to be coordination between Anthropic and OpenAI in the future; I felt I was doing a proxy negotiation with Anthropic while the Anthropic employee refused to directly participate.

quoted_text:
Zcash’s latest rally is a narrative bid. A big market cap does not mean a coin earned its place. Sitting near Solana and Hyperliquid on a ranking list does not mean Zcash does what those two do.

The launch was not fair. For the first four years, 20 percent of every block reward was taken as the Founders’ Reward. That money went to founders, staff, advisors, and early investors. It added up to 2.1 million ZEC, or 10 percent of the 21 million cap. Bitcoin paid miners. Zcash also paid a company and its backers. When that first cut was supposed to stop, a similar 20 percent cut came back as a “development fund”. A coin that writes itself into the block reward should not be sold as clean, neutral money.

The cut did not buy a real economy. Privacy was the sales pitch. Using it was optional. Open addresses stayed the easy path for exchanges and simple wallets. For most of Zcash’s life, most coins sat in the open. Optional privacy is marketing. Default privacy is the protocol. Management stayed a board fight: Electric Coin Company, the Foundation, Bootstrap, the brand name, the wallet, and who gets the cut. In January 2026 the whole ECC team left and said they were pushed out. That is not a side issue. That is how the project runs. A base-layer team that cannot stay in the same building as its nonprofit board is not “decentralized.” It is broken at the top.

Then came the security mess the market is already trying to skip. In May 2026 a serious bug in the Orchard pool was made public. It had been there about four years. In theory it could create fake ZEC with no clear on-chain trail. Because the pool is private, nobody can prove fake coins were never made. Ironwood in July closed the old pool and forced coins through a gate. That is cleanup, not a reason for a top-ten price. A money whose private supply cannot be checked like Bitcoin, and that needed an emergency fix after a four-year bug, is not “hard money.”

The point is plain. An unfair launch, a team cut without a matching product, years of board drama, and a four-year hole in the private pool are not the record of a top-ten network. They are the record of a story coin. Solana and Hyperliquid can be disliked for their own reasons. They still clear real use. Zcash cleared a listing and a squeeze. Those are not the same thing. Mixing them up is like sending 701.4 of the wrong asset, or treating EST and EDT as the same hour.

text:
OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking investment-grade ratings ahead of their planned IPOs, with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs reportedly in direct talks with S&P, Moody's, and Fitch on both companies' behalf. Investment-grade status would open access to the roughly $11.7T corporate bond market, letting pension funds and insurers, who are typically restricted from buying speculative-grade debt, participate in financing from day one.

The stakes go beyond cheaper borrowing. Nvidia currently guarantees up to $105B in lease obligations for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, an obligation tied to OpenAI securing "a satisfactory credit rating." Oracle is separately looking to refinance debt tied to a $300B OpenAI infrastructure buildout, while Google and Broadcom have extended tens of billions in support for Anthropic. An investment-grade rating would let both labs shift that exposure off their Big Tech partners' balance sheets and onto public bond markets directly.

The hurdle is real, though. OpenAI posted a $20.9B operating loss on $13.1B revenue in 2025, and Anthropic doesn't expect to break even until 2028, OpenAI not until 2030. Rating analysts are reportedly still treating both as speculative-grade borrowers. Worth watching the SpaceX precedent here too: SpaceX secured investment-grade ratings quickly after its June IPO, and its bonds still traded down toward junk-level pricing within days. A rating agency's stamp doesn't necessarily settle how the market actually prices the risk.

text:
This story underscores that privacy remains one of the core unsolved problems in AI.

We feel intuitively that AIs are our closest confidantes. We routinely share our secrets, vulnerabilities, and most valuable work with our AIs. AIs have become an extension of our conversations with ourselves; like the innermost chambers of our minds.

But legally, that's not how it works. 

According to the law, you have sent your data to a third party, and according to the third party doctrine, you have lost your right to 4th amendment protections. Your data can be looked at, pored over, it can be retrieved without a search warrant, it must be handed over in legal discovery, and so on. It is no longer yours. Legally, you have willingly given it away.

We need to fix this. We need to pass strong privacy laws around AI usage, and harmonize them with stuff like email (which the Supreme Court has only recently definitively established is legally protected).

This is a big part of the reason why we invested into @AskVenice, which is fully private by default, even for consumers. They take an Apple-like ideological stance that AI usage should be private and belong solely to the user. I believe all of American society is going to move in this direction. If not now, then soon.

text:
Running AI agents inside our own operations changed how I think about red teaming them.

A single bad answer is rarely the worst outcome. The real risk appears when the answer can become a tool call, survive in memory, reach another integration, and leave through a channel the system already trusts.

That is why I test the whole path around the model—not only the prompt. I want to know what the agent can read, remember, call, modify, and send after untrusted content enters the system.

That operating experience is now part of how Zealynx scopes AI red-team audits.

https://t.co/QVDVUkeNDX
author: TheBlockChainer
quoted_text:
An AI agent can pass a prompt-injection benchmark and still fail as a system.

The dangerous path is usually a chain:

untrusted document → instruction override → privileged tool call → data sent through an approved channel

That is why our AI red-team audits test the application around the model: prompts, retrieval sources, tool definitions, persistent state, permissions, and multi-step execution.

The deliverable is not a list of clever jailbreaks. It is a reproducible attack chain engineering can fix, followed by fix verification.

https://t.co/guiplZiAyD

text:
The r’s in strawberry thing was always a red herring. The reason LLMs struggle with it is because they don’t read letters, they read numerical token ids. So if they see ‘straw’ ‘ber’ ‘ry’  they just see [token ID 401] [token ID 3547] [token ID 76]

Honestly the fact that they *can* answer it without explicit tools is incredible. It means they inferred enough from the pretraining to directly embed in the weights how individual tokens are spelled probably from stuff like alphabetical lists. 

The best analogy is imagine you live in a world where letters all have different color patterns, but you’re color blind. But you’ve read so much that you’ve absorbed context from people just talking about what color letters are to know them all

cultural command is one of the few positions left that AI can't commoditize.

text: Something I’ve been watching with Eden on Celestia is starting to make more sense alongside Celestia’s zkEVM work. Eden is already a standalone EVM using Celestia mainnet for DA, while Celestia is developing SP1 programs that can prove the EVM state of chains whose transaction data is posted to Celestia. The stated goal of celestia-zkevm is a ZK bridge between Celestia’s base layer and Celestia rollups, with a future forwarding module designed to enable transfers between rollups. Eden’s bridge today still uses Hyperlane, so this isn’t production infrastructure yet. But the architecture is the interesting part: independent execution environments can post their data to Celestia, have their state proven from that data, and eventually communicate through proofs rather than treating every sovereign chain as an isolated island. $TIA  https://t.co/ZMgX1xCP1Q

text:
What is Predictive Allocation?

@aeroxyz's upcoming primitive takes the truth discovery of prediction markets and applies it to spot markets for the first time, and it's nothing like Hyperliquid.

"On Aerodrome, when you stake your $AERO you get to allocate capital each week to markets."

"You allocate AERO rewards to liquidity providers in those markets."

"With predictive allocation, if you believe that there is a market in which there's going to be a lot of activity, you're gonna allocate capital to that market, basically betting on that activity."

"That could be like you're betting on a Sunday headline. You could be betting on an earnings report, and you're betting on getting paid on the volatility in that market."

"The big shift here is you're not necessarily needing to bet on the direction of that market, and you're not needing to be exposed necessarily to either side of that market."

"You are just betting on there's gonna be demand for that market."

"If you are right, you get the same sort of asymmetric upside you would betting on an outcome in a prediction market."

@wagmiAlexander, CEO of @DromosLabs on the live show today.

text: The new desk essential on AI-native teams isn't a bigger monitor — it's a microphone. Once he explains why, it seems completely obvious.
author: CorbinOfficial_
quoted_text:
Saw an indie dev’s new vibe coding setup — no keyboard, just a mic, headphones, and a foot pedal.
Turns out the most AI-savvy people on my team all have one new desk essential: a microphone.
Lots of folks here switched to “voice-first workstations”, so I tried it too.
It’s not just faster than typing. The best part? AI gets you even when you’re rambling, unpolished thoughts and all.
Now I just talk through half-baked ideas straight to AI, stream of consciousness.
Typing makes you edit out the messy thinking, only leaving “final” conclusions.
Talking lets your whole thought process unfold naturally.
That meandering, “pointless” chit-chat? That’s the richest context for AI.
I’ve been using @ComuAI_ to record chats and meetings. Beyond auto-recaps and action items, it catches details I missed in the moment — super useful.
Old way: Think it all through first, then ask AI.
New way: Think out loud. With smart audio, AI is always listening, always helping.
Voice might just be AI’s native interface.

text:
MetaDAO is rethinking capital formation for startups.

Most launchpads help projects raise money and then step away. MetaDAO uses token markets to govern some of the capital decisions that come next.

Capital raised through the platform enters a DAO treasury with spending limits. When a project seeks more funding or wants to change how its treasury is used, it can submit a proposal to a decision market. Traders estimate what the token would be worth if the proposal passes or fails, and the difference between those prices determines the outcome.

Four approved proposals have raised another $13.34M for MetaDAO itself since launch. Two passed only after earlier versions failed and the terms changed. The same process has returned remaining capital to investors when projects were wound down.

This model depends on active tokenholders. One restructuring passed with only seven wallets and less than $700 in volume. Across 12 launches, a median 52% of allocated wallets sold some tokens within seven days. It remains unclear whether launch recipients will become long-term owners.

The opportunity is larger than a better token launchpad. If tokenization becomes a meaningful way to fund operating businesses, MetaDAO could develop into a founder platform for a new generation of companies raising capital online.

Five numbers tell you whether an AI business is a real business.

Gross retention.@WeAreLegora is 95%. Customers who bought last year are still here this year. If this one is broken, nothing downstream matters.

NRR. Ours is 300%+. Gross retention is the floor. NRR is how much taller customers build on top of it. We don't sell shelf-ware. 

DAU/MAU. Ours is north of 50%, and the average active user spends 17 hours a month in the product. A rollout tells you a firm has signed. This indicates the work actually matters, and it moves here before it appears in retention or NRR.

Win-rates. Our August pilot closed-won-win rate was 78%. Winning roughly 4 out of 5 competitive pilots is downstream from offering a superior product.

Gross margin. The one that matters most. Ours is positive and improving every quarter. Our customers want Legora to be a long-term partner, and this is what makes that possible.

text:
Notional V1 Exploit Post-Mortem

On September 3, 2026, Notional V1 was exploited on Ethereum for roughly 1.65M USDC and 69K DAI. The Notional Team paused the affected contract shortly afterward to protect remaining user funds.

Notional V1 was publicly deprecated in January 2022 following the launch of Notional V2, but withdrawals remained available indefinitely for users who kept assets in the protocol. The exploited funds were residual assets that remained in the legacy V1 Escrow contract.

No exploited funds have been recovered, but the team is engaging with US law enforcement and a leading crypto incident response firm to pursue any possible recovery. No other funds in any Notional product are at risk.

The exploit

The attacker caused an integer overflow error related to the mintfCashPair function. This error enabled him to create a large debt in one account, bypass the collateral check on that account, and then transfer an unbacked collateral position to a second account.

Following this setup, the attacker borrowed against that unbacked collateral position from the second account and drained the Notional V1 Escrow.

Exploited contract: 0x9abd0b8868546105F6F48298eaDC1D9c82f7f683

Exploit transaction: 0xc3f3e318f7ab2d0daaba59e6ec901d25d1fe8a89aafe2b2b62e3b9aee1a24efa

Find a deep-dive on the details of the exploit on the Quill Audits blog.

The response

Immediately following the exploit, the Notional Team investigated the transaction, confirmed that it was likely an exploit, and moved to pause the contract to protect remaining funds. Shortly after this initial investigation, the team upgraded the Notional V1 contract and paused all operations.

Pause transaction: 0x012fc554b165b3b3ccf3121018ae26503cab50031fa84adea29253b1cd5831d9

The Notional Team alerted security partners shortly thereafter and has since engaged with US law enforcement and Zero Shadow, a crypto incident response firm, to pursue all possible avenues toward recovery.

These recovery efforts are ongoing and the Notional Team will make an additional announcement in the event of any asset recovery or distribution.

Legacy contract management

This exploit highlights a shortcoming in Notional’s policy of legacy contract management. Although Notional V1 had been deprecated for nearly five years, substantial user assets remained. Given the pace of evolution in smart contract security, legacy contracts must be handled with the same ongoing scrutiny as production contracts. Smart contract security is a moving target, not a static one.

Going forward, any Notional smart contract deprecation plan will include a mechanism to migrate or return all user assets to ensure that no funds are left idle indefinitely in legacy contracts.

Thank you for your patience as we work to resolve this incident.

In a difficult and dangerous world, a decade on from Brexit, there is a risk that Britain loses the confidence to lead and stand up for its values. 

I’m not prepared to let that happen. It is more important than ever that Britain stands for something.

We have called for years for a two-state solution in the Middle East, but we must recognise that those words are meaningless unless we back them up with action.

For too long, we have been hesitant to act, fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel. 

Today we are announcing carefully judged, targeted steps that are not aimed at the Israeli people, but at the unacceptable policies of the current Israeli government.

The suffering of the Palestinian people is a scar on the conscience of the world. Innocent Palestinians, including children, continue to be killed in Gaza. And there is still a humanitarian crisis, with far too little aid getting in.

The scale of destruction is hard to comprehend. More than 70,000 people lie dead - at least 20,000 of them children. Families and communities have been torn apart. Millions displaced. And the population of Gaza is now penned into just one third of the territory.

I know that people across the UK feel very deeply about this issue - and so do I.

Before I became Prime Minister, I said our country’s response had been too slow and simply not good enough. That’s why I committed to changing the government’s approach.

I will not stand by as the horrific suffering continues to grow and the prospect of a two-state solution - the best hope for peace and stability in the region - comes under attack.

More settlements have been approved under the four years of this Israeli government than in the previous 20 years. The UN has reported more than 1,500 incidents of settler violence so far this year, aimed at driving out Palestinians. And the situation is growing worse, fast.

The Israeli government has now approved 104 new settlements since it took office in December 2022, and ahead of the October elections in Israel, it is allowing tenders for the construction of the E1 mega settlement to go ahead. This would cut a swathe through the heart of the West Bank - snuffing out the hope of realising a two-state solution. It cannot be allowed to happen.

That’s why we are announcing a new package of tough measures to put pressure on the Israeli government: 

First, we will ban the trade in goods with illegal settlements in Palestine.

Second, we have formally changed the view of the British government to say for the first time that the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory is unlawful - independent of, but in line with, the conclusion of the international court of justice.

And third, we will sanction individuals and companies that support, facilitate or profit from illegal settlements. That includes any businesses or investors that take part in the construction of the E1 settlement.

In addition, we are announcing a new package of desperately needed humanitarian aid to Gaza.

We are taking these steps because it is the right thing to do.

I have condemned the monstrous terrorist attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in the strongest possible terms - and continue to condemn Hamas. However, it does not justify the Israeli government’s actions in Gaza or the West Bank.

The measures we are taking are about targeting illegal settlements and increasing the pressure on the Israeli government to change course. We are not imposing sanctions on Israel as a whole, which would punish the Israeli people, many of whom disagree with their government’s position.

The Israeli people are not responsible for the actions of their government. And nor is the Jewish community in the UK. Blaming British Jews for the actions of Benjamin Netanyahu’s government is wrong, plain and simple. And it is antisemitism, plain and simple.

I met the representatives of the Jewish community just last week. I know the fear they live with day by day. My government will stop at nothing to ensure they are safe and to stamp out antisemitism in every part of our society.

The measures we are announcing today are about protecting the only solution that could see the Israeli and Palestinian people living side by side in peace and security - something that people up and down the UK desperately want to see. 

The government I lead will keep working with our partners around the world to keep that hope alive.

text:
Everyone keeps telling me altcoins are outperforming, and they always have ten examples ready.

Here is the test I use. Pick two dates when Bitcoin was at the same price, then look up the altcoin on both of them.

I ran it this afternoon. Bitcoin was 78,318 on August 22. It is 78,440 today. Seventeen days apart, and Bitcoin has gone nowhere.

Here is where the biggest coins sat on those same two dates.

Ethereum: down 1%
XRP: down 2%
Dogecoin: down 2%
Tron: down 1%
Cardano: down 3%
Avalanche: up 2%

Six of the nine largest altcoins are within a few percent of exactly where they were the last time Bitcoin was at this price. They went up harder when Bitcoin went up, and they gave it back when Bitcoin stalled. A coin that only moves louder than Bitcoin is still following Bitcoin.

Now the honest part, because there were real exceptions.

Solana: up 10%
BNB: up 9%
Chainlink: up 5%

Those are genuine. If you were in them before anyone was talking about them, well done, that was a good trade.

But that is the bit that gets skipped when someone shows me their ten examples. Those trades needed you to already know the narrative, not to hear about it. By the time it reaches me, and then reaches you through me, the move has been made.

So here is where I actually am. I am sitting in Bitcoin and waiting.

Not because altcoins are finished, I do not think that at all. It is because "altcoins are outperforming" turned out to mean two or three of them did, and I would rather hold the thing I know my level on than chase the ones I was too slow for.

text:
Tasklet’s multi-model harness is incredible for building rich, complex apps — especially games!

In the 90’s there was a game by Ambrosia Software called Escape Velocity that I was obsessed with. So I decided to recreate something similar with Tasklet.

In the game, you can fly around the galaxy warping from place to place. You can land on planets, fight pirates, take on secret missions, trade commodities and so much more. It’s a rich immersive world.

To build this in Tasklet, I used:
- Astra for most of the coding
- Fable 5.1 for most of the creative work — storylines, missions, characters, etc.
- OpenAI image models for the sprites, planets, avatars, etc.
- Gemini omni for video generation for cutscenes.
- GLM 5.3 to actually power the interactions on the game (for lower cost)

Tasklet’s instant apps feature made it effortless to actually build & serve the app, and Tasklet’s browser use allowed the agent to visually inspect it’s work to make sure everything looked right. For example, it spent a long time reviewing the landing sequence animations to make sure they were fun.

text:
I have no options left.

This fundraiser was supposed to help us. That is what it was created for. It was supposed to give us a chance to get back on our feet, repair our car, get the basic furniture we need, and slowly rebuild a stable life for my children and me.

But today, we can’t wait anymore.

Tomorrow, I may have to sell our car instead of repairing it, simply to try to pay our rent and avoid ending up on the streets with my children.

And after the car, I may have to sell the little that I still own.

I won’t be able to buy another car. The furniture will have to wait. Our plans will have to wait. Everything we hoped to rebuild will have to be postponed once again.

Little by little, we will try to pay our debts. We will cut back on everything we can. We will even have to reduce what we spend on food.

Very few people have believed in us so far.

And maybe that is because we are just ordinary people. We are not famous. We are not important. We are simply a family trying desperately to stay standing and protect what little stability we have left.

But this fundraiser was meant to help us through exactly this kind of situation.

I don't know what else to do.

If you can donate, even a small amount could help us hold on a little longer. If you can't donate, please share our fundraiser. Your share could reach someone who can.

We are not asking for a perfect life.

We are asking for a chance.

A chance to keep our home. A chance to repair what can still be repaired. A chance to rebuild instead of constantly losing more.

Please don't let our story disappear simply because we are ordinary people.

We need help now.
